purpose: New 9NNN rule rows discovered by the step-2 fee gap pass (source: fee_gap/raw/<ST>.json), banked for the rules library. Rules referenced ONLY by the excluded payment.method item are listed under excluded, not banked.

excluded.reason: payment.method excluded per owner decision 2026-08-20 — card/payment-instrument acceptance is finance-department policy, applies city-wide, not open-records-specific.

AL.legal_concept: Copy on payment of a reasonable fee (§ 36-12-41 as amended 2024)
AL.atomic_rule: Every public officer having custody of a public record a resident may inspect shall provide, on proper request, a copy of the record on payment of a reasonable fee, as further provided in Article 3.
AL.trigger: Proper request for a copy of an inspectable public record
AL.source_language: Every public officer having custody of a public record that a resident has a right to inspect shall provide him or her, on proper request as provided in this article, with a copy of the public record, on payment of a reasonable fee, as further provided in this article.
AL.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
AL.notes: Amends AL-0039's description: the 2024 rewrite replaced 'certified copy ... on payment of the legal fees therefor' with 'a copy ... on payment of a reasonable fee'; certification is no longer mentioned in Article 3. Mapped to fee.actual_cost_basis as the closest canonical soft-standard key although the Alabama term is 'reasonable fee', not 'actual cost'. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

AL.legal_concept: Default request-form notice: extensive requests may increase fees for the administrative cost of searching and copying
AL.atomic_rule: Absent written procedures to the contrary, the standard request form shall read substantially as prescribed, including the notice that extensive requests may increase the fees to cover the administrative cost of searching and copying the requested records and that payment of fees may be required before the request is fulfilled.
AL.trigger: Public officer has not adopted written procedures to the contrary; request form in use
AL.source_language: Records requested: (Be as specific as possible. A public officer is not obligated to respond to a request that is vague, ambiguous, overly broad, or unreasonable in scope, nor is a public officer obligated to respond to a request that seeks records that do not exist or materials that are not public records. Additionally, extensive requests for public records may increase the fees to cover the administrative cost of searching and copying the requested records.) [...] Payment of fees may be required before your request is fulfilled.
AL.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
AL.notes: Form text, not a fee rule; it is the only statutory acknowledgement that search/copying labor cost is a component of the reasonable fee. Officer 'may require additional information or modify the order or format'. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

AL.legal_concept: Pre-search deposit bounded at the whole estimated fee
AL.atomic_rule: The public officer may require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records — i.e., a pre-search deposit of up to 100% of the estimate.
AL.trigger: Officer elects to require prepayment before searching (standard or time-intensive request)
AL.source_language: Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records.
AL.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
AL.notes: Ceiling: 100% of the estimated fee (unit judgment from 'all or a portion of the estimated fee'). No statutory percentage or dollar threshold; the city sets the operative deposit share. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

AL.legal_concept: Reasonable fee for redaction/editing of law-enforcement recordings
AL.atomic_rule: A custodial law enforcement agency may charge a reasonable fee for redaction and editing of a body-worn/dashboard-camera recording requested for disclosure.
AL.trigger: Written request for disclosure of a law-enforcement recording under §§ 36-21-210 to -213
AL.source_language: A custodial law enforcement agency may charge a reasonable fee for redaction and editing of a recording.
AL.notes: Applies to any 'custodial law enforcement agency' (§ 36-21-210(2)), including municipal police. The article governs 'disclosure' (viewing/listening), not 'release' (copies).

AL.legal_concept: State executive-branch agency retrieval/preparation cap and redaction no-charge (EO 734)
AL.atomic_rule: A state executive-branch agency may charge up to $20.00 per hour, including a standard minimum fee of $20.00, for time spent locating, retrieving and preparing records, and may not charge for legal review or redaction.
AL.trigger: Public-records request to a state executive-branch agency
AL.source_language: Document retrieval and preparation. The agency may charge the requester up to $20.00 per hour, including a standard, minimum fee of $20.00, for time spent locating, retrieving, and preparing records for production. The agency may not charge for legal review or redaction necessary to withhold legally protected information.
AL.effective_status: Current per the State's public-records portal (publicrecordsrequest.alabama.gov) as of 2026-08-19; requires manual verification whether amended after Act 2024-278
AL.notes: STATE EXECUTIVE-BRANCH AGENCIES ONLY (§7: 'any agency, department, board, office, commission, or other entity within the executive branch of state government'); does not bind municipalities. Source type: Governor's executive order (recorded as Official Guidance for schema fit).

AL.atomic_rule: A state executive-branch agency may charge a per-page fee of up to $0.50 for copies on standard 8.5x11 paper and may not charge a per-page fee for documents provided electronically.
AL.trigger: Public-records request to a state executive-branch agency
AL.source_language: Per-page fees. The agency may charge a per-page fee of up to $.50 for copies produced on standard 8.5x11 paper. The agency may not charge a per-page fee for documents provided electronically.
AL.effective_status: Current per the State's public-records portal as of 2026-08-19; requires manual verification whether amended after Act 2024-278
AL.notes: STATE EXECUTIVE-BRANCH AGENCIES ONLY; does not bind municipalities.

AL.legal_concept: State executive-branch agency actual-cost pass-through with advance notice (EO 734)
AL.atomic_rule: A state executive-branch agency may charge actual costs incurred in processing a request (e.g., flash drive/hardware, special paper sizes, electronic-database search costs) if the requester is informed of the cost in advance.
AL.trigger: Actual cost item incurred; requester informed in advance
AL.source_language: Actual costs. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the agency may charge any actual costs incurred while processing or responding to a public-records request—for example, for a flash drive or other hardware necessary for electronically producing records, for special paper sizes, and for costs associated with searching electronic databases—if the requester is informed of the cost in advance of being charged.
AL.effective_status: Current per the State's public-records portal as of 2026-08-19; requires manual verification whether amended after Act 2024-278
AL.notes: STATE EXECUTIVE-BRANCH AGENCIES ONLY; does not bind municipalities.

AL.legal_concept: Officer may process a request less expensively (no bar to charging less)
AL.atomic_rule: Nothing in Article 3 prohibits a public officer from processing a public records request in a manner that is less expensive or more prompt from the requester's perspective.
AL.source_language: Nothing in this article shall be construed to prohibit a public officer from processing a public records request in a manner that is less expensive or more prompt from the perspective of the requester.
AL.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
AL.notes: Supports discretionary fee reduction/waiver and free-allowance policies; does not state grounds. Interaction with the mandatory time-intensive fee (§ 36-12-44(b)(2)) unresolved — human legal review. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

AZ.legal_concept: Onetime fee per copy for local law-enforcement video recordings — ceiling $46 per video-hour reviewed
AZ.atomic_rule: A county, city, town or political subdivision may establish a onetime fee per copy, not to exceed $46 per video-hour reviewed, charged to a person who submits a public records request to a local law enforcement agency for a copy of a video recording; in setting the amount it may consider the reasonable cost of reviewing, transmitting, copying and (as necessary) redacting the video recording and any other relevant information.
AZ.trigger: Public records request to a local law-enforcement agency for a copy of a video recording; requester is not a § 39-127 crime victim/representative.
AZ.source_language: Except as provided in section 39-127, a county, a city, a town or any political subdivision of this state may establish a onetime fee per copy, not to exceed $46 per video-hour reviewed, that is charged to a person who submits a public records request to a local law enforcement agency for a copy of a video recording. A county, a city, a town or any political subdivision of this state may take into consideration the following information when determining the amount of the onetime fee per copy: 1. The reasonable cost of reviewing, transmitting, making a copy of and, as necessary, redacting the video recording. 2. Any other relevant information.
AZ.source_authority: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 39-129 (added by Laws 2023, ch. 190, SB 1148)
AZ.effective_status: Effective October 30, 2023 (added by Laws 2023, ch. 190, SB 1148, approved June 20, 2023; general effective date of the 56th Leg., 1st Reg. Sess.) — codified text opened 2026-08-19; no later amendment found
AZ.notes: Authority scope is Local-Government General (counties, cities, towns, political subdivisions) — does not bind state agencies. Ceiling: $46 per video-hour reviewed, structured as a onetime fee per copy. Related: § 39-127 free-copy exception (AZ-9009 amending AZ-0021).

AZ.legal_concept: Non-commercial fee limited to copying and postage; no charge for searching for or retrieving records (Hanania rule)
AZ.atomic_rule: For a non-commercial request a public body may charge only (1) postage to mail copies and (2) the cost of copying records it furnishes; it may not charge for searching for or retrieving the record.
AZ.trigger: Request is not for a commercial purpose (§ 39-121.03).
AZ.source_language: This plain language indicates that a public body may charge a fee for responding to a public records request for a noncommercial purpose for (1) postage charges to mail copies of public records to the requesting party or (2) copying public records and furnishing them to the requesting party if the proper facilities are available. In Hanania v. City of Tucson, 128 Ariz. 135, 136, 624 P.2d 332, 333 (App. 1981), the court determined that the public records law allowed a public body to charge a fee for copying a public record, but not for searching for or retrieving the record. Arizona's public records law allows a public body to impose copying fees in response to public records requests for noncommercial purposes. Under that law, a public body can impose copying fees to offset copying costs only when a requesting party asks the public body to furnish copies of records. A public body should not impose copying fees on a party making a public records request when the requesting party asks only to inspect records or uses a personal device to make his or her own copies.
AZ.source_authority: Ariz. Att'y Gen. Op. I13-012 (R13-018), Dec. 2, 2013 (restating Hanania v. City of Tucson, 128 Ariz. 135 (App. 1980) and Ariz. Att'y Gen. Op. I86-090)
AZ.effective_status: Current (opinion 2013; underlying § 39-121.01(D)(1) fee sentence unchanged through Laws 2025, ch. 102)
AZ.notes: Formal AG opinion (opened, verbatim). Applies to all public bodies. AG Op. I86-090 itself could not be opened on azag.gov (404) — cited only as restated here and in the AG Agency Handbook § 6.5.5. Commercial requests are governed instead by § 39-121.03(A) (AZ-0019).

AZ.legal_concept: No copying fee for inspection-only requests or personal-device copies
AZ.atomic_rule: A public body may not charge a copying fee when the requester asks only to inspect records (even if the body must print or copy internally, e.g., to redact) or when the requester makes copies with a personal device.
AZ.trigger: Requester asks to inspect only, or copies with own device (non-disruptive).
AZ.source_language: A public body in Arizona therefore cannot charge copying fees to recoup the cost of copies made internally to allow a member of the public to inspect the records. ... For these reasons, a public body cannot charge a copying fee when a member of the public inspects a record and makes a copy of the record using his or her own personal device.
AZ.source_authority: Ariz. Att'y Gen. Op. I13-012 (R13-018), Dec. 2, 2013
AZ.notes: Two sentences joined with an ellipsis from Parts A and B of the opinion's analysis; each sentence is verbatim. Opinion footnote 3: does not require permitting a personal device that would disrupt business or damage records.

AZ.legal_concept: Permissible non-commercial copying fee: amount the agency deems appropriate for copying, including a reasonable amount for time, equipment and personnel used in producing copies — not search costs
AZ.atomic_rule: An agency may charge a fee it deems appropriate for copying records, including a reasonable amount for the cost of time, equipment and personnel used in producing copies, but not for costs of searching for the records.
AZ.source_language: An agency may charge a fee it deems appropriate for copying records, including a reasonable amount for the cost of time, equipment, and personnel used in producing copies of records, but not for costs of searching for the records. A.R.S. § 39-121.01(D)(1); Hanania v. City of Tucson, 128 Ariz. 135, 136, 624 P.2d 332, 333 (App. 1980); Ariz. Att'y Gen. Op. I86-090. When the requester only wants to inspect the record, the agency may not charge a copying fee incurred, for example, to make redactions before public inspection. Ariz. Att'y Gen. Op. I13-012.
AZ.source_authority: Arizona Attorney General, Agency Handbook, ch. 6 (Public Records) § 6.5.5 (rev. 2018; corrected copy posted azag.gov May 2025)
AZ.effective_status: Current (rev. 2018 handbook; posted 2025-05; reproduced in Ombudsman 2025 booklet)
AZ.notes: Guidance, not law: it glosses § 39-121.01(D)(1) via Hanania and AG Op. I86-090. Written for state agencies but states the § 39-121.01 rule that applies to all public bodies. Note tension with the Ombudsman FAQ (AZ-9005), which lists 'labor' among non-chargeable items; the handbook admits copy-production personnel time. Constraint basis soft-standard: no number.

AZ.legal_concept: Ombudsman guidance: no charge for inspection, labor, redaction, overhead, or review to determine disclosability
AZ.atomic_rule: The public body cannot charge for the cost of searching, for inspection of the record, labor, redaction, overhead costs, or any fee to examine or review a record to determine whether it is disclosable.
AZ.source_language: The public body may not charge for the cost of searching the records. Hanania v. City of Tucson, 128 Ariz. 135, 624 P.2d 332 (Ct. App. 1980); Ariz. Att'y Gen. Op. I13-012. The public body also cannot charge for inspection of the record, labor, redaction, overhead costs, or any fee to examine or review a record to determine whether the record is disclosable.
AZ.source_authority: Arizona Ombudsman-Citizens' Aide, FAQs – Public Records ('Can the public body charge me for copies?')
AZ.notes: Lowest tier of the source hierarchy (records-authority FAQ). Broader than the AG opinion it cites (adds redaction/overhead/review). Human legal review before treating the redaction/overhead bar as binding; § 39-129 expressly lets local LE video fees consider review/redaction cost within its cap.

AZ.legal_concept: Fee waiver is discretionary; no hardship waiver required
AZ.atomic_rule: A public body is not required to waive a copying fee for financial hardship, but is not required to impose a charge for copies at all.
AZ.trigger: Requester asks for a fee waiver (non-statutory ground).
AZ.source_language: I requested copies of public records and cannot afford the copying fee. Must the public body waive the copying fee if it causes financial hardship? No. The law permits public bodies to impose a copying fee and does not require a waiver for financial hardship. That said, public bodies are not required to impose a charge for copies.
AZ.source_authority: Arizona Ombudsman-Citizens' Aide, FAQs – Public Records
AZ.notes: Guidance only; statute is silent on discretionary waivers. Mandatory no-charge categories are § 39-122 and § 39-127 (AZ-9008, AZ-9009).

AZ.legal_concept: Requester must affirm non-commercial purpose (or undertake to give a commercial-purpose statement) at the time of the request
AZ.atomic_rule: At the time of the request the requesting person shall affirm that the record is not for a commercial purpose or, if it is, that the person will provide the § 39-121.03(A) statement of intended use.
AZ.trigger: Any request to examine or be furnished copies.
AZ.source_language: At the time of the request, the requesting person shall affirm that the public record is not for a commercial purpose or, if the public record is for a commercial purpose, that the requesting person will provide a statement that explains the intended use pursuant to section 39-121.03, subsection A.
AZ.source_authority: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 39-121.01(D)(1), as amended by Laws 2025, ch. 102 (SB 1372, approved May 2, 2025)
AZ.effective_status: Amended effective September 26, 2025 (Laws 2025, ch. 102, SB 1372, approved May 2, 2025; general effective date of the 57th Leg., 1st Reg. Sess.) — codified text opened at azleg.gov 2026-08-19
AZ.notes: Drives the fee-basis fork (non-commercial copying-only fee vs § 39-121.03(A) commercial charge). Included because the engine branches on it; requester need not state a purpose beyond the affirmation.

AZ.legal_concept: No fee for certified copies of, or searches for, public records used in claims/benefits presented to the United States (verbatim replacement for AZ-0020)
AZ.atomic_rule: No state, county or city (or officer or board thereof) shall demand or receive a fee for issuing certified copies of public records or for making search for them when they are to be used in connection with a claim for a pension, allotment, allowance, compensation, insurance or other benefits presented to the United States; the service is rendered on request of a US official, the claimant, or the claimant's guardian or attorney.
AZ.trigger: Records to be used with a claim/benefit presented to the United States; request by US official, claimant, guardian or attorney.
AZ.source_language: A. No state, county or city, or any officer or board thereof shall demand or receive a fee or compensation for issuing certified copies of public records or for making search for them, when they are to be used in connection with a claim for a pension, allotment, allowance, compensation, insurance or other benefits which is to be presented to the United States or a bureau or department thereof. C. The services specified in subsections A and B shall be rendered on request of an official of the United States, a claimant, his guardian or attorney. For each failure or refusal so to do, the officer so failing shall be liable on his official bond.
AZ.notes: AMENDS AZ-0020 (which carried is_paraphrase=true): supplies the verbatim clause. Applies to 'state, county or city' — all public bodies. Search AND certified-copy fees both barred.

AZ.legal_concept: Crime victims: one free copy of police report, audio recordings and video recordings (verbatim replacement for AZ-0021; reflects 2024–2025 amendments)
AZ.atomic_rule: A victim of a Part I crime (or delinquent act), the victim's attorney, or an immediate family member if the victim is killed or incapacitated has the right to receive one copy of the police report, audio recordings and video recordings from the investigating law enforcement agency or charging prosecutorial agency at no charge; DV/sexual-offense victims have the same right regardless of Part I status; law-enforcement agencies shall prioritize processing such requests.
AZ.trigger: Requester qualifies as victim/attorney/immediate family under § 39-127(A)–(C) and requests the police report / recordings of that offense.
AZ.source_language: A. A victim of a criminal offense that is a part I crime under the statewide uniform crime reporting program, the victim's attorney on behalf of the victim or an immediate family member of the victim if the victim is killed or incapacitated has the right to receive one copy of the police report, audio recordings and video recordings from the investigating law enforcement agency or charging prosecutorial agency at no charge and, on request of the victim, the court or the clerk of the court shall provide, at no charge, the minute entry or portion of the record of any proceeding in the case that arises out of the offense committed against the victim and that is reasonably necessary to pursue a claimed victim's right. C. Notwithstanding subsection A or B of this section, if a police report involves a domestic violence offense or a sexual offense, the victim or the victim's attorney on behalf of the victim has the right to receive one copy of the police report, audio recordings and video recordings from the investigating law enforcement agency or charging prosecutorial agency at no charge and, on request of the victim, the court or the clerk of the court shall provide, at no charge, the minute entry or portion of the record of any proceeding in the case that arises out of the offense committed against the victim and that is reasonably necessary to pursue a claimed victim's right. D. A law enforcement agency shall prioritize the processing and providing of each police report that is requested pursuant to this section.
AZ.effective_status: Amended effective September 26, 2025 (Laws 2024, ch. 56, SB 1371; Laws 2025, ch. 37; Laws 2025, ch. 65, SB 1220) — codified text opened 2026-08-19
AZ.notes: AMENDS AZ-0021 (is_paraphrase=true): verbatim clauses; adds 'audio recordings' and 'charging prosecutorial agency' (Laws 2025, ch. 37 and ch. 65) and the (D) prioritization duty. Subsection (B) (delinquent acts) is parallel and omitted here for length. Overrides the § 39-129 video fee for qualifying victims.

CA.legal_concept: No charge for requester's own-equipment copying during on-premises inspection
CA.atomic_rule: A requester inspecting a disclosable record on the agency's premises may photograph or otherwise copy the record with the requester's own equipment without being charged any fees or costs, provided the method does not physically contact the record, damage it, or access the agency's systems; the agency may impose reasonable limits to protect the records or its orderly function.
CA.trigger: Requester inspects on premises and uses own equipment
CA.source_language: A requester who inspects a disclosable record on the premises of the agency has the right to use the requester’s equipment on those premises, without being charged any fees or costs, to photograph or otherwise copy or reproduce the record in a manner that does not require the equipment to make physical contact with the record, unless the means of copy or reproduction would result in either of the following: (1) Damage to the record. (2) Unauthorized access to the agency’s computer systems or secured networks by using software, equipment, or any other technology capable of accessing, altering, or compromising the agency’s electronic records.
CA.effective_status: Current (added Stats. 2021, ch. 614 (AB 473), operative Jan. 1, 2023; no amendment 2024–2026 as of 2026-08-19)
CA.notes: applies_to: all_public_bodies ('the agency' — state or local). Bears on rules.freePages (no per-page allowance, but self-copying is free). Subdivision (c) limits are structural, not a value.

CA.legal_concept: Redaction and search of electronic records not chargeable as 'data extraction'
CA.atomic_rule: An agency may not charge a requester for the cost of redacting exempt material from otherwise disclosable electronic records (including digital video footage), nor for time spent searching for responsive electronic records; such tasks are not 'data compilation, extraction, or programming' under § 7922.575(b) (former § 6253.9(b)(2)).
CA.trigger: Request for electronic records requiring search or redaction
CA.source_language: We hold only that section 6253.9(b)(2), as presently written, does not provide a basis for charging requesters for the costs of redacting government records kept in an electronic format, including digital video footage. … But the term “extraction” does not cover every process that might be colloquially described as “taking information out.” It does not, for example, cover time spent searching for responsive records in an e-mail inbox or a computer’s documents folder. Just as agencies cannot recover the costs of searching through a filing cabinet for paper records, they cannot recover comparable costs for electronic records. Nor, for similar reasons, does “extraction” cover the cost of redacting exempt data from otherwise producible electronic records.
CA.source_authority: National Lawyers Guild, S.F. Bay Area Chapter v. City of Hayward (2020) 9 Cal.5th 488 (Cal. Supreme Court, No. S252445, May 28, 2020)
CA.effective_status: Current (published May 28, 2020; construes former § 6253.9(b)(2), recodified without substantive change as § 7922.575(b) by Stats. 2021, ch. 614)
CA.notes: AMENDS CA-0024: replaces its is_paraphrase=true holding text with the verbatim holding and the searching/redaction passage from the opened official opinion (courts.ca.gov archive PDF, pp. 25 & 28). Also disapproves Fredericks v. Superior Court (2015) 233 Cal.App.4th 209 to the extent inconsistent. applies_to: all_public_bodies.

CA.legal_concept: 'Direct costs of duplication' excludes retrieval, inspection, review and redaction time
CA.atomic_rule: 'Direct costs of duplication' covers the cost of running the copy machine and conceivably the expense of the person operating it, and excludes the ancillary tasks of retrieval, inspection and handling of the file, including staff time searching the records, reviewing them for exempt information, and deleting exempt information.
CA.trigger: Any request for copies of paper records
CA.source_language: The reference to “direct costs of duplication” has long been understood to cover “the ‘cost of running the copy machine, and conceivably also the expense of the person operating it’ while excluding any charge for ‘the ancillary tasks necessarily associated with the retrieval, inspection and handling of the file from which the copy is extracted.’ ” (County of Santa Clara, supra, 170 Cal.App.4th at p. 1336, quoting North County Parents Organization v. Department of Education (1994) 23 Cal.App.4th 144, 148 (North County).) Nonchargeable ancillary costs include “staff time involved in searching the records, reviewing records for information exempt from disclosure under law, and deleting such exempt information.” (North County, at p. 146.)
CA.source_authority: National Lawyers Guild, S.F. Bay Area Chapter v. City of Hayward (2020) 9 Cal.5th 488 (Cal. Supreme Court, No. S252445, May 28, 2020), at 9 Cal.5th pp. 3-4 of slip op., quoting County of Santa Clara v. Superior Court (2009) 170 Cal.App.4th 1301, 1336 and North County Parents Organization v. Department of Education (1994) 23 Cal.App.4th 144, 146, 148
CA.effective_status: Current (statement of settled construction of former § 6257/§ 6253(b), now § 7922.530(a))
CA.notes: Verbatim from the opened NLG opinion; the North County and County of Santa Clara opinions themselves were not opened (official reporter not freely hosted) — the quotation is as reproduced by the Supreme Court. applies_to: all_public_bodies. Resolves labor.search.rate / labor.review.rate as not_applicable.

CA.legal_concept: § 7922.575(b) cost-shift excludes initial gathering, conversion and maintenance costs
CA.atomic_rule: When the § 7922.575(b) cost-shift applies, the fee may include the cost to construct the record and the cost of programming and computer services necessary to produce a copy, but may not include expenses associated with the agency's initial gathering of the information, its initial conversion into an electronic format, or its maintenance.
CA.trigger: Electronic record produced only at scheduled intervals, or request requires data compilation/extraction/programming
CA.source_language: If the request is made at a time other than when the data is periodically produced, the fee may additionally include “the cost to construct [the] record, and the cost of programming and computer services necessary to produce a copy of the record.” (§ 6253.9, subd. (b)(1).) The fee may similarly cover such additional costs when “[t]he request would require data compilation, extraction, or programming to produce the record.” (§ 6253.9, subd. (b)(2).) In either event, however, the fee may not include expenses associated with the county’s initial gathering of the information, or with initial conversion of the information into an electronic format, or with maintaining the information.
CA.source_authority: Cal. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 04-1105 (Oct. 3, 2005) (Lockyer, A.G.; Stone, D.A.G.), Conclusion 3 and Analysis pt. 3 (reported at 88 Ops.Cal.Atty.Gen. 153 — reporter cite to be verified)
CA.notes: Question posed about a county assessor's parcel-map data; the reasoning construes the statute generally ('a state or local agency'). applies_to: all_public_bodies (opinion addressed to counties). Bears on labor.programming.rate, dup.specialty.rate, labor.overheadPct.

CA.legal_concept: Local legislative body may charge a fee or deposit for copies; no disability surcharge
CA.atomic_rule: The Brown Act does not prevent the legislative body of a local agency from charging a fee or deposit for a copy of a public record pursuant to § 7922.530, except that no surcharge may be imposed on persons with disabilities in violation of ADA Title II.
CA.trigger: Local agency charges for a copy of a public record (agenda materials or otherwise)
CA.source_language: This chapter shall not be construed to prevent the legislative body of a local agency from charging a fee or deposit for a copy of a public record pursuant to Section 7922.530, except that a surcharge shall not be imposed on persons with disabilities in violation of Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof.
CA.source_authority: Cal. Gov. Code § 54957.5(d) (Ralph M. Brown Act)
CA.notes: applies_to: municipalities (local agencies; the Brown Act does not govern state agencies). Non-preclusion clause — it presupposes rather than grants deposit authority; no threshold or cap. Basis for rules.deposit.threshold = defers_to_city. The ADA no-surcharge clause is a Prohibition rider (secondary rule type).

CA.legal_concept: Agency may adopt requirements allowing greater access than the CPRA minimums (basis for local fee reduction/waiver policy)
CA.atomic_rule: Except as otherwise prohibited by law, a state or local agency may adopt requirements for itself that allow for faster, more efficient, or greater access to records than the CPRA's minimum standards.
CA.trigger: Agency adopts its own records policy (including charging less than direct cost or waiving fees)
CA.source_language: Except as otherwise prohibited by law, a state or local agency may adopt requirements for itself that allow for faster, more efficient, or greater access to records than prescribed by the minimum standards set forth in this division.
CA.effective_status: Current (added Stats. 2021, ch. 614 (AB 473), operative Jan. 1, 2023; no amendment 2024–2026 as of 2026-08-19)
CA.notes: Mapped to fee.waiver only because it is the sole statutory hook for a local waiver policy; the clause is general and not fee-specific (flag for the reconcile step — may better sit under a general 'agency may exceed minimums' key if the dictionary has one). applies_to: all_public_bodies.

CA.legal_concept: Political Reform Act statements: copies ≤ $0.10/page; retrieval fee ≤ $5/request for records 5+ years old
CA.atomic_rule: A filing officer (including a city clerk) shall provide copies of reports and statements filed under the Political Reform Act at a charge not to exceed ten cents ($0.10) per page, and may charge a retrieval fee not to exceed five dollars ($5) per request for copies of reports and statements five or more years old; a request for several reports/statements at one time is a single request.
CA.trigger: Request for copies of campaign statements / statements of economic interests filed under the Political Reform Act
CA.source_language: Copies shall be provided at a charge not to exceed ten cents ($0.10) per page. In addition, the filing officer may charge a retrieval fee not to exceed five dollars ($5) per request for copies of reports and statements which are five or more years old. A request for more than one report or statement or report and statement at the same time shall be considered a single request.
CA.source_authority: Cal. Gov. Code § 81008 (Political Reform Act; two codified versions — Stats. 2013, ch. 654 and Stats. 2018, ch. 662 (SB 1239, conditionally operative) — carry identical fee text)
CA.effective_status: Current (fee text identical in both codified versions; the SB 1239 version's operative date is tied to Secretary of State certification under Stats. 2018, ch. 662, § 44 — verify which is operative if precision matters)
CA.notes: This is the 'statutory fee if applicable' path from § 7922.530(a) for one common municipal record class (city clerks are PRA filing officers). ceiling: $0.10/page; retrieval $5/request (5+ years old). No conditions or identification may be imposed on requesters. applies_to: all_public_bodies (all filing officers).

CA.legal_concept: Agenda-packet mailing fee may not exceed the cost of providing the service
CA.atomic_rule: The legislative body of a local agency may establish a fee for mailing the agenda or agenda packet to a person who has requested it, which fee shall not exceed the cost of providing the service; e-mail delivery must be provided on request where the agency has a website.
CA.trigger: Standing request for mailed agenda/agenda packet
CA.source_language: The legislative body may establish a fee for mailing the agenda or agenda packet, which fee shall not exceed the cost of providing the service.
CA.source_authority: Cal. Gov. Code § 54954.1 (Ralph M. Brown Act)
CA.notes: Record-specific (agenda materials) and local-agency only; the CPRA itself has no postage/handling rule. applies_to: municipalities.

CA.legal_concept: Inspection of meeting audio/video recordings free on agency equipment
CA.atomic_rule: Any inspection of a local agency's audio or video recording of an open meeting shall be provided without charge on equipment made available by the local agency; the recording is subject to CPRA inspection and may be erased 30 days after the recording notwithstanding § 34090.
CA.trigger: Request to inspect a recording of a legislative-body meeting
CA.source_language: Any recording of an open and public meeting made for whatever purpose by or at the direction of the local agency shall be subject to inspection pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Division 10 (commencing with Section 7920.000) of Title 1), but, notwithstanding Section 34090, may be erased or destroyed 30 days after the recording. Any inspection of an audio or video recording shall be provided without charge on equipment made available by the local agency.
CA.source_authority: Cal. Gov. Code § 54953.5(b) (Ralph M. Brown Act)
CA.notes: Inspection-only no-charge rule; copies of the recording remain subject to the § 7922.575(a) direct-cost standard. applies_to: municipalities. Numbered CA-9012 (CA-9011 intentionally unused — reserved slot for a § 7921.300 row was withdrawn because the purpose-neutrality rule likely already exists in the CA eligibility rows; see resolution 'commercial').

CO.legal_concept: Adjusted maximum hourly research-and-retrieval fee (Legislative Council posting)
CO.atomic_rule: The maximum hourly fee a custodian may charge for research and retrieval of public records after the first free hour is $41.37 effective July 1, 2024 (adjusted from $30.00 to $33.58 on July 1, 2019, and to $41.37 on July 1, 2024, by the Director of Research of Legislative Council Staff under § 24-72-205(6)(b)); a custodian must revise and publish its CORA policy to include the new fee before charging it.
CO.trigger: Custodian charges research-and-retrieval fee after the first hour under a pre-published written policy
CO.source_language: Section 24-72-205 (6) (b), C.R.S., requires the Director of Research of the Legislative Council Staff to adjust the Colorado Open Records Act maximum hourly fee for the research and retrieval of public documents for inflation on July 1, 2019, and each five years thereafter. The maximum hourly fee increased from $30.00 to $33.58 on July 1, 2019. Effective July 1, 2024, the maximum hourly fee will increase to $41.37. Before increasing the fee, government entities must revise and publish their Colorado Open Records Act policies to include the new fee. || Memo (June 12, 2024): Pursuant to Section 24-72-205 (6), C.R.S., the maximum hourly fee for the research and retrieval of public documents in response to a Colorado Open Records Act will increase from $33.58 to $41.37 as of July 1, 2024. State law allows government agencies to charge a fee for the research and retrieval of public documents that shall not exceed this amount, although they shall not charge a fee for the first hour of time expended on each request. Before increasing the fee, government entities must revise and publish their Colorado Open Records Act policies to include the new fee.
CO.source_authority: Legislative Council Staff, Director of Research — posting under C.R.S. § 24-72-205(6)(b); Memorandum 'Colorado Open Records Act Maximum Hourly Research and Retrieval Fee' (June 12, 2024)
CO.effective_status: Effective July 1, 2024 (next statutory adjustment due by July 1, 2029)
CO.notes: Delegated instrument for the § 24-72-205(6)(a) $30 figure. The statute text still reads 'thirty dollars per hour'; the operative ceiling is the posted adjusted figure. Binds every CORA custodian (state, agencies, institutions, political subdivisions incl. cities/towns). Ceiling; the municipality sets its own rate at or below $41.37 in its published policy. Memo phrase 'first hour of time expended on each request' supports a per-request reading of the free hour.

CO.legal_concept: No per-page fee for records provided in digital or electronic format
CO.atomic_rule: A custodian shall not charge a per-page fee for providing records in a digital or electronic format.
CO.trigger: Records are provided in a digital or electronic format
CO.source_language: A custodian may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a public record or a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing a copy, printout, or photograph of a public record in a format other than a standard page; except that a custodian shall not charge a per-page fee for providing records in a digital or electronic format.
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: Added by SB 23-286 (2023). Fixed $0 per page for digital/electronic delivery; the 25¢ ceiling (CO-0016) applies only to paper standard-page copies. Actual-cost charges for the medium/format (CO-0017) and research-and-retrieval fees remain available.

CO.legal_concept: Copy transmitted only after payment or payment arrangements; availability notice; three-business-day send
CO.atomic_rule: When a requester asks for transmission of a copy, the custodian shall, within the § 24-72-203(3)(a) period, notify the requester that a copy is available but will be sent only once the custodian receives payment or makes arrangements for payment of all transmission costs and all other fees lawfully allowed (unless waived by the custodian), and shall then send the record as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receiving payment or making payment arrangements.
CO.trigger: Requester seeks transmission (mail, delivery service, fax, or e-mail) of a copy of a public record
CO.clock_spec: notice within the 24-72-203(3)(a) period (3 working days, extendable) from request; record sent ≤ 3 business-days from receipt of payment or from making arrangements to receive payment
CO.source_language: Upon request for records transmission by a person seeking a copy of any public record, the custodian shall transmit a copy of the record by United States mail, other delivery service, facsimile, or electronic mail. No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail. Within the period specified in section 24-72-203 (3)(a), the custodian shall notify the record requester that a copy of the record is available but will only be sent to the requester once the custodian either receives payment or makes arrangements for receiving payment for all costs associated with records transmission and for all other fees lawfully allowed, unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian. Upon either receiving such payment or making arrangements to receive such payment at a later date, the custodian shall send the record to the requester as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receipt of, or making arrangements to receive, such payment.
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: Production gate: pay (or arrange payment) before release. Also functions as the statutory cost notice — no dollar/hour threshold; applies to every transmission request. Statute does not say what happens if the requester never pays (no withdrawal period). Mail/delivery-service transmission costs are chargeable; e-mail transmission is free (CO-0021).

CO.legal_concept: Credit card / electronic payment must be accepted if accepted for other services; processor fee pass-through
CO.atomic_rule: If a custodian allows the public to pay for any other service or product with a credit card or electronic payment, the custodian must allow the requester to pay any fee or deposit associated with the request by credit card or electronic payment, and may require the requester to pay any service charge or fee imposed by the payment processor.
CO.trigger: Custodian accepts credit-card or electronic payment for any other service or product
CO.source_language: If a custodian of a public record requested pursuant to this part 2 allows members of the public to pay for any other service or product provided by the custodian with a credit card or electronic payment, the custodian must allow the requester of the public record to pay any fee or deposit associated with the request with a credit card or via an electronic payment. The custodian may require a requester to pay any service charge or fee imposed by the processor of a credit card or electronic payment.
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: Added by SB 23-286 (2023). Conditional requirement (not unconditional). Statute recognizes a 'deposit associated with the request' but sets no deposit threshold or cap anywhere in CORA.

CO.legal_concept: Data-manipulation (programming) fee capped at actual cost
CO.atomic_rule: If, in response to a specific request, a political subdivision performs a manipulation of data to generate a record in a form it does not use, it may charge a reasonable fee not to exceed the actual cost of manipulating the data and generating the record.
CO.trigger: Custodian performs a manipulation of data to generate a record in a form not used by the public body
CO.source_language: If, in response to a specific request, the state or any of its agencies, institutions, or political subdivisions has performed a manipulation of data so as to generate a record in a form not used by the state or by said agency, institution, or political subdivision, a reasonable fee may be charged to the person making the request. Such fee shall not exceed the actual cost of manipulating the said data and generating the said record in accordance with the request. Persons making subsequent requests for the same or similar records may be charged a fee not in excess of the original fee.
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: Soft standard ('reasonable') bounded by 'actual cost of manipulating the said data and generating the said record'. No hourly figure. Applies expressly to political subdivisions.

CO.legal_concept: Subsequent requests for the same/similar manipulated-data record capped at the original fee
CO.atomic_rule: Persons making subsequent requests for the same or similar manipulated-data records may be charged a fee not in excess of the original fee.
CO.trigger: A later request for the same or similar record previously generated by data manipulation
CO.source_language: If, in response to a specific request, the state or any of its agencies, institutions, or political subdivisions has performed a manipulation of data so as to generate a record in a form not used by the state or by said agency, institution, or political subdivision, a reasonable fee may be charged to the person making the request. Such fee shall not exceed the actual cost of manipulating the said data and generating the said record in accordance with the request. Persons making subsequent requests for the same or similar records may be charged a fee not in excess of the original fee.
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: Scope limited to records generated by data manipulation under § 24-72-205(3); CORA has no general repeat-request or aggregation rule (aggregation of requests within 14 days was proposed in SB25-077 (vetoed 2025) and SB26-107 (postponed indefinitely 2026) and is not law).

CO.legal_concept: Fee basis for computer output other than word processing
CO.atomic_rule: If the public record is a result of computer output other than word processing, the fee for a copy, printout, or photograph may be based on recovery of the actual incremental costs of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with building and maintaining the information system.
CO.trigger: Record is computer output other than word processing
CO.source_language: If the public record is a result of computer output other than word processing, the fee for a copy, printout, or photograph thereof may be based on recovery of the actual incremental costs of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with building and maintaining the information system. Such fee may be reduced or waived by the custodian if the electronic services and products are to be used for a public purpose, including public agency program support, nonprofit activities, journalism, and academic research. Fee reductions and waivers shall be uniformly applied among persons who are similarly situated.
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: Soft standard: 'actual incremental costs' plus 'a reasonable portion' of system costs. No number. Interaction with the SB 23-286 prohibition on per-page fees for digital format (CO-9002) is not addressed in statute.

CO.legal_concept: Discretionary reduction/waiver of computer-output fee for public purposes; must be uniformly applied
CO.atomic_rule: The custodian may reduce or waive the computer-output fee if the electronic services and products are to be used for a public purpose, including public agency program support, nonprofit activities, journalism, and academic research; reductions and waivers shall be uniformly applied among similarly situated persons.
CO.trigger: Requester will use computer-output electronic services/products for a public purpose
CO.source_language: If the public record is a result of computer output other than word processing, the fee for a copy, printout, or photograph thereof may be based on recovery of the actual incremental costs of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with building and maintaining the information system. Such fee may be reduced or waived by the custodian if the electronic services and products are to be used for a public purpose, including public agency program support, nonprofit activities, journalism, and academic research. Fee reductions and waivers shall be uniformly applied among persons who are similarly situated.
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: Discretionary ('may'), limited to § 24-72-205(4) computer-output fees. Uniformity duty is mandatory once a waiver policy is applied. No written-denial, purpose-statement or appeal procedure is prescribed.

CO.legal_concept: Specifically-prescribed fees (incl. certified copies) override the CORA copy fee
CO.atomic_rule: Where the fee for a certified copy or other copy, printout, or photograph of a record is specifically prescribed by law, the specific fee applies instead of the § 24-72-205(5) fee.
CO.trigger: A statute or other law specifically prescribes a fee for the certified copy or other copy requested
CO.source_language: In all cases in which a person has the right to inspect a public record, the person may request a copy, printout, or photograph of the record. The custodian shall furnish a copy, printout, or photograph and may charge a fee determined in accordance with subsection (5) of this section; except that, when the custodian is the secretary of state, fees shall be determined and collected pursuant to section 24-21-104 (3), and when the custodian is the executive director of the department of personnel, fees shall be determined and collected pursuant to section 24-80-102 (10). Where the fee for a certified copy or other copy, printout, or photograph of a record is specifically prescribed by law, the specific fee shall apply.
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: CORA itself sets no certification/certified-copy fee. Same subsection routes the secretary of state (§ 24-21-104(3)) and the department of personnel (§ 24-80-102(10)) to their own fee statutes — state-agency regime, not municipal. No municipal certified-copy fee statute was found in C.R.S. Title 31 (2026 ed.).

CO.legal_concept: Certified copies free of charge for U.S. veterans'-benefits eligibility
CO.atomic_rule: Whenever a copy of a public record is required by the U.S. veterans administration or another federal agency to determine a veteran's or dependent's eligibility for federal service-connected benefits, the official charged with custody of the record shall provide a certified copy without charge to the applicant, a person acting on the applicant's behalf, or the agency representative.
CO.trigger: Certified copy required by a federal agency for veterans'-benefits eligibility determination
CO.source_language: Whenever a copy of any public record is required by the United States veterans administration or its successors or any other agency of the government of the United States to be used in determining the eligibility of any person who has served in the armed forces of the United States or any dependent of such person to participate in benefits for such person made available by the laws of the United States in relation to such service in the armed forces of the United States, the official charged with the custody of such public records, without charge, shall provide the applicant for such benefits or any person acting on his behalf, or the representative of such bureau or other agency, with a certified copy of such record.
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: Mandatory waiver (fixed $0) for one narrow ground; applies to any 'official charged with the custody of such public records' (municipal custodians included). Cited by Colo. AG Formal Opinion No. 01-1 (July 5, 2001), Q10.

CO.legal_concept: Custodian may waive recovery of transmission costs and other fees
CO.atomic_rule: The custodian may waive recovery of all or any portion of the transmission costs and other lawfully allowed fees otherwise payable before a copy is sent.
CO.trigger: Custodian elects not to recover costs/fees on a transmission request
CO.source_language: Upon request for records transmission by a person seeking a copy of any public record, the custodian shall transmit a copy of the record by United States mail, other delivery service, facsimile, or electronic mail. No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail. Within the period specified in section 24-72-203 (3)(a), the custodian shall notify the record requester that a copy of the record is available but will only be sent to the requester once the custodian either receives payment or makes arrangements for receiving payment for all costs associated with records transmission and for all other fees lawfully allowed, unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian. Upon either receiving such payment or making arrangements to receive such payment at a later date, the custodian shall send the record to the requester as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receipt of, or making arrangements to receive, such payment.
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: General discretionary waiver recognized by the clause 'unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian'. No grounds, purpose statement, written denial, or appeal prescribed. Criminal-justice-record fees: § 24-72-306(1) 'may waive fees at their discretion' (CO-9013).

CO.legal_concept: Supervision-of-copying fee equals the copy fee; requester pays cost of outside copying facilities
CO.atomic_rule: When the requester makes the copy under the custodian's supervision, the custodian may charge the same fee for supervising the copying as it may charge for furnishing a copy under § 24-72-205(5), and if other facilities are necessary the requester pays the cost of providing them.
CO.trigger: Custodian lacks copying facilities and the requester makes the copy under supervision, or copying must occur at other facilities
CO.source_language: If other facilities are necessary, the cost of providing them shall be paid by the person desiring a copy, printout, or photograph of the record. The custodian may establish a reasonable schedule of times for making a copy, printout, or photograph and may charge the same fee for the services rendered in supervising the copying, printing out, or photographing as the custodian may charge for furnishing a copy, printout, or photograph under subsection (5) of this section.
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: Supervision fee is capped by reference to the (5)(a) copy-fee ceiling (25¢/standard page or actual cost for other formats).

CO.legal_concept: Criminal-justice-record fees: actual costs incl. personnel for search, retrieval, redaction; 25¢/page; municipal governing body sets amounts
CO.atomic_rule: For criminal justice records requested under CCJRA, a criminal justice agency (including a municipal police department) may assess reasonable fees not to exceed actual costs, including personnel and equipment, for search, retrieval, and redaction; may waive fees at its discretion; may charge not more than 25¢ per standard page or actual cost for other formats; and where the agency is a department of a municipality, the amount of such fees shall be established by the municipal governing body in accordance with this subsection.
CO.trigger: Request is for criminal justice records under C.R.S. 24-72-301 et seq. (CCJRA)
CO.source_language: Criminal justice agencies may assess reasonable fees, not to exceed actual costs, including but not limited to personnel and equipment, for the search, retrieval, and redaction of criminal justice records requested pursuant to this part 3 and may waive fees at their discretion. In addition, criminal justice agencies may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a criminal justice record or a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing a copy, printout, or photograph of a criminal justice record in a format other than a standard page. Where fees for certified copies or other copies, printouts, or photographs of criminal justice records are specifically prescribed by law, such specific fees shall apply. Where the criminal justice agency is an agency or department of any county or municipality, the amount of such fees shall be established by the governing body of the county or municipality in accordance with this subsection (1).
CO.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
CO.notes: Separate fee regime for municipal police/criminal-justice records: no free first hour, no $41.37 cap, redaction time expressly chargeable, and the fee amounts are expressly delegated to the municipal governing body (defers_to_city). Not amended 2024–2026 (source note: L. 2008 last).

CO.legal_concept: Legislative Council Staff guidance: deposit for requests exceeding one hour of research and retrieval; true-up
CO.atomic_rule: Per Legislative Council Staff guidance, before completing a request that will take more than one hour of research and retrieval time the custodian may require a deposit equal to the estimated staff time, and may require additional payment or make a partial refund if actual time differs from the estimate.
CO.trigger: Request expected to exceed one hour of research and retrieval time
CO.source_language: Before completing a request that will take more than one hour of research and retrieval time, the custodian may require the requestor to pay a deposit equal to the estimated staff time needed to comply with the request. If the actual time spent turns out to be more or less than the initial estimate, the custodian may require an additional payment or make a partial refund of the deposit, respectively.
CO.source_authority: Legislative Council Staff, 'Colorado Law Summary: Colorado Open Records Act (CORA)' (last reviewed 09/18/2024), p. 2–3
CO.notes: GUIDANCE, NOT LAW: CORA's text contains no deposit threshold, deposit cap, or true-up rule; the statute only recognizes that a 'deposit associated with the request' may exist (§ 24-72-205(7)) and requires the research-and-retrieval policy to state its 'applicable conditions' (§ 24-72-205(6)(a)). This row records the Legislative Council's description of practice; it does not bind municipalities. Manual verification recommended before treating the one-hour trigger or 'equal to estimated staff time' as a value.

CT.legal_concept: DAS BEST guidelines on calculating fees for computer-stored records (delegated instrument under § 1-212(b)(4))
CT.atomic_rule: Under the DAS guidelines issued pursuant to § 1-212(b)(4), a fee for computer-stored records requiring programming may include only the employee's hourly salary for time spent formatting and programming the request (not search/retrieval time, not fringe benefits), the cost of the media, and the actual cost of any private-company services; printed computer-stored records follow the hard-copy per-page schedule; and programming/formatting costs may not be re-charged on later requests that reuse the existing programming.
CT.trigger: Request for computer-stored public records that require programming/formatting
CT.source_language: Section 1-212(b)(4) of the Connecticut General Statutes requires the Department of Administrative Services to provide guidelines to agencies regarding the calculation of fees charged for copies of computer-stored public records to ensure that such fees are reasonable and consistent among agencies. The following is a recommended policy for agency use: Upon receiving a request for computer-stored public records that require programming, a state agency should conform to the following policy, unless covered by another statutory fee schedule. • The calculation of fees should include only the time it takes the state employee(s) to format and program the request. • It cannot include the time it takes for the search and retrieval of the information. • The hourly salary for the state employee(s) doing the programming and formatting is an allowable charge. • Fees can not include any employee fringe benefit costs. • The cost of the media is an allowable charge (i.e., if the information is supplied on a diskette, the state agency can charge for the cost of that diskette). • If an agency uses a private company, the agency can only charge for the costs incurred for those services. Charges for any computer-stored public records that are printed rather than copied to diskette or other electronic storage device will follow hard copy FOI fee schedules. [...] • Once this programming and formatting is completed, the fees for any subsequent request that can be retrieved by using the existing programming and formatting cannot include those costs. The fee should only include the cost for the media or the cost for the hard copy printed information.
CT.source_authority: Conn. Dept. of Administrative Services, Bureau of Enterprise Systems and Technology, 'Policy Guidelines' under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-212(b)(4) (electronic_data_guidelines.pdf)
CT.effective_status: Current (undated; posted on DAS 'FOI Guidelines for Agencies and Municipalities' page; statute reference to DAS current since P.A. 11-51/12-205)
CT.notes: Delegated instrument for § 1-212(b)(4). Text is framed as 'a recommended policy' for 'a state agency'; the statute's component list itself binds all public agencies. Worked example: 3 hrs × $15/hr + $0.75 diskette = $45.75; 1 hr run time not chargeable. Not a rate schedule — the rate is the actual hourly salary. Municipal applicability of the guideline as such is advisory.

CT.legal_concept: Town clerk copy and certification fees for recorded/filed documents
CT.atomic_rule: A town clerk shall receive $1 per page (or fraction) for a copy, in any format, of any document recorded or filed in the clerk's office; $2 for certifying such a copy; the actual cost for a copy of any survey or map; and $2 for certifying a copy of a survey or map.
CT.trigger: Copy or certified copy of a document, survey or map recorded or filed in the town clerk's office (land records etc.)
CT.source_language: Town clerks shall receive, for a copy, in any format, of any document either recorded or filed in their offices, one dollar for each page or fractional part thereof, as the case may be; for certifying any copy of the same, two dollars; for making a copy of any survey or map, the actual cost thereof; and for certifying such copy of a survey or map, two dollars.
CT.effective_status: Current (Gen. Stat. rev. to Jan. 1, 2025; § 7-34a not amended in the 2025 or 2026 sessions per reference table/PA search)
CT.notes: Municipal-only, record-specific: displaces the FOIA $0.50/page ceiling and the $1/$0.50 certification fee for records in the town clerk's custody ('Except as otherwise provided by law', § 1-212(e); 'Except as otherwise provided by state statute', § 1-211(a)). Fixed ('shall receive'), not a ceiling. Applies to municipalities.

CT.legal_concept: No fee for time spent reviewing or redacting records; § 1-212 is the exclusive list of chargeable fees
CT.atomic_rule: A public agency may not charge for time spent reviewing records for exempt material or redacting them (redaction is not 'formatting or programming' under § 1-212(b)(1)); § 1-212 sets forth all permissible fees, so for paper records only the per-page copy fee may be charged; and a prepayment demand may rest only on fees the Act permits and not on costs that would have to be waived because the records are exempt.
CT.trigger: Any request; especially requests requiring review/redaction (paper or computer-stored, incl. body-camera video)
CT.source_language: 35. The provisions of §1-212, G.S., set forth all permissible fees that an agency may charge in connection with providing copies of public records. See §1-212(a), G.S., ("[t]he fee for any copy provided in accordance with the [FOI] Act.") (Emphasis added); see also §1-212(b), G.S., ("[t]he fee for any copy provided in accordance with subsection (a) of section 1-211. . . .") (Emphasis added). 36. In the context of non-computer-stored records (i.e. paper records), the explicit terms of §§1-212(a)(A) and (B), G.S., limit permissible fees to copying fees of twenty-five cents per page for state agencies and fifty cents per page for all other public agencies. 37. It is clear, therefore, that the fees a public agency may charge for paper records are solely derived from the costs attributable to providing the records in the prescribed medium. As an agency would not be able to provide original versions of paper records to requestors, they must make physical copies of such records to provide them to requestors. In the case of paper records, the physical copy is the prescribed medium in which the agency is obligated to provide records. Notably, nothing in §1-212(a), G.S., would permit the respondents to charge a fee for (or predicate their fee estimate on) any of the labor costs identified in paragraph 33, above. 52. The Commission has long held that public agencies cannot charge a fee for the time spent redacting public records, and the Commission's position, as described in paragraphs 50 and 51, above, is consistent with both case law and its prior decisions. 66. Based upon the foregoing, it is found that the plain language of §1-212(b), G.S., does not support the respondents' position that the time spent redacting records constitute permissible charges under the FOI Act. 67. The Commission has previously held that the redaction of public records does not constitute "programming or formatting" for which fees may be assessed pursuant to §1-212(b)(1), G.S. See David Collins and The Day, v. Chief, Police Department, City of New London et al., Docket FIC#2022-0176 (April 12, 2023). [...] 69. The Commission's previous conclusions in Osmond I, Osmond II, and Clark do not support the respondents' position that it is permissible to charge a fee for time spent redacting. The Commission reaches the same conclusion with respect to the respondents' contention that they can charge a fee for time spent in anticipation of or preparation for redactions. 70. In addition, the Commission has also previously concluded that no provision of the FOI Act permits a public agency to charge time taken to review public records to ascertain whether they contain any information that is exempt from disclosure. See Pamela Walsh v. Chief, Police Department, City of New London; and Police Department, City of New London, Docket # FIC 2010-369 (May 11, 2011). 74. The Commission also finds the respondents' position unavailing regarding their perceived ability to charge prepayment fees, based upon redacting exempt information—when such fees would, ultimately, need to be waived pursuant to §1-212(d)(2), G.S. Taken to the extreme, the respondents could charge the complainant for $25,000 in fees and then have to return every dollar in the event that every potential record was exempt from disclosure. 75. As the Commission found in Clark, it so too finds here that it is entirely improper for the respondents to request prepayment of estimated fees predicated on costs that would ultimately need to be waived, pursuant to §1-212(d)(2), G.S. || FIC 2022-0176: 37. It is found that the respondents arrived at the fee of $628.99 by using the hourly rate of the employee who was trained and charged with reviewing and redacting (i.e., pixelating and removing audio) from the requested video footage ($612) and copying such footage onto a flash drive ($16.99). 38. At the hearing, the respondents contended that the process of redacting video footage constitutes "formatting or programming" that changes the format of the original video and results in the creation of a new video. 39. It is found that the pixelations and removal of audio conducted by the respondents were performed using existing computer software and that the respondents did not have to develop a program or contract with an outside entity to develop a program in order to comply with the records request. 40. It is found that the respondents failed to prove that the tasks, described in paragraph 37, above, constituted formatting and programming functions within the meaning of §1-212(b)(1), G.S. 41. It is concluded that the $612 fee is not allowable under §1-212(b)(1), G.S. 42. Nevertheless, pursuant to §1-212(c), G.S., "[a] public agency may require the prepayment of any fee required or permitted under the Freedom of Information Act if such fee is estimated to be ten dollars or more..." It is found that the fee for copying the footage onto a flash drive was more than ten dollars (i.e., $16.99) and therefore the respondents were permitted to require prepayment of such fee.
CT.source_authority: FOIC Final Decision, DiPalma v. Secretary, Office of Policy & Management, Docket #FIC 2025-0213 (Mar. 25, 2026), ¶¶ 29, 35-37, 52, 66-70, 74-78; FOIC Final Decision, Collins & The Day v. Chief, Police Department, City of New London, Docket #FIC 2022-0176 (Apr. 12, 2023), ¶¶ 37-42; citing Walsh v. Chief, Police Dept., City of New London, FIC 2010-369 (May 11, 2011)
CT.effective_status: Current (final decisions of Apr. 12, 2023 and Mar. 25, 2026; statute unamended; SB 225 (2026) redaction-fee bill not enacted)
CT.notes: FOIC contested-case decisions bind the parties and state the Commission's settled construction; a municipality (New London PD) was the respondent in FIC 2022-0176 and FIC 2010-369. Minor typographic normalization of PDF text extraction (e.g., '3 7.' → '37.'). Kept as one row: a single exclusivity holding with its corollaries.

CT.legal_concept: No fee for electronic transmission of nonexempt computer-stored records requested electronically
CT.atomic_rule: When a requester asks that computer-stored records be provided electronically (e.g., by e-mail), the agency may not charge a copy fee for those nonexempt records — there is no cost associated with transmitting a record electronically — and may not print them out for its own convenience and charge a per-page fee; but if it must make a copy of a record in order to redact information required by law to be redacted, it may charge the statutory fee for that copy.
CT.trigger: Request for computer-stored records with electronic delivery requested
CT.source_language: 59. In Stedman, the Commission found that: the superintendent printed out the potentially responsive emails because it was easier for her to read them that way, rather than on her computer, and because she believed that some of the emails might need to be redacted. Although the Commission appreciates that it may be easier for some people to review emails when they are in printed form, as opposed to reading them on a computer screen, the FOI Act does not permit a public agency to charge a fee for a copy of a nonexempt electronic record, when the requestor has asked that such record be provided electronically. The Commission takes administrative notice of the fact that there is no cost associated with transmitting a record electronically. (Emphasis added). Id. at ¶ 18. 60. [...] Id. at n. 2. ("The Commission notes, however, that if a public agency receives a request for a copy of, or to inspect a record that contains information that is required by law to be redacted, and the public agency must make a copy of the record in order to redact such information, the public agency may charge the requestor the statutory fee for that copy.") (Emphasis in original). 61. Additionally, such records were requested to be produced in an electronic format (specifically, email). Therefore, the District was not required to print out the records to provide them in the medium requested. Id. ("Accordingly it is concluded that the respondents violated §§1-211(a) and 1-212(b), G.S., by charging the complainant a copy fee of $.25 per page for unredacted paper copies, rather than providing them to her electronically, free of charge as she requested.") (Emphasis added).
CT.source_authority: FOIC Final Decision, Stedman v. Vogel, Superintendent, Regional School District #1, Docket #FIC 2018-0293 (Feb. 13, 2019) ¶¶ 18, 20 & n.2, as quoted and reaffirmed in FIC 2025-0213 (Mar. 25, 2026) ¶¶ 57-62
CT.notes: Stedman itself was not opened; its holdings are reproduced verbatim inside FIC 2025-0213 (opened). Respondent in Stedman was a regional school district (local public agency). Interacts with § 1-211(a) (electronic copy sent to requester's e-mail address if the agency can reasonably make it).

CT.legal_concept: Hand-held scanner copying fee structure — ceiling $20 per visit
CT.atomic_rule: A public agency may establish a fee structure, not to exceed twenty dollars, for an individual to pay each time the individual copies records at the agency with a hand-held scanner; any individual may copy a public record with such a scanner.
CT.trigger: Requester copies records on-site with a battery-operated hand-held scanner
CT.source_language: (g) Any individual may copy a public record through the use of a hand-held scanner. A public agency may establish a fee structure not to exceed twenty dollars for an individual to pay each time the individual copies records at the agency with a hand-held scanner. As used in this section, “hand-held scanner” means a battery operated electronic scanning device the use of which (1) leaves no mark or impression on the public record, and (2) does not unreasonably interfere with the operation of the public agency.
CT.effective_status: Current — Gen. Stat. rev. to Jan. 1, 2025; § 1-212 not in the 2026 Supplement (rev. to Jan. 1, 2026 — only § 1-210(b)(17) amended in 2025); last amended P.A. 12-205; 2026-session public acts (through P.A. 26-68) searched — none amend § 1-212
CT.notes: Ceiling ($20 per session), discretionary ('may establish'); city sets the structure at or below $20. Applies to all public agencies. Raised from $10 by June Sp. Sess. P.A. 09-3.

CT.legal_concept: Copies of names of registered voters — ceiling 3¢ per name or cost, whichever less
CT.atomic_rule: Notwithstanding any other provision of § 1-212, the fee for any copy of the names of registered voters shall not exceed three cents per name delivered or the cost thereof to the public agency as determined under § 1-212(b), whichever is less.
CT.trigger: Request for a copy of registered-voter names (e.g., from a municipal registrar of voters)
CT.source_language: Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, the fee for any copy of the names of registered voters shall not exceed three cents per name delivered or the cost thereof to the public agency, as determined pursuant to this subsection, whichever is less.
CT.effective_status: Current — Gen. Stat. rev. to Jan. 1, 2025; § 1-212 not in the 2026 Supplement (rev. to Jan. 1, 2026 — only § 1-210(b)(17) amended in 2025); last amended P.A. 12-205; 2026-session public acts (through P.A. 26-68) searched — none amend § 1-212
CT.notes: Record-specific ceiling; municipal registrars are the usual custodians. Not a commercial-purpose rate.

CT.legal_concept: Inspection requiring redaction — statutory copy fee chargeable for the copies the agency must make
CT.atomic_rule: If a request to inspect (or copy) a record that contains information required by law to be redacted obliges the agency to make a copy of the record in order to redact it, the agency may charge the requester the statutory fee for that copy (the requester keeps the copy); inspection itself carries no fee provision.
CT.trigger: Inspection request for paper records containing information that must be redacted by law
CT.source_language: 54. [...] Since [the requestor's] request to inspect public records in this case required the department to make copies of those records in order to comply with the law, the department was entitled to charge [the requestor] any fees that applicable statutes permit. Of course, [the requestor] would be entitled to keep the copies for his own use.
