[Kozlowski, 1997 WL 435860, at *2-3, as quoted in FIC 2025-0213] || Stedman n.2: The Commission notes, however, that if a public agency receives a request for a copy of, or to inspect a record that contains information that is required by law to be redacted, and the public agency must make a copy of the record in order to redact such information, the public agency may charge the requestor the statutory fee for that copy.
CT.source_authority: Kozlowski v. FOIC, Docket No. CV-96-0556965, 1997 WL 435860 (Conn. Super. Ct. July 29, 1997) and FOIC Stedman (FIC 2018-0293) n.2, both as quoted in FOIC Final Decision FIC 2025-0213 (Mar. 25, 2026) ¶¶ 53-56, 60
CT.source_type: Records-authority final decision (FOIC) quoting Superior Court decision
CT.notes: Superior Court (trial-level) decision quoted by the FOIC; not an appellate holding. Kept because it is the only source stating when a fee attaches to an inspection request. Municipal applicability: general (Stedman respondent was a regional school district).

FL.legal_concept: Copies furnished upon payment of the prescribed fee
FL.atomic_rule: The custodian shall furnish a copy or certified copy of a public record upon payment of the fee prescribed by law; if no fee is prescribed by law, the s. 119.07(4) fees are the fees authorized.
FL.trigger: Requester asks for a copy or certified copy of a public record
FL.source_language: The custodian of public records shall furnish a copy or a certified copy of the record upon payment of the fee prescribed by law. If a fee is not prescribed by law, the following fees are authorized:
FL.effective_status: Current (2025 Florida Statutes; s. 119.07 last amended s. 1, ch. 2021-173; no 2024, 2025 or 2026 amendment to subsection (4) — CS/HB 437 (2026), which would have restricted fees, authorized waivers and required written cost estimates, passed the House 111-0 on 3/4/2026 and died in Senate Rules 3/13/2026)
FL.notes: Statutory production gate: copies are furnished 'upon payment'; courts read this as permitting the custodian to delay production until fees are remitted (Promenade D'Iberville, 1st DCA 2014) and to require advance deposits (Colby; Morris Publishing; Dorchester Holdings) — see FL-9006. Binds every 'agency' (s. 119.011(2) includes municipal officers/units). Inspection itself remains free (AGO 85-03) except the s. 119.07(4)(d) special service charge.

FL.legal_concept: Department of State special service charge rule: 'extensive' = more than 15 minutes; quarter-hour increments; prepayment of estimated charge
FL.atomic_rule: For Department of State public-records requests, 'extensive' means more than 15 minutes of personnel time; the special service charge is computed to the nearest quarter hour exceeding 15 minutes at the wages-and-benefits cost of the lowest-paid personnel with the necessary skill; the requestor must prepay estimated special service charges, with refund of any excess or billing of any shortfall, and release is withheld until a shortfall is paid.
FL.trigger: Department of State request that requires extensive clerical/supervisory assistance or IT resources under s. 119.07(4)(d)
FL.source_language: 1-2.0031 Public Records Requests: Special Service Charge. (1) When a public records request is of the nature described in Section 119.07(4)(d), F.S., the following will apply: (a) The term “extensive” means more than 15 minutes expended by personnel to complete all tasks defined in paragraphs (b) and (c), below. (b) The term “clerical or supervisory assistance” includes searching for and or locating the requested record, reviewing for statutorily exempt information, deletion of statutorily exempt information, and preparing, copying and re-filing of the requested record. (c) The term “use of information technology resources” includes the setup and implementation of information technology defined in Section 282.0041(11), F.S. (2)(a) The Department will determine which personnel are appropriate to provide assistance in fulfilling the request. The special service charge will be computed to the nearest quarter of an hour exceeding 15 minutes based on the cost of wages and benefits of the lowest paid personnel who, in the discretion of the Department, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request. The special service charge shall be in addition to the duplication charge as provided in Sections 119.07(4)(a) and (b), F.S., and will be assessed regardless of the number of individual copies made. Payment for special services shall also be imposed where extensive use of personnel or information technology is necessary to determine whether the public record exists or is exempt from public disclosure. (b) The requestor shall be required to pay any estimated special service charges, as determined by the Department, prior to personnel rendering such services. The Department will refund to the requestor any monies deposited with the Department in excess of the actual costs incurred to fulfill a request, or, in the alternative, the requestor shall be required to remit additional monies to pay for any costs in excess of the deposit. In the event the requestor fails to remit additional monies to cover costs in excess of the monies deposited, the Department shall withhold releasing any public records identified pursuant to that request until those amounts are paid in full. Rulemaking Authority 20.10(3), 119.07(4)(d) FS. Law Implemented 119.07(4)(d) FS. History–New 3-21-06, Amended 9-17-08.
FL.source_authority: Fla. Admin. Code R. 1-2.0031 (Department of State)
FL.notes: AGENCY-SPECIFIC (Department of State only) — s. 119.07(4)(d) contains no rulemaking delegation binding municipalities; each state agency that adopts a rule sets its own definition (DOC rule upheld in Florida Institutional Legal Services, 1st DCA 1991, also used 15 minutes). Recorded as guidance for the municipal regime: cities may adopt a similar policy but are not bound by this figure. Not a delegated instrument for cities.

FL.legal_concept: Copy in the medium requested; fee for non-routine medium or compilation governed by s. 119.07(4)
FL.atomic_rule: An agency must provide a copy of an electronic record in the medium requested if it maintains the record in that medium and may charge a fee in accordance with ch. 119; if it elects to provide a copy in a medium not routinely used or to compile information not routinely maintained or requiring substantial manipulation or programming, the fee must be in accordance with s. 119.07(4).
FL.trigger: Requester asks for an electronic record in a particular medium, or a compilation/programming
FL.source_language: (f) Each agency that maintains a public record in an electronic recordkeeping system shall provide to any person, pursuant to this chapter, a copy of any public record in that system which is not exempted by law from public disclosure. An agency must provide a copy of the record in the medium requested if the agency maintains the record in that medium, and the agency may charge a fee in accordance with this chapter. For the purpose of satisfying a public records request, the fee to be charged by an agency if it elects to provide a copy of a public record in a medium not routinely used by the agency, or if it elects to compile information not routinely developed or maintained by the agency or that requires a substantial amount of manipulation or programming, must be in accordance with s. 119.07(4).
FL.effective_status: Current (2025 Florida Statutes; last amended s. 1, ch. 2005-251)
FL.notes: Routes electronic-media and programming charges to the s. 119.07(4) schedule: material/supplies at actual cost of duplication (FL-0022/FL-0023) plus the special service charge only where 'extensive' (FL-0025). Binds all agencies incl. municipalities.

FL.legal_concept: Advance deposit / prepayment before production is permitted (case law collected in the AG Manual)
FL.atomic_rule: An agency's policy of requiring payment of a deposit or advance payment before redaction and delivery of voluminous records is permissible ('facially reasonable'); the custodian may delay production if the requester fails to remit the appropriate fees; reasonableness of the policy and its application is judged case by case.
FL.trigger: Voluminous/extensive request; agency policy requires deposit or prepayment
FL.source_language: Section 119.07(4)(a)1., F.S., states that the custodian of public records shall furnish a copy or a certified copy of the record “upon payment of the fee prescribed by law . . . .” See Wootton v. Cook, 590 So. 2d 1039, 1040 (Fla. 1st DCA 1991) (if a requestor “identifies a record with sufficient specificity to permit [the agency] to identify it and forwards the appropriate fee, [the agency] must furnish by mail a copy of the record.”) (e.s.); and Promenade D’Iberville, LLC v. Sundy 145 So. 3d 980, 983 (Fla. 1st DCA 2014) (a records custodian may delay production “if the requesting party fails to remit the appropriate fees”). Accordingly, an agency’s policy of requiring the payment of a deposit prior to redaction and delivery of hundreds of telephone recordings related to a criminal trial was determined to be “facially reasonable.” Morris Publishing Group, LLC v. State, 154 So. 3d 528, 534 (Fla. 1st DCA 2015), review denied, 163 So. 3d 512 (Fla. 2015). Accord Board of County Commissioners of Highlands County v. Colby, 976 So. 2d 31, 37 (Fla. 2d DCA 2008), noting that a “policy of requiring an advance deposit seems prudent given the legislature’s determination that taxpayers should not shoulder the entire expense of responding to an extensive request for public records.” “[T]he reasonableness of a policy and its application — based on the facts in a particular case — guides whether an abuse of discretion is shown.” Morris Publishing Group, LLC at 534. And see Agency for Health Care Administration v. Zuckerman Spaeder, LLP, 221 So. 3d 1260 (Fla. 1st DCA 2017) (lower court abused its discretion by ordering the agency to produce a large number of responsive public records within 48 hours of the issuance of the order without requiring advance payment of the agency’s invoices associated with production of the records); City of St. Petersburg v. Dorchester Holdings, LLC, 331 So. 3d 799 (Fla. 2d DCA 2021) (trial court erred in holding that the City’s prepayment request constituted an unlawful interference with requester’s right of access to public records).
FL.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 187, citing Wootton v. Cook, 590 So. 2d 1039 (Fla. 1st DCA 1991); Promenade D'Iberville, LLC v. Sundy, 145 So. 3d 980 (Fla. 1st DCA 2014); Morris Publishing Group, LLC v. State, 154 So. 3d 528 (Fla. 1st DCA 2015); Bd. of County Comm'rs of Highlands County v. Colby, 976 So. 2d 31 (Fla. 2d DCA 2008); AHCA v. Zuckerman Spaeder, LLP, 221 So. 3d 1260 (Fla. 1st DCA 2017); City of St. Petersburg v. Dorchester Holdings, LLC, 331 So. 3d 799 (Fla. 2d DCA 2021)
FL.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
FL.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
FL.notes: No statutory deposit threshold or percentage; authority is appellate case law as collected in the AG's Manual (verbatim from the Manual, not from the opinions themselves — opinions not opened). Applies to all agencies incl. cities (Colby = county; Dorchester = city). Municipal-policy dependent: 'the reasonableness of a policy and its application' governs.

FL.legal_concept: Unpaid prior-request fees: agency may withhold further records until paid; may not impose a permanent ban; may bill deposit shortfall
FL.atomic_rule: An agency may refuse to produce additional records until the requester pays the fees owed for a previous request, but a failure to timely pay does not permit banning the requester permanently once the amount owing is paid; the custodian may bill the requester for any shortfall between a deposit and the actual cost when copies were made and the requester then says the records are not needed.
FL.trigger: Requester has an unpaid balance from a prior request, or abandons a request after copies were made against a deposit
FL.source_language: An agency may refuse to produce additional records if the fees for a previous request for records have not been paid by the requestor. See Lozman v. City of Riviera Beach, 995 So. 2d 1027 (Fla. 4th DCA 2008) (s. 119.07[4], F.S., “does not require the City to do any more than what it did in this case,” i.e., require Lozman to pay the bill for the first group of records he requested before the city would make any further documents available). And see AGO 05-28 (custodian authorized to bill the requestor for any shortfall between the deposit and the actual cost of copying the public records when the copies have been made and the requesting party subsequently advises the city that the records are not needed). Compare, Smith v. State, 335 So. 3d 795 (Fla. 2d DCA 2022) (Smith’s failure to timely pay fees to obtain requested public records does not permit the agency to ban him from ever obtaining records in the future, provided Smith pays the amount owing for the first request).
FL.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 187-188, citing Lozman v. City of Riviera Beach, 995 So. 2d 1027 (Fla. 4th DCA 2008); AGO 05-28; Smith v. State, 335 So. 3d 795 (Fla. 2d DCA 2022)
FL.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
FL.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
FL.notes: No statutory 'withdrawn after N days' rule exists in ch. 119. Prior-debt gate is a Permission (city 'may'), from a case involving a city. Verbatim from the Manual; underlying opinions/AGO 05-28 not opened.

FL.legal_concept: Agency must respond to requests for cost information; fees not collectible where agency policy required an estimate/invoice before production and none was given
FL.atomic_rule: An agency must respond to a requester's request for information as to copying costs (a schedule alone is not the total cost); where an agency's own policy requires an estimate or invoice before production and none was provided (and no advance agreement), a court may deny collection of the s. 119.07(4)(d) charge after production; the AG strongly encourages agencies to adopt a written procedure addressing the special service charge.
FL.trigger: Requester asks what the copies will cost; agency intends to impose a special service charge
FL.source_language: In order to comply with the statutory directive that an agency provide copies of public records upon payment of the statutory fee, an agency must respond to requests for information as to copying costs. Wootton v. Cook, supra. See also Woodard v. State, 885 So. 2d 444 (Fla. 4th DCA 2004), remanding a case for further proceedings where the custodian forwarded only information relating to the statutory fee schedule rather than the total cost to copy the requested records. In Miami Dade College v. Nader + Museu I, LLLP, 47 F.L.W. D1814 (Fla. 3d DCA August 31, 2022), the court affirmed the trial court’s refusal to grant an agency’s motion to collect fees under s. 119.07(4)(d), F.S., because the agency failed to provide the requester with an estimate or invoice prior to production thereby violating both its own policies and procedures and the language of s. 119.07(4), F.S. And see AGO 13-03, in which the Attorney General’s Office strongly encouraged agencies to adopt a public records procedure that addresses imposition of special service charge.
FL.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 188, citing Wootton v. Cook, 590 So. 2d 1039 (Fla. 1st DCA 1991); Woodard v. State, 885 So. 2d 444 (Fla. 4th DCA 2004); Miami Dade College v. Nader + Museu I, LLLP, 47 F.L.W. D1814 (Fla. 3d DCA Aug. 31, 2022); AGO 13-03
FL.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
FL.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
FL.notes: Structural: no dollar/hour threshold and no requester response window in Florida law; the duty is to answer cost inquiries and (per Nader + Museu) to follow the agency's own estimate/invoice policy before production. CS/HB 437 (2026) would have added a written-estimate-on-request duty; it died in Senate Rules 3/13/2026.

FL.legal_concept: No statutory fee waiver; agency may choose to furnish informational copies free; no indigent/inmate exemption
FL.atomic_rule: Chapter 119 contains no fee-waiver provision and no exemption for indigent persons or inmates; an agency is not precluded from choosing to provide informational copies of public records without charge.
FL.trigger: Requester seeks free copies or a fee waiver
FL.source_language: An agency is not precluded from choosing to provide informational copies of public records without charge. AGO 90-81. However, chapter 119, F.S., does not contain a provision that prohibits agencies from charging indigent persons or inmates the applicable statutory fee to obtain copies of public records. See Roesch v. State, 633 So. 2d 1, 3 (Fla. 1993) (indigent inmate not entitled to receive copies of public records free of charge nor to have original state attorney files mailed to him in prison; prisoners are “in the same position as anyone else seeking public records who cannot pay” the required costs); [...] and Yanke v. State, 588 So. 2d 4 (Fla. 2d DCA 1991), review denied, 595 So. 2d 559 (Fla. 1992), cert. denied, 112 S.Ct. 1592 (1992) (prisoner must pay copying and postage charges to have copies of public records mailed to him).
FL.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 188, citing AGO 90-81; Roesch v. State, 633 So. 2d 1 (Fla. 1993); Yanke v. State, 588 So. 2d 4 (Fla. 2d DCA 1991)
FL.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
FL.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
FL.notes: Waiver is purely discretionary local policy; no statutory grounds, no purpose statement (purpose may not be required — FL-9014), no written-denial or appeal step. Yanke also supports charging postage for mailed copies (see FL-9011). Verbatim from Manual; AGO 90-81 itself not opened.

FL.legal_concept: Overhead, travel and development costs may not be added; labor cost may include salary and benefits actually incurred
FL.atomic_rule: An agency may not add overhead costs (utilities, office expenses), travel time to retrieve off-site records, or costs to recoup development/production of the records; a special service charge may include the employee's salary and benefits but must be reasonable and based on actual labor cost incurred; absent an 'extensive' trigger, only the actual cost of duplication may be charged for computerized records.
FL.trigger: Agency computes a labor/special service charge or a copy charge
FL.source_language: An agency should not consider the furnishing of public records to be a “revenue-generating operation.” AGO 85-03. See also AGO 89-93 (city not authorized to sell copies of its growth management book for $35.00 each when the actual cost to reproduce the book is $15.10 per copy; city is limited to charging only the costs authorized by Ch. 119, F.S.). The Public Records Act does not authorize the addition of overhead costs such as utilities or other office expenses to the charge for public records. AGO 99-41. Similarly, an agency may not charge for travel time to obtain public records stored off-premises. AGO 90-07. For example, if municipal pension records are stored in a records storage facility outside city limits, the city may not pass along to the public records requester the costs to retrieve the records. Inf. Op. to Sugarman, September 5, 1997. [...] An agency may not assess fees designed to recoup the original cost of developing or producing the records. AGO 88-23 (state attorney not authorized to impose a charge to recover part of costs incurred in production of a training program; the fee to obtain a copy of the videotape of such program is limited to the actual cost of duplication of the tape). [...] Therefore, unless a specific request for copies requires extensive clerical or supervisory assistance or extensive use of information technology resources so as to trigger the special service charge authorized by s. 119.07(4)(d), F.S., an agency may charge only the actual cost of duplication for copies of computerized public records. AGO 99-41. The imposition of the service charge, however, is dependent upon the nature or volume of records requested, not on the cost to either develop or maintain the records or the database system. Id. || In Board of County Commissioners of Highlands County v. Colby, 976 So. 2d 31 (Fla. 2d DCA 2008), the court approved a county’s special service charge pursuant to s. 119.07(4), F.S., which included both an employee’s salary and benefits in calculating the labor cost for the special service charge, recognizing, however, that the charge must be reasonable and based upon the actual labor costs incurred by or attributable to the county. See Trout v. Bucher, 205 So. 3d 876 (Fla. 4th DCA 2016) (supervisor of elections not required to charge the lowest hourly rate of the employee capable of doing the work needed to comply with Trout’s request to inspect ballots in accordance with s. 119.07[5], F.S., because s. 119.07[4][d] allows the agency to charge the labor cost of the personnel that is “actually incurred” by the agency where extensive assistance is required).
FL.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 186, 189, citing AGO 85-03; AGO 89-93; AGO 99-41; AGO 90-07; AGO 88-23; Bd. of County Comm'rs of Highlands County v. Colby, 976 So. 2d 31 (Fla. 2d DCA 2008); Trout v. Bucher, 205 So. 3d 876 (Fla. 4th DCA 2016)
FL.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
FL.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
FL.notes: Overhead surcharge = not permitted (0%); fringe benefits enter only as part of the actual labor cost (Colby). AGO 89-93 and Inf. Op. to Sugarman are city-specific. Reinforces the s. 119.011(1) definition (FL-0023). Verbatim from Manual; AGOs not opened.

FL.legal_concept: Review/redaction labor: not ordinarily chargeable, but the special service charge may cover voluminous exemption review
FL.atomic_rule: An agency is not ordinarily authorized to charge for the cost to review records for exempt material, but where the volume of records and number of potential exemptions make review and redaction time-consuming the special service charge may be imposed for that work, and a requester may be required to pay the cost of searching, review and redaction prior to production.
FL.trigger: Voluminous request whose records require exemption review and redaction
FL.source_language: An agency is not ordinarily authorized to charge for the cost to review records for statutorily exempt material. AGO 84-81. However, the special service charge may be imposed for this work if the volume of records and the number of potential exemptions make review and redaction of the records a time-consuming task. See Florida Institutional Legal Services v. Florida Department of Corrections, 579 So. 2d at 269. And see Agency for Health Care Administration v. Zuckerman Spaeder, LLP, 221 So. 3d 1260 (Fla. 1st DCA 2017) (prior court decisions as well as the language in s. 119.07[4], F.S., dictate that the requester, who had submitted several voluminous public records requests for records which included confidential information “should be required to pay for the cost of searching, review, and redaction of exempted information prior to production”). Accordingly, because “the Public Records Act requires a records custodian to determine whether the requested records exist, locate the records, and review each record to determine if any of those records are exempt from production,” the agency may charge the special service charge as authorized under s. 119.07(4)(d), F.S., for the cost to review voluminous requested records for exempt material. City of St. Petersburg v. Dorchester Holdings, LLC, 331 So. 3d 799 (Fla. 2d DCA 2021).
FL.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 186, citing AGO 84-81; Florida Institutional Legal Services v. DOC, 579 So. 2d 267 (Fla. 1st DCA 1991); AHCA v. Zuckerman Spaeder, LLP, 221 So. 3d 1260 (Fla. 1st DCA 2017); City of St. Petersburg v. Dorchester Holdings, LLC, 331 So. 3d 799 (Fla. 2d DCA 2021)
FL.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
FL.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
FL.notes: Review/redaction labor is chargeable only through the s. 119.07(4)(d) 'extensive' gate; rate = actual labor cost (Gudinas: attorney rate approved where only attorney/paralegal could do the review; Colby: lower-paid employee's salary approved). Dorchester involved a city. Verbatim from Manual.

FL.legal_concept: Postage for mailed copies is payable by the requester; e-mail delivery carries no labor/overhead charge
FL.atomic_rule: A requester must pay copying and postage charges to have copies mailed; an agency may charge only the 'actual cost of duplication' when it e-mails records, and the definition allows no labor or overhead cost, so forwarding e-mail in lieu of photocopying carried no identifiable duplication cost.
FL.trigger: Copies are mailed or e-mailed to the requester
FL.source_language: and Yanke v. State, 588 So. 2d 4 (Fla. 2d DCA 1991), review denied, 595 So. 2d 559 (Fla. 1992), cert. denied, 112 S.Ct. 1592 (1992) (prisoner must pay copying and postage charges to have copies of public records mailed to him). || Cf. AGO 13-03 (while agency may charge “actual cost of duplication” if it sends public records via e-mail, agency did not identify any actual costs of duplication involved in forwarding copies of electronic mail in lieu of photocopying and “the definition [of actual cost of duplication] does not allow for the imposition of labor costs or associated overhead costs”).
FL.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 185, 188, citing Yanke v. State, 588 So. 2d 4 (Fla. 2d DCA 1991); AGO 13-03
FL.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
FL.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
FL.notes: Postage: statute silent; only Yanke (prisoner context) supports a postage charge — verify. E-mail: AGO 13-03 (City of Miami Gardens) — actual cost of duplication only, and none was identified for e-mail. Verbatim from Manual; AGO 13-03 itself could not be opened (myfloridalegal.com 403).

FL.legal_concept: 'Extensive' is undefined; special service charge may not be routinely imposed; agencies encouraged to adopt a written procedure
FL.atomic_rule: The statute does not define 'extensive'; the special service charge may be imposed only where the nature or volume of the request requires extensive IT resources or clerical/supervisory assistance, decided case by case and not routinely; the charge must be reasonable; the AG strongly encourages agencies to adopt a public-records procedure addressing imposition of the charge (a DOC rule defining 'extensive' as more than 15 minutes was upheld).
FL.trigger: Agency considers imposing the s. 119.07(4)(d) special service charge
FL.source_language: Section 119.07(4)(d), F.S., “does not identify the Legislature’s intent as to what may constitute ‘extensive use’ and provides no definition of that term.” AGO 13-03. In 1991, a divided First District Court of Appeal upheld a hearing officer’s order rejecting an inmate challenge to a Department of Corrections rule that defined “extensive” for purposes of the special service charge to mean that it would take more than 15 minutes to locate, review for confidential information, copy and refile the requested material. Florida Institutional Legal Services, Inc. v. Florida Department of Corrections, 579 So. 2d 267 (Fla. 1st DCA 1991), review denied, 592 So. 2d 680 (Fla. 1991). [...] In light of the lack of clear direction in the statute as to the meaning of the term “extensive,” the Attorney General’s Office has suggested that agencies implement the service charge authorization “in a manner that reflects the purpose and intent of the Public Records Act and that does not constitute an unreasonable infringement upon the public’s statutory and constitutional right of access to public records.” AGO 13-03. In addition, the Attorney General’s Office also strongly encourages agencies to adopt a public records procedure that addresses imposition of special service charge. Id. Moreover, the statute mandates that the special service charge be “reasonable.” See Carden v. Chief of Police, 696 So. 2d 772, 773 (Fla. 2d DCA 1996), in which the court reviewed a challenge to a service charge that exceeded $4,000 for staff time involved in responding to a public records request, and said that an “excessive charge could well serve to inhibit the pursuit of rights conferred by the Public Records Act.” || Section 119.07(4)(d), F.S., however, authorizes the imposition of a special service charge when the nature or volume of public records to be inspected is such as to require extensive use of information technology resources, or extensive clerical or supervisory assistance, or both. The charge must be reasonable and based on the labor or computer costs actually incurred by the agency. See Board of County Commissioners of Highlands County v. Colby, 976 So. 2d 31 (Fla. 2d DCA 2008) (special service charge applies to requests for both inspection and copies of public records when extensive clerical assistance is required). In addition, an agency may adopt a policy imposing a reasonable special service charge based on the actual labor cost for clerical personnel who are required, due to the nature or volume of a public records request, to safeguard such records from loss or destruction during their inspection. AGO 00-11. [...] A determination of whether the nature or volume of the public records requires such extensive assistance must be made on a case-by-case basis; the special service charge may not be routinely imposed. Id.
FL.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 184-186, citing AGO 13-03; AGO 00-11; Florida Institutional Legal Services, Inc. v. DOC, 579 So. 2d 267 (Fla. 1st DCA 1991); Carden v. Chief of Police, 696 So. 2d 772 (Fla. 2d DCA 1996); Bd. of Trustees, Jacksonville Police & Fire Pension Fund v. Lee, 189 So. 3d 120 (Fla. 2016)
FL.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
FL.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
FL.notes: This is the labor 'billable-when' gate for Florida: labor below 'extensive' is not chargeable at all; the threshold is a soft standard the city defines in its own procedure (state agencies have used >15 minutes — FL-9002; not binding on cities). Verbatim from Manual.

FL.legal_concept: Only statutorily authorized fees may be imposed; inspection is free; furnishing records is not revenue-generating
FL.atomic_rule: Public records must be open for inspection without charge unless expressly provided by law, and only those fees or charges authorized by statute may be imposed on a person seeking access; furnishing records is not a profit-making or revenue-generating operation.
FL.trigger: Agency sets or imposes any charge for access to or copies of public records
FL.source_language: Providing access to public records is a statutory duty imposed by the Legislature upon all record custodians and should not be considered a profit-making or revenue-generating operation. AGO 85-03. Thus, public information must be open for inspection without charge unless otherwise expressly provided by law. See State ex rel. Davis v. McMillan, 38 So. 666 (Fla. 1905). See also AGOs 84-03 and 76-34 (only those fees or charges which are authorized by statute may be imposed upon an individual seeking access to public records).
FL.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 184, citing AGO 85-03; State ex rel. Davis v. McMillan, 38 So. 666 (Fla. 1905); AGO 84-03; AGO 76-34
FL.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
FL.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
FL.notes: Request-level ceiling in Florida is the statutory schedule itself: no charge beyond s. 119.07(4) (or another fee 'prescribed by law'); municipal ordinances cannot add fees (AGO 89-93 city growth-management book). Verbatim from Manual; AGOs not opened.

FL.legal_concept: Requester need not state a purpose; motive is irrelevant
FL.atomic_rule: The requester is not required to explain the purpose or reason for a public records request; the motivation of the person seeking records does not affect the right of access.
FL.source_language: The requester is not required to explain the purpose or reason for a public records request. “The motivation of the person seeking the records does not impact the person’s right to see them under the Public Records Act.” Curry v. State, 811 So. 2d 736, 742 (Fla. 4th DCA 2002). See also Barfield v. School Board of Manatee County, 135 So. 3d 560, 562 (Fla. 2d DCA 2014) (“An individual’s reason for requesting a public record is irrelevant”); Timoney v. City of Miami Civilian Investigative Panel, 917 So. 2d 885, 886n.3 (Fla. 3d DCA 2005) (“generally, a person’s motive in seeking access to public records is irrelevant”).
FL.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 164, citing Curry v. State, 811 So. 2d 736 (Fla. 4th DCA 2002); Barfield v. School Board of Manatee County, 135 So. 3d 560 (Fla. 2d DCA 2014); Timoney v. City of Miami Civilian Investigative Panel, 917 So. 2d 885 (Fla. 3d DCA 2005)
FL.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
FL.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
FL.notes: Bears on the commercial-purpose item: with purpose immaterial and fees limited to statute (FL-9013), a commercial-purpose fee schedule has no footing under ch. 119. Shared universal-access key per V2 discipline. Verbatim from Manual.

GA.legal_concept: Copy charge capped at 10 cents per page (letter/legal); other sizes at actual cost
GA.atomic_rule: An agency may charge a copying fee not to exceed 10 cents per page for letter or legal size documents or, for other documents, the actual cost of producing the copy.
GA.source_language: In addition to a charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records, an agency may charge a fee for the copying of records or data, not to exceed 10¢ per page for letter or legal size documents or, in the case of other documents, the actual cost of producing the copy.
GA.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
GA.notes: AMENDS GA-0018: rule_type corrected from Requirement to Permission (operative verb 'may charge ... not to exceed'); notes cleaned of the stray '$0.25' remark. Substance unchanged: ceiling $0.10/page letter/legal; actual cost for other document sizes. Confirmed unamended through the 2026 session via Legislative Counsel summaries.

GA.legal_concept: ORA procedures and fees do not apply to investigative requests from grand juries, taxing authorities, law enforcement or prosecutors
GA.atomic_rule: The ORA's procedures and fees do not apply to public records requested in writing by a state or federal grand jury, taxing authority, law enforcement agency, or prosecuting attorney in conjunction with an ongoing administrative, criminal, or tax investigation; the custodian shall provide copies to the requesting agency unless privileged or restricted by law.
GA.trigger: Written request from a grand jury, taxing authority, law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney in conjunction with an ongoing administrative, criminal or tax investigation
GA.source_language: The procedures and fees provided for in this article shall not apply to public records, including records that are exempt from disclosure pursuant to Code Section 50-18-72, which are requested in writing by a state or federal grand jury, taxing authority, law enforcement agency, or prosecuting attorney in conjunction with an ongoing administrative, criminal, or tax investigation. The lawful custodian shall provide copies of such records to the requesting agency unless such records are privileged or disclosure to such agencies is specifically restricted by law.
GA.effective_status: Current (enacted Ga. L. 1999, p. 809; amended Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); no 2024–2026 amendment)
GA.notes: Mandatory no-fee (and no-ORA-procedure) category for a class of governmental requesters; routes such requests out of the fee engine entirely. Text opened in the AG-hosted Sunshine Laws guide appendix (statute reproduction) and cross-checked against the 2024–2026 Legislative Counsel summaries.

GA.legal_concept: No fee for mere inspection of routinely-inspectable records
GA.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged when a person seeks only to inspect records that are routinely subject to public inspection (e.g., deeds, city ordinances, zoning maps).
GA.trigger: Requester seeks only to inspect a record routinely subject to public inspection
GA.source_language: The Georgia Supreme Court has held that no fee may be charged when a person seeks only to inspect records that are routinely subject to public inspection, such as deeds, city ordinances and zoning maps.
GA.source_authority: AG/GFAF 'Sunshine Laws: A Guide to Open Government in Georgia' (6th ed., June 2019) p. 5, restating McFrugal Rental of Riverdale v. Garr, 262 Ga. 369 (1992)
GA.notes: Guidance restating a Georgia Supreme Court holding; the opinion itself was not opened. Guide is published by the Georgia First Amendment Foundation 'in cooperation with' and hosted by the Office of the Attorney General. Human legal review recommended before treating as a hard gate.

GA.legal_concept: No charge for attorney time spent advising whether records should be disclosed
GA.atomic_rule: An agency may not charge for time its attorneys spend advising whether records should be disclosed.
GA.trigger: Legal review of disclosability performed by agency attorneys
GA.source_language: An agency also may not charge for time its attorneys spend advising whether records should be disclosed.
GA.source_authority: AG/GFAF 'Sunshine Laws: A Guide to Open Government in Georgia' (6th ed., June 2019) p. 5, restating Trammell v. Martin, 200 Ga. App. 435, 436 (1991)
GA.notes: Same provenance caveats as GA-9003. Also restated in the AG-approved LE guide (2014) Part D.2. Narrows the chargeable 'review/redaction' labor to non-attorney redaction work.

GA.legal_concept: Mailing among the reasonable administrative costs an agency may charge (guidance)
GA.atomic_rule: An agency may charge a reasonable fee for administrative costs associated with search, retrieval, redaction, review, copying, reproduction and mailing, must use the most economical means, bears the burden of demonstrating the charge meets that standard, and may waive the charge.
GA.trigger: Agency mails records to the requester
GA.source_language: An agency may charge a reasonable fee for the administrative costs associated with the search, retrieval, redaction, review, copying, reproduction and mailing of public records. However, an agency must provide copies of requested documents “in the most economical means available.” For any charge, it is the agency’s burden to demonstrate the charge meets this standard. An agency may also waive this charge.
GA.source_authority: 'Georgia Law Enforcement and the Open Records Act' (3d ed. 2014) Part D.2 'Optional charges', approved by the Georgia Department of Law et al., restating O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c)
GA.notes: Statute (c)(1) names 'production or copying costs' but not postage; 'mailing' appears only in this guidance. Addressed to law-enforcement agencies (municipal police departments included) but restates the general ORA fee provision. Guidance, not law — flag for legal review before configuring a postage charge as state-authorized.

GA.legal_concept: Agency is not required to charge and may waive any charges (guidance)
GA.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to charge for complying with an Open Records Act request and may waive any charges.
GA.trigger: Agency decides whether to assess ORA fees
GA.source_language: An agency is not required to charge for complying with an Open Records Act request and may waive any charges.
GA.source_authority: 'Georgia Law Enforcement and the Open Records Act' (3d ed. 2014) Part D.1 'Fee notification requirement', approved by the Georgia Department of Law et al., restating O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c)(1) ('may impose')
GA.notes: Statutory root is the permissive 'An agency may impose a reasonable charge' in (c)(1); no statutory waiver grounds, purpose statement, written denial or appeal exist. Discretionary waiver rests with the agency (city).

ID.legal_concept: Nonresident fee rates and schedule at agency discretion, not to exceed actual costs
ID.atomic_rule: A public agency may charge fees for labor and copying costs for requests by a person who is not a resident or an employee of a resident; the rates and schedule are at the agency's discretion as long as the fees do not exceed the agency's actual costs.
ID.trigger: Request from a person who is not a resident (Idaho Code § 74-101(15)) or an employee of a resident
ID.source_language: Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, a public agency or public official may charge fees for labor and copying costs associated with locating and copying documents requested by a person who is not a resident or an employee of a resident. The fee rates and schedule for requests made by persons who are not residents or employees of residents shall be at the discretion of the public agency or public official as long as such fees do not exceed actual costs of the public agency or public official.
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: Amends ID-0022 (which was a flagged paraphrase) with the verbatim clause. Nonresidents get no free 2-hour/100-page allotment and no lowest-paid-staff rate bound; only the actual-cost ceiling. Added by 2025 ch. 298 (H0253), eff. 7/1/2025.

ID.legal_concept: Conditions under which labor and copying fees may be established
ID.atomic_rule: A public agency may establish fees to recover actual labor and copying costs only if the request is for more than 100 pages of paper records, or includes records from which nonpublic information must be deleted, or the actual labor exceeds two person-hours.
ID.trigger: One of the three enumerated conditions is met
ID.source_language: A public agency or public official may establish fees to recover the actual labor and copying costs associated with locating and copying documents if: (i) The request is for more than one hundred (100) pages of paper records; or (ii) The request includes records from which nonpublic information must be deleted; or (iii) The actual labor associated with responding to requests for public records in compliance with the provisions of this chapter exceeds two (2) person hours.
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: Gate on chargeability at all (labor.billableWhen). Disjunctive triggers. Interplay with (10)(a) free first 2 hours/100 pages for residents is not expressly reconciled.

ID.legal_concept: Itemized statement of fees; no lump sums; nonresident fees separately identified
ID.atomic_rule: Statements of fees shall be itemized to show per-page copy costs, hourly rates of employees and attorneys involved, and actual time spent; no lump-sum costs may be assigned; if a separate nonresident fee schedule is adopted, nonresident fees shall be separately identified.
ID.trigger: A public agency states fees for a request
ID.source_language: Statements of fees by a public agency shall be itemized to show the per page costs for copies, and hourly rates of employees and attorneys involved in responding to the request, and the actual time spent on the public records request. No lump sum costs shall be assigned to any public records request. If a separate fee schedule is adopted for requests from persons who are not residents or employees of residents, the separate fees for such nonresidents shall be separately identified.
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: No dollar/hour threshold triggers the itemized statement; it applies whenever fees are stated. Nonresident-identification sentence added 2025 ch. 298.

ID.legal_concept: Attorney redaction labor rate ceilings (resident requests)
ID.atomic_rule: For a resident request requiring redactions by an agency-employed attorney, the rate charged shall be no more than the per-hour rate of the lowest paid attorney within the agency who is necessary and qualified; if the agency has no attorney on staff, no more than the usual and customary rate of the attorney retained for that purpose.
ID.trigger: Resident request; redactions performed by an attorney
ID.source_language: If a request from a resident requires redactions to be made by an attorney who is employed by the public agency, the rate charged shall be no more than the per hour rate of the lowest paid attorney within the public agency who is necessary and qualified to process the public records request. If a request from a resident is submitted to a public agency that does not have an attorney on staff, and requires redactions by an attorney, the rate shall be no more than the usual and customary rate of the attorney who is retained by the public agency for that purpose.
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: Split from ID-0020 (general lowest-paid-staff rate) so the attorney tier is its own ceiling. Nonresidents: agency discretion ≤ actual costs (ID-9001).

ID.legal_concept: Aggregation of requests segregated to avoid fees
ID.atomic_rule: A requester may not file multiple requests solely to avoid fees; when the agency reasonably believes one or more requesters is segregating a request into a series to avoid fees it may aggregate them and charge appropriate fees, may consider the time period of the requests, and shall not aggregate multiple requests on unrelated subjects from one requester.
ID.trigger: Agency reasonably believes requests are segregated to avoid fees
ID.source_language: A requester may not file multiple requests for public records solely to avoid payment of fees. When a public agency reasonably believes that one (1) or more requesters is segregating a request into a series of requests to avoid payment of fees authorized pursuant to this section, the public agency may aggregate such requests and charge the appropriate fees. The public agency may consider the time period in which the requests have been made in its determination to aggregate the related requests. A public agency shall not aggregate multiple requests on unrelated subjects from one (1) requester.
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: Secondary type: Prohibition (shall not aggregate unrelated subjects). No numeric window or threshold.

ID.legal_concept: Refund of advance payment exceeding actual costs
ID.atomic_rule: Any portion of an advance payment in excess of the actual costs of labor and copying incurred in responding to the request shall be returned to the requester.
ID.trigger: Advance payment collected; actual costs are lower
ID.source_language: Any portion of an advance payment in excess of the actual costs of labor and copying incurred by the agency in responding to the request shall be returned to the requester.
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: Companion to ID-0024. Middle sentence of (12) (crediting of receipts to the agency account) excluded as fiscal administration.

ID.legal_concept: Mandatory no-charge when a resident demonstrates the three-part public-interest/inability-to-pay test
ID.atomic_rule: The public agency shall not charge any cost or fee for copies or labor when the requester is a resident and demonstrates that the examination/copying (i) is likely to contribute significantly to the public's understanding of government operations or activities, (ii) is not primarily in the requester's individual interest (including litigation interest), and (iii) will not occur if fees are charged because the requester has insufficient financial resources.
ID.trigger: Resident requester demonstrates all three conditions
ID.source_language: The public agency shall not charge any cost or fee for copies or labor when the requester is a resident and demonstrates that the requester’s examination and/or copying of public records: (i) Is likely to contribute significantly to the public’s understanding of the operations or activities of the government; (ii) Is not primarily in the individual interest of the requester including, but not limited to, the requester’s interest in litigation in which the requester is or may become a party; and (iii) Will not occur if fees are charged because the requester has insufficient financial resources to pay such fees.
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: Amends ID-0023: full verbatim test captured; rule type is Requirement ('shall not charge'), not Discretion; resident-only since 2025 ch. 298. AG Manual (July 2026) Q16 says 'allowed to waive' and reproduces (10)(f) without 'is a resident and' — statute governs; guidance inconsistency noted.

ID.legal_concept: Computer tape/disc/microfilm duplicate fee ceiling (three enumerated components, uniform to residents)
ID.atomic_rule: For a duplicate of a computer tape, computer disc, microfilm or similar record system, the agency may charge a fee, uniform to all residents, not exceeding the sum of its direct cost of copying in that form, the standard cost (if any) of selling the same information as a publication, and its or a third party's cost of conversion to another electronic form.
ID.trigger: Request for a duplicate of computer tape/disc/microfilm or analogous record system
ID.source_language: For providing a duplicate of a computer tape, computer disc, microfilm or similar or analogous record system containing public record information, a public agency or public official may charge a fee, uniform to all residents, that does not exceed the sum of the following: 1. The agency’s direct cost of copying the information in that form; 2. The standard cost, if any, for selling the same information in the form of a publication; 3. The agency’s cost of conversion, or the cost of conversion charged by a third party, if the existing electronic record is converted to another electronic form.
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: Amends ID-0021 with the complete verbatim three-component list (ID-0021's ellipsis note asked for this).

ID.legal_concept: Additional electronic-media duplication fees for nonresidents (uniform to nonresidents)
ID.atomic_rule: A public agency may charge additional fees, uniform to all persons who are not residents, for requests involving duplication of a computer tape, computer disc, microfilm or similar record system.
ID.source_language: A public agency or public official may charge additional fees, uniform to all persons who are not residents, for requests involving duplication of a computer tape, computer disc, microfilm or similar or analogous record system containing public record information.
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: Bounded by the actual-costs ceiling of (10)(g). Added 2025 ch. 298.

ID.legal_concept: After-hours examination: reasonable compensation of custodian's representatives, funded in advance by the requester
ID.atomic_rule: If the custodian authorizes examination outside regular office or working hours, the persons designated to represent the custodian are entitled to reasonable compensation paid by the agency out of funds provided in advance by the person examining the records.
ID.trigger: Custodian authorizes examination outside regular hours
ID.source_language: In this event, the persons designated to represent the custodian during such examination shall be entitled to reasonable compensation to be paid to them by the public agency having custody of such records, out of funds provided in advance by the person examining such records, at other than regular office or working hours.
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: Advance funding is mandatory for this service once authorized; the amount is 'reasonable compensation' (soft standard). AG Manual Q15 also cites advance payment for outside copying contractors/overtime.

ID.legal_concept: Recovery of actual mailing/telecommunications costs when asked to mail or fax records (AG guidance)
ID.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to send records to a requester, but may recover actual mailing or telecommunications costs when asked to mail or fax records.
ID.trigger: Requester asks the agency to mail or fax records
ID.source_language: The law does not prevent the recovery of actual mailing or telecommunications costs if there is a request to mail or fax information to someone.
ID.source_authority: Idaho Attorney General, Idaho Public Records Law Manual (July 2026), Question No. 14
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: Guidance, not statute; Title 74 is silent on postage. Statute separately permits e-mail delivery (§ 74-102(4)). Preceding sentence of the answer: 'The law requires an agency to provide public records to members of the public; the agency is not required to send the records to the person making the request.'

ID.legal_concept: City may not by ordinance charge above actual cost of reproduction (AG Legal Guideline 1/25/1993)
ID.atomic_rule: A city may not pass an ordinance allowing it to charge a fee in excess of the actual cost of reproducing requested public records, notwithstanding the 'otherwise provided by law' language.
ID.source_language: Attorney General’s Legal Guideline, January 25, 1993 (city may not pass ordinance to allow it to charge a fee in excess of actual cost of reproducing requested public records despite the “otherwise provided by law” language of Idaho Code § 9-338(8)).
ID.source_authority: Attorney General’s Legal Guideline, January 25, 1993, as indexed in the Idaho Public Records Law Manual (July 2026), p. 69
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: The guideline itself was not opened; the source language is the manual's own summary (verbatim from the manual). Issued under former § 9-338(8), predecessor of § 74-102(10)(c). Municipal-specific.

ID.legal_concept: Fees authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law are preserved
ID.atomic_rule: The free-allotment rule and the actual-cost copying ceiling apply 'except for fees that are authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law' / 'if another fee is not otherwise provided by law'.
ID.trigger: Another Idaho statute prescribes a fee for the record (e.g. recorder, court records)
ID.source_language: Except for fees that are authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law, no fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a request submitted by a resident for public records, or for copying the first one hundred (100) pages of paper records that are requested by a resident. | A public agency or public official may establish separate copying fee schedules for requests submitted by residents and requests submitted by persons who are not residents. The fee for residents may not exceed the actual cost to the agency of copying the record if another fee is not otherwise provided by law.
ID.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
ID.notes: AG Manual Q13: exception 'preserve[s] fees already established by other laws, such as recorders’ fees and fees for court records.' No general municipal certified-copy or records fee statute found in Title 50; per AG Guideline 1993 (ID-9012) a city ordinance is not 'other law' for this purpose.

IL.legal_concept: Actual-cost reimbursement standard for reproduction and certification
IL.atomic_rule: Except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute, a public body may charge fees reasonably calculated to reimburse its actual cost for reproducing and certifying public records and for the use of its equipment to copy records; that actual cost may not include search, review or other personnel costs except for commercial requests under Sec. 6(f).
IL.trigger: Public body charges a fee for reproducing or certifying records
IL.source_language: Except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute, each public body may charge fees reasonably calculated to reimburse its actual cost for reproducing and certifying public records and for the use, by any person, of the equipment of the public body to copy records. In calculating its actual cost for reproducing records or for the use of the equipment of the public body to reproduce records, a public body shall not include the costs of any search for and review of the records or other personnel costs associated with reproducing the records, except for commercial requests as provided in subsection (f) of this Section.
IL.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
IL.notes: Soft-standard outer ceiling ('reasonably calculated to reimburse its actual cost'); the numeric per-band caps (15 cents, $1) sit inside it. 'Except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute' preserves record-specific statutory fees (e.g., 625 ILCS 5/11-416 crash reports, IL-9010).

IL.legal_concept: Standard scale of fees, established and made public
IL.atomic_rule: Fees under Sec. 6(b) must be imposed according to a standard scale of fees established and made public by the public body imposing them, and the public body must prominently display on its website (and post at its offices if it has no website) any fees allowable under Section 6.
IL.source_language: Such fees shall be imposed according to a standard scale of fees, established and made public by the body imposing them. (b) A brief description of the methods whereby the public may request information and public records, a directory designating the Freedom of Information officer or officers, the address where requests for public records should be directed, and any fees allowable under Section 6 of this Act.
IL.effective_status: Current (Sec. 6 P.A. 98-1129 eff. 12-3-14; Sec. 4 last amended P.A. 104-438 eff. 1-1-26 — quoted clause unchanged)
IL.notes: The city (governing body) is the fee-setting authority within the state's ceilings; the Act delegates the operative amounts to the public body's published scale. Non-compliant fee = denial (IL-9004).

IL.legal_concept: Fee estimate required in commercial / recurrent / voluminous responses
IL.atomic_rule: For a commercial-purpose request (21 working days), a recurrent-requester request (21 business days) or a voluminous request (final response under Sec. 3.6(c)), the public body's response, if it does not deny or produce, must provide an estimate of the fees to be charged (and, for commercial and recurrent, of the time required), which it may require the requester to pay in full before copying.
IL.trigger: Request classified as commercial-purpose, recurrent-requester or voluminous
IL.source_language: The response shall (i) provide to the requester an estimate of the time required by the public body to provide the records requested and an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents, (ii) deny the request pursuant to one or more of the exemptions set out in this Act, (iii) notify the requester that the request is unduly burdensome and extend an opportunity to the requester to attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions, or (iv) provide the records requested. [Sec. 3.6(c):] The response shall: (i) provide an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents; (ii) deny the request pursuant to one or more of the exemptions set out in this Act; (iii) notify the requester that the request is unduly burdensome and extend an opportunity to the requester to attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions; or (iv) provide the records requested.
IL.notes: No dollar/hour threshold anywhere in the Act; the estimate duty is class-based. Ordinary requests carry no estimate duty. Full-prepayment permission is IL-0019.

IL.legal_concept: Fee inconsistent with Sec. 6(a)/(b) is a denial
IL.atomic_rule: The imposition of a fee not consistent with Sec. 6(a) and (b) constitutes a denial of access to public records for purposes of judicial review.
IL.trigger: Public body imposes a fee inconsistent with Sec. 6(a) or 6(b)
IL.source_language: The imposition of a fee not consistent with subsections (6)(a) and (b) of this Act constitutes a denial of access to public records for the purposes of judicial review.
IL.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
IL.notes: Trigger for the appeal path (court under Sec. 11; PAC request for review under Sec. 9.5 — PAC binding opinions 25-014/25-015 reviewed fee assessments as denials). Names only 6(a) and (b), not the 6(c) waiver.

IL.legal_concept: Voluminous-request fee is a debt due and owing
IL.atomic_rule: If a requester does not pay a Sec. 6 fee charged for a voluminous request, the debt is a debt due and owing to the public body collectible under applicable law, and the fee may be charged even if the requester fails to accept or collect the prepared records; the Sec. 3.6(a) voluminous notice must warn the requester of this.
IL.trigger: Voluminous request; fee charged under Sec. 6 unpaid or records not collected
IL.source_language: If a requester does not pay a fee charged pursuant to Section 6 of this Act for a voluminous request, the debt shall be considered a debt due and owing to the public body and may be collected in accordance with applicable law. This fee may be charged by the public body even if the requester fails to accept or collect records the public body has prepared in response to a voluminous request.
IL.notes: Only nonpayment consequence in the Act; no withdrawal clock, no prior-debt prepayment rule; silent for non-voluminous requests.

IL.legal_concept: Off-site storage retrieval/transport cost (commercial requests only)
IL.atomic_rule: On a commercial-purpose request, a public body may charge the actual cost of retrieving and transporting public records from an off-site storage facility when the records are maintained by a third-party storage company under contract with the public body.
IL.trigger: Commercial-purpose request; responsive records held off-site by a contracted third-party storage company
IL.source_language: A public body may charge the actual cost of retrieving and transporting public records from an off-site storage facility when the public records are maintained by a third-party storage company under contract with the public body. The provisions of this subsection (f) apply only to commercial requests.
IL.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
IL.notes: Actual cost, no number. Commercial only. Accounting of all fees/costs/hours required when any 6(f) fee is imposed (IL-0037).

IL.atomic_rule: A public body that fails to respond to a request within the Sec. 3 response period (or within the time permitted for an extension) but thereafter provides copies may not impose a fee for those copies, and may not treat the request as unduly burdensome.
IL.trigger: Public body misses the Sec. 3(d) 5-business-day deadline or the Sec. 3(e)/(f) extended deadline and later provides copies
IL.source_language: A public body that fails to respond to a request within the requisite periods in this Section but thereafter provides the requester with copies of the requested public records may not impose a fee for such copies. A public body that fails to respond to a request within the time permitted for extension but thereafter provides the requester with copies of the requested public records may not impose a fee for those copies.
IL.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/3 last amended by P.A. 104-438, eff. 1-1-26; the quoted clause is unchanged by that Act)
IL.notes: Sec. 3(i) removes commercial, recurrent and voluminous requests from the Sec. 3 time periods, so the forfeiture does not reach them (AG FAQ 10/2023 agrees). Fixed statutory consequence; the city cannot charge around it.

IL.legal_concept: Repeated identical requests deemed unduly burdensome
IL.atomic_rule: Repeated requests from the same person for the same records that are unchanged or identical to records previously provided or properly denied are deemed unduly burdensome under Sec. 3(g), permitting denial after the conferral step.
IL.trigger: Same requester re-requests records previously provided or properly denied, unchanged
IL.source_language: Repeated requests from the same person for the same records that are unchanged or identical to records previously provided or properly denied under this Act shall be deemed unduly burdensome under this provision.
IL.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/3 last amended by P.A. 104-438, eff. 1-1-26; the quoted clause is unchanged by that Act)
IL.notes: Structural repeat-request rule; no fee carry-forward. Aggregation into 'voluminous' (2(h), >5 categories/20 business days or >500 pages) and 'recurrent requester' (2(g)) are classification rules already in IL-0022/IL-0023.

IL.legal_concept: Traffic crash report copy fee (local law enforcement)
IL.atomic_rule: A law enforcement agency of a local authority may furnish copies of traffic crash reports it prepared and may receive a fee not to exceed $5 per copy, or not to exceed $20 for a crash investigated by a crash reconstruction officer or team.
IL.trigger: Request for a copy of a traffic crash report prepared by the municipal police
IL.source_language: Other State law enforcement agencies or law enforcement agencies of local authorities may furnish copies of traffic crash reports prepared by such agencies and may receive a fee not to exceed $5 for each copy or in the case of a crash which was investigated by a crash reconstruction officer or crash reconstruction team, the State or local law enforcement agency may receive a fee not to exceed $20.
IL.notes: A 'fee otherwise fixed by statute' under 5 ILCS 140/6(b); the AG PAC webinar (4/10/2025) cites it as the example of a statutory fee chargeable instead of the Sec. 6(b) fee. Ceiling; city sets ≤ $5 / ≤ $20. Applies to municipal police (local authorities) as well as State agencies.

IL.legal_concept: Electronic records: fee limited to recording medium; no redaction-cost recovery (PAC binding opinion 25-014)
IL.atomic_rule: For records maintained in electronic format (there, police body-camera video), Sec. 6(a) limits the copying fee to the actual cost of the recording medium; a public body may not charge to recover the cost of redaction software or per-minute redaction work, and Sec. 6(b)'s actual-cost clause for color/nonstandard paper copies does not apply to video.
IL.trigger: Requester seeks copies of electronically maintained records requiring redaction
IL.source_language: 11) Because the Department maintains the requested video footage in electronic format, section 6(a) of FOIA limits the copying fee to the actual cost of the recording medium. [Reasoning:] If the General Assembly had intended to allow a public body to charge fees to reimburse the actual cost it incurred to make redactions to copies of records in electronic format, it would have expressly authorized such a fee in section 6(a) of FOIA.
IL.source_authority: Ill. Att'y Gen. Pub. Acc. Op. No. 25-014 (Dec. 3, 2025), citing Sage Information Services v. Humm, 2012 IL App (5th) 110580, ¶18 and Sage Information Services v. Suhr, 2014 IL App (2d) 130708, ¶¶14-15
IL.effective_status: Current (binding opinion issued Dec. 3, 2025; final administrative decision reviewable under 5 ILCS 140/11.5)
IL.notes: Binding on the parties; the PAC applies it generally. Cited appellate holdings: 'the current version of section 6 of the FOIA does not allow a fee in excess of the cost of the electronic medium for the reproduction of electronic records' (Humm) and a non-FOIA statute's fee applies to electronic records only if it expressly says so (Suhr).

IL.legal_concept: Driver's-record abstract fee delegated to Vehicle Code (Secretary of State)
IL.atomic_rule: The fee for each abstract of a driver's record is as provided in 625 ILCS 5/6-118, whether furnished on paper or electronically; 6-118(a-5) fixes the fee for a driver's record or data contained therein at $20.
IL.trigger: Request for an abstract of a driver's record
IL.source_language: The fee for each abstract of a driver's record shall be as provided in Section 6-118 of "The Illinois Vehicle Code", approved September 29, 1969, as amended, whether furnished as a paper copy or as an electronic copy. [625 ILCS 5/6-118:] (a-5) The fee for a driver's record or data contained therein is $20 and shall be disbursed as set forth in subsection (k) of Section 2-123 of this Code.
IL.effective_status: Current (625 ILCS 5/6-118 last amended P.A. 104-435, eff. 11-21-25)
IL.notes: Delegation followed for completeness: driver's-record abstracts are held by the Secretary of State; the figure binds that State office, not municipalities (applies_to state_agencies_only).

IL.legal_concept: Paper-copy fees inapplicable to records furnished electronically
IL.atomic_rule: Except to the extent the General Assembly expressly provides, statutory fees applicable to paper copies (including the 15-cent page fee) do not apply to records furnished in electronic format; only the recording-medium cost may be charged, so records delivered by e-mail or portal carry no copy fee.
IL.trigger: Records furnished to the requester in electronic format
IL.source_language: Except to the extent that the General Assembly expressly provides, statutory fees applicable to copies of public records when furnished in a paper format shall not be applicable to those records when furnished in an electronic format. A public body may charge the requester for the actual cost of purchasing the recording medium, whether disc, diskette, tape, or other medium.
IL.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
IL.notes: PAC binding opinion 25-015 (Dec. 23, 2025): a body that maintains records only on paper may charge 15 cents/page for the paper copies even if it chooses to e-mail some of them, but a body that creates electronic copies is limited to the electronic-record fees. Confirms 'delivery: email' = no charge.

IN.legal_concept: No fee to inspect; no fee to search for, examine, or review a record to determine disclosability
IN.atomic_rule: Except as provided in § 8, a public agency may not charge any fee under APRA to inspect a public record or to search for, examine, or review a record to determine whether it may be disclosed.
IN.trigger: Any request; exceptions only where § 8 itself authorizes a fee (e.g., § 8(m) schools; § 8(n) non-resident supplemental fee)
IN.source_language: Except as provided in this section, a public agency may not charge any fee under this chapter: (1) to inspect a public record; or (2) to search for, examine, or review a record to determine whether the record may be disclosed.
IN.source_authority: Ind. Code § 5-14-3-8(b)(1), (3) (subdivision (2) at time of the handbook text)
IN.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff. July 1, 2026) added (n)-(o) without altering this text per PAC's Statutory Additions summary. Codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: Text opened in PAC Handbook (rev. Mar. 2022) p. 52. Current codified text renumbers the search/review item as (b)(3) prefaced 'Subject to subdivision (2)' (school search fee) — numbering not verified at iga.in.gov (site inaccessible). Applies to all public agencies.

IN.legal_concept: No fee for an electronic copy provided by electronic mail
IN.atomic_rule: A public agency may not charge any fee under APRA to provide an electronic copy of a public record by electronic mail (subject to the subsection's enumerated exceptions).
IN.trigger: Requester receives an electronic copy by e-mail
IN.source_language: …a public agency may not charge any fee under this chapter for the following: … (4) To provide an electronic copy of a public record by electronic mail.
IN.effective_status: Current (quoted by the PAC in 22-FC-53, 2022; present in codified text as of Jan. 1, 2026 per secondary check) — codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19)
IN.notes: Verbatim clause opened in PAC advisory opinion 22-FC-53. Exception sentence (paraphrase, unverified in an official copy): a fee may still be charged for a record transmitted by e-mail if authorized under § 8(f) or (j), § 6(c), or IC 36-2-7-10/-10.1 (county recorder).
