Not in the 2022 handbook copy (stale). Manual verification of the exception text required.

IN.legal_concept: Advance payment of search and copying costs may be required
IN.atomic_rule: A public agency may require that the payment for search and copying costs be made in advance.
IN.source_language: A public agency may require that the payment for search and copying costs be made in advance.
IN.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff. July 1, 2026) added (n)-(o) without altering this text per PAC's Statutory Additions summary. Codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: Verbatim as quoted by the PAC in 25-FC-326 (July 21, 2026). Older text (2022 handbook; also quoted in 25-FC-121) reads 'payment for copying costs' — the words 'search and' appear in the current version; confirm at iga.in.gov. No threshold, no percentage. Inspection may never be conditioned on a fee (IN-9001).

IN.legal_concept: Local fee schedule set by fiscal body; certification ≤ $5/document; copies ≤ greater of $0.10 (non-color)/$0.25 (color) per page or actual cost; uniformity
IN.atomic_rule: For a public agency that is not a state agency, the fiscal body (or governing body if none) shall establish by schedule the certification and copying fees; certification may not exceed $5 per document; copying may not exceed the greater of $0.10 per non-color page / $0.25 per color page or the agency's actual cost (paper + per-page equipment cost, excluding labor and overhead); the fee must be uniform throughout the agency and to all purchasers.
IN.trigger: Local public agency charges for certification or paper copies
IN.source_language: This subsection applies to a public agency that is not a state agency. The fiscal body (as defined in IC 36-1-2-6) of the public agency, or the governing body, if there is no fiscal body, shall establish a fee schedule for the certification or copying of documents. The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document. The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of: (1) ten cents ($0.10) per page for copies that are not color copies or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for color copies; or (2) the actual cost to the agency of copying the document. As used in this subsection, "actual cost" means the cost of paper and the per-page cost for use of copying or facsimile equipment and does not include labor costs or overhead costs. A fee established under this subsection must be uniform throughout the public agency and uniform to all purchasers.
IN.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff. July 1, 2026) added (n)-(o) without altering this text per PAC's Statutory Additions summary. Codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: Supersedes IN-0019 (paraphrase) with the verbatim subsection; corrects IN-0016's citation ($5 certification ceiling for local agencies is § 8(d), not (b)). Opened in PAC opinion 25-FC-326 and PAC Handbook p. 52; identical in 19-FC-67. Ceilings: fiscal body supplies operative values.

IN.legal_concept: Fee ceiling for duplicates of electronic media, microfilm and law-enforcement recordings — direct cost; LE recording copy ≤ $150
IN.atomic_rule: For a duplicate of a computer tape, computer disc, microfilm, law enforcement recording or analogous record system, a public agency may charge a fee, uniform to all purchasers, not exceeding the sum of its direct cost of supplying the information in that form (a law-enforcement-recording copy may not exceed $150) plus the standard price of any published version.
IN.trigger: Requester obtains a duplicate on electronic media/microfilm or a copy of a law enforcement recording
IN.source_language: Except as provided by subsection (h), for providing a duplicate of a computer tape, computer disc, microfilm, law enforcement recording, or similar or analogous record system containing information owned by the public agency or entrusted to it, a public agency may charge a fee, uniform to all purchasers, that does not exceed the sum of the following: (1) The agency's direct cost of supplying the information in that form. However, the fee for a copy of a law enforcement recording may not exceed one hundred fifty dollars ($150). (2) The standard cost for selling the same information to the public in the form of a publication if the agency has published the information and made the publication available for sale. (3) In the case of the legislative services agency, a reasonable percentage of the agency's direct cost of maintaining the system in which the information is stored. However, the amount charged by the legislative services agency under this subdivision may not exceed the sum of the amounts it may charge under subdivisions (1) and (2).
IN.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff. July 1, 2026) added (n)-(o) without altering this text per PAC's Statutory Additions summary. Codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: Opened in PAC Handbook p. 52-53; (g)(1) quoted verbatim in PAC 21-FC-131, 25-FC-121, 25-FC-152, 25-FC-221 (2021–2026). $150 is a ceiling not a floor (21-FC-131). Fees for LE recordings may be retained locally without appropriation (§ 8(l)).

IN.legal_concept: Definition of 'direct cost' — 105% of program development + retrieval labor + output medium
IN.atomic_rule: 'Direct cost' for § 8(g) electronic duplicates and § 6(c) reprogramming means 105% of the sum of the cost of initial program development (if any), the labor required to retrieve electronically stored data, and any medium used for electronic output.
IN.source_language: "Direct cost" means one hundred five percent (105%) of the sum of the cost of: (1) the initial development of a program, if any; (2) the labor required to retrieve electronically stored data; and (3) any medium used for electronic output; for providing a duplicate of electronically stored data onto a disk, tape, drum, or other medium of electronic data retrieval under section 8(g) of this chapter, or for reprogramming a computer system under section 6(c) of this chapter.
IN.source_authority: Ind. Code § 5-14-3-2 (definition of 'direct cost'; lettered (d) in the 2022 handbook copy)
IN.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff. July 1, 2026) added (n)-(o) without altering this text per PAC's Statutory Additions summary. Codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: Fixed 5% uplift is the only overhead-type figure in Indiana public-records fee law. HEA 1360 (2026) added definitions to § 5-14-3-2 ('data scraping' (d), 'phishing' (p)), so the letter of this definition has shifted — verify.

IN.legal_concept: Supplemental fee for requests from non-Indiana residents / out-of-state entities — ceiling $0.25 per page and $25 per hour of staff time
IN.atomic_rule: A public agency may collect a supplemental fee for processing public records requests submitted by non-Indiana residents or out-of-state entities; the fee must be reasonably related to the cost of fulfilling the request and may not exceed $0.25 per page and $25 per hour of staff time spent processing the request.
IN.trigger: Requester is a non-Indiana resident or out-of-state entity (or, per § 8.1(b), request originates from an out-of-state entity or automated system)
IN.source_language: (n) Except as provided in subsection (o), a public agency may collect a supplemental fee for processing public records requests submitted by non-Indiana residents or out-of-state entities. The fee: (1) must be reasonably related to the cost of fulfilling the request; and (2) may not exceed twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page and twenty-five dollars ($25) per hour of staff time spent processing the request.
IN.effective_status: Effective July 1, 2026 (HEA 1360, P.L. 97-2026, signed March 4, 2026) — text opened in the PAC's official 'Statutory Additions under HEA 1360' document; codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: Verbatim from the PAC's official 'Statutory Additions under HEA 1360'. PAC Overview adds: 'If adopted, agencies must apply the fee consistently to all out-of-state and automated requests.' This is the only provision under which a municipality may charge staff time on an ordinary request. Proposed concept key: fee.nonresident_surcharge.

IN.legal_concept: Public-interest waiver of the non-resident supplemental fee
IN.atomic_rule: A public agency may waive the § 8(n) supplemental fee if it finds that the public records request serves the public interest.
IN.trigger: Agency has imposed or would impose the § 8(n) fee
IN.source_language: (o) A public agency may waive the fee under subsection (n) if the public agency finds that the public records request serves the public interest.
IN.effective_status: Effective July 1, 2026 (HEA 1360, P.L. 97-2026, signed March 4, 2026) — text opened in the PAC's official 'Statutory Additions under HEA 1360' document; codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: Discretionary; no written-denial or appeal procedure specified.

IN.legal_concept: Fees specified by other statute or court order must be collected
IN.atomic_rule: Notwithstanding § 8(b)–(d) and (g)–(i), a public agency shall collect any certification, copying, facsimile machine transmission, or search fee that is specified by statute or is ordered by a court.
IN.trigger: Another statute or a court order specifies a fee for the record
IN.source_language: Notwithstanding subsection (b), (c), (d), (g), (h), or (i), a public agency shall collect any certification, copying, facsimile machine transmission, or search fee that is specified by statute or is ordered by a court.
IN.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff. July 1, 2026) added (n)-(o) without altering this text per PAC's Statutory Additions summary. Codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: Record-specific statutory fees (e.g., county recorder IC 36-2-7-10) override APRA ceilings and the e-mail no-fee rule.

IN.legal_concept: Electronic map fee — reasonable percentage of direct cost of maintaining/upgrading/enhancing plus direct cost of supplying; fiscal-body approval
IN.atomic_rule: A public agency may charge a fee, uniform to all purchasers, for an electronic map based on a reasonable percentage of its direct cost of maintaining, upgrading and enhancing the map plus the direct cost of supplying it in the requested form; within a political subdivision having a fiscal body the fee is subject to that body's approval.
IN.trigger: Request is for an electronic map (GIS data)
IN.source_language: Except as provided in subsection (k), a public agency may charge a fee, uniform to all purchasers, for providing an electronic map that is based upon a reasonable percentage of the agency's direct cost of maintaining, upgrading, and enhancing the electronic map and for the direct cost of supplying the electronic map in the form requested by the purchaser. If the public agency is within a political subdivision having a fiscal body, the fee is subject to the approval of the fiscal body of the political subdivision.
IN.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff. July 1, 2026) added (n)-(o) without altering this text per PAC's Statutory Additions summary. Codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: Amends IN-0017: the electronic-map fee is § 8(j) (not (g)) and includes the fiscal-body approval gate. PAC 25-FC-145 (2025) applied it to a $750 commercial GIS user fee.

IN.legal_concept: Electronic-map maintenance fee waivable for noncommercial use
IN.atomic_rule: The § 8(j) maintenance/upgrade/enhancement component of an electronic-map fee may be waived if the map will be used for a noncommercial purpose, including public agency program support, nonprofit activities, journalism, or academic research.
IN.trigger: Electronic-map request for a noncommercial purpose
IN.source_language: The fee charged by a public agency under subsection (j) to cover costs for maintaining, upgrading, and enhancing an electronic map may be waived by the public agency if the electronic map for which the fee is charged will be used for a noncommercial purpose, including the following: (1) Public agency program support. (2) Nonprofit activities. (3) Journalism. (4) Academic research.
IN.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff. July 1, 2026) added (n)-(o) without altering this text per PAC's Statutory Additions summary. Codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).

IN.legal_concept: Ordinance may condition commercial use of data received on disk or tape
IN.atomic_rule: A political subdivision may enact an ordinance prescribing the conditions under which a person who receives information on disk or tape under § 3(d) may or may not use it for commercial purposes; news, nonprofit and academic uses are not prohibited; a violator may be barred from obtaining further data.
IN.trigger: Electronic data provided on disk/tape under § 3(d)
IN.source_language: A state agency may adopt a rule under IC 4-22-2, and a political subdivision may enact an ordinance, prescribing the conditions under which a person who receives information on disk or tape under subsection (d) may or may not use the information for commercial purposes, including to sell, advertise, or solicit the purchase of merchandise, goods, or services, or sell, loan, give away, or otherwise deliver the information obtained by the request to any other person for these purposes. Use of information received under subsection (d) in connection with the preparation or publication of news, for nonprofit activities, or for academic research is not prohibited. A person who uses information in a manner contrary to a rule or ordinance adopted under this subsection may be prohibited by the state agency or political subdivision from obtaining a copy or any further data under subsection (d).
IN.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff. July 1, 2026) added (n)-(o) without altering this text per PAC's Statutory Additions summary. Codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: Use-restriction power, not a fee schedule; Indiana has no commercial-purpose fee surcharge.

IN.legal_concept: State-agency uniform copying fee set by the Indiana Department of Administration
IN.atomic_rule: The Indiana Department of Administration shall establish a uniform per-page copying fee for standard-sized documents copied by state agencies, not exceeding the greater of the average cost of copying or $0.10 per page; a state agency may not collect more than that fee, and shall set a reasonable fee for nonstandard-sized documents.
IN.source_language: The Indiana department of administration shall establish a uniform copying fee for the copying of one (1) page of a standard-sized document by state agencies. The fee may not exceed the average cost of copying records by state agencies or ten cents ($0.10) per page, whichever is greater. A state agency may not collect more than the uniform copying fee for providing a copy of a public record. However, a state agency shall establish and collect a reasonable fee for copying nonstandard-sized documents.
IN.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff. July 1, 2026) added (n)-(o) without altering this text per PAC's Statutory Additions summary. Codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY — does not bind municipalities. Delegation followed: no published IDOA instrument (rule, memo or schedule) stating the current uniform fee was found on in.gov/idoa or in PAC materials; agency guides (e.g., Treasurer of State APRA guide) state $0.10/page. Recorded as delegated_unresolved for the state-agency regime; irrelevant to the local-body regime.

IN.legal_concept: Priority for Indiana residents and civic/journalistic/academic/personal-use requests; out-of-state or automated requests may be delayed and charged the § 8(n) fee
IN.atomic_rule: A public agency may give priority to requests from Indiana residents and requests for civic, journalistic, academic or personal use; requests identified as originating from out-of-state entities or automated systems may be delayed as necessary to prevent disruption of core agency functions and subjected to the § 8(n) supplemental fee.
IN.trigger: Requester residency/purpose identified (portal or intake questions)
IN.source_language: Sec. 8.1.(a) A public agency may give priority in fulfilling public records requests to: (1) Indiana residents; and (2) requests submitted for civic, journalistic, academic, or personal use. (b) Requests identified as originating from out-of-state entities or automated systems may be: (1) delayed as necessary to prevent disruption of core agency functions; and (2) subject to a fee under section 8(n) of this chapter.
IN.effective_status: Effective July 1, 2026 (HEA 1360, P.L. 97-2026, signed March 4, 2026) — text opened in the PAC's official 'Statutory Additions under HEA 1360' document; codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
IN.notes: Structural fork: residency-based priority and fee. PAC Overview: to receive priority the requester must clearly state the purpose; § 3(a) still bars denying a request for refusing to state a purpose.

IN.legal_concept: School corporations/charter schools: electronic-record search fee after 5 free hours, ≤ lesser of searcher's hourly rate or $20/hour; actual time only; no computer processing time; no minimum; prorated
IN.atomic_rule: A school corporation or charter school may not charge for the first five hours of searching for electronic-format records; beyond five hours it may charge an hourly search fee not exceeding the lesser of the searcher's hourly rate or $20 per hour, only for time actually spent, with no charge for computer processing time, no minimum fee, and proration for partial hours.
IN.trigger: Requester to a school corporation or charter school; electronic search exceeds 5 hours (not applicable to searches requested by an exclusive representative per § 8(b)(2))
IN.source_language: This subsection applies to a school corporation and a charter school. For purposes of this subsection, "computer processing time" means the amount of time a computer takes to process a command or script to extract or copy electronically stored data that is the subject of a public records request. A school corporation or charter school may not charge a fee for the first five (5) hours required to search for records that are in an electronic format. A school corporation or charter school may charge a search fee for any time spent searching for records that are in an electronic format that exceeds five (5) hours. If the school corporation or charter school charges a search fee, the school corporation or charter school shall charge an hourly fee that does not exceed the lesser of: (1) the hourly rate of the person making the search; or (2) twenty dollars ($20) per hour. A school corporation or charter school charging an hourly fee under this subsection for searching for records that are in an electronic format may charge only for time that the person making the search actually spends in searching for the records that are in an electronic format. A school corporation or charter school may not charge for computer processing time and may not establish a minimum fee for searching for records that are in an electronic format. A school corporation or charter school shall make a good faith effort to complete a search for records that are in an electronic format that is within a reasonable time in order to minimize the amount of a search fee. The fee must be prorated to reflect any search time of less than one (1) hour.
IN.effective_status: Current (quoted by the PAC in 25-FC-483, Aug. 11, 2026); codified iga.in.gov copy not opened
IN.notes: SCHOOLS ONLY — not a municipal rule; recorded so the labor items' 'not_applicable' scope is explicit. Verbatim from PAC advisory opinion 25-FC-483 (quoted 'in relevant part').

IN.legal_concept: PAC reading of § 8(d) actual cost: labor/overhead excluded; actual-cost branch reserved for unusually sized paper and postage to remote requesters
IN.atomic_rule: Per the Public Access Counselor, the § 8(d) actual-cost branch excludes labor and overhead, is capped by the price of ink and paper, and 'comes into play only when copying unusually sized pieces of paper and postage costs to remote requesters'; standard-size copies should use the per-page rate.
IN.trigger: Local agency invokes 'actual cost' above $0.10/$0.25 per page, or mails copies
IN.source_language: Labor and overhead costs are specifically excluded from the calculation of actual cost. The price of ink and paper is the cap to actual cost. Even then, given the practical cost of printing, agencies likely come out ahead if capping copies at $.10 per page. Chesterfield's fees are not justifiable or reasonable. In reality, the actual cost calculation comes into play only when copying unusually sized pieces of paper and postage costs to remote requesters. There is no need to use the actual cost calculation with standard size copies.
IN.source_authority: Opinion of the Public Access Counselor 19-FC-67 (Town of Chesterfield); reaffirmed in 19-FC-90, 21-FC-131, 25-FC-326
IN.effective_status: Current (advisory opinion; PAC opinions are advisory, not binding)
IN.notes: Guidance, not law: supports treating postage as recoverable actual cost and rejects flat per-report fees. Verify no later PAC opinion departs.

KS.legal_concept: Reasonable fee for allowing subject persons to listen to/view body-camera or vehicle-camera recordings
KS.atomic_rule: When a person described in K.S.A. 45-254(c) (subject of the recording, parent/guardian of a minor subject, heir at law of a deceased subject, or their attorney) requests to listen to or view a body-camera or vehicle-camera recording, the law enforcement agency shall allow it within 20 days and may charge a reasonable fee for such services.
KS.trigger: Request under 45-254(b) by a person listed in 45-254(c) to listen to/view a body or vehicle camera recording
KS.clock_spec: 20 calendar-days from making the request (viewing/listening must be allowed)
KS.source_language: The law enforcement agency shall allow the person to listen to the requested audio recording or to view the requested video recording within 20 days after making the request, and may charge a reasonable fee for such services provided by the law enforcement agency.
KS.notes: Applies to every 'law enforcement agency' — municipal police included (all_public_bodies operating law enforcement). 'Reasonable fee' is a soft standard; no per-recording/per-minute figure. The recordings are criminal investigation records (45-254(a); 45-217(e)(1)); this section grants an access right and fee permission in addition to any KORA disclosure. Copies of AV items generally are not required under 45-219(a) unless shown/played at a public meeting (KS-0044).

KS.legal_concept: Executive Order 18-05 — no copy charge for first 100 pages (Kansas residents, executive-branch agencies under the Governor)
KS.atomic_rule: Executive-branch departments, agencies, boards and commissions under the jurisdiction of the Office of the Governor shall not assess any charge or fee for copying documents responsive to a KORA request made by a Kansas resident, up to and including the first 100 pages, and shall inform resident requesters of this policy in the initial response.
KS.trigger: KORA request by a resident of Kansas to an executive-branch agency under the Governor
KS.source_language: The Office of the Governor and all Executive Branch departments, agencies, boards, and commissions under the jurisdiction of the Office of the Governor shall not assess any charge or fee for the copying of documents responsive to an open records request made by any resident of Kansas under the Kansas Open Records Act, up to and including the first one hundred (100) pages of such documents. All residents of Kansas making such a request shall be informed of this policy in the initial response to their request.
KS.source_authority: Kansas Executive Order No. 18-05, 'Open Records Copy Charges' (Gov. Jeff Colyer, 2018)
KS.effective_status: Effective immediately on filing with the Secretary of State (2018); still cited as operative on admin.ks.gov (accessed 2026-08-19) — currency requires manual verification (no rescission located)
KS.notes: STATE_AGENCIES_ONLY — does not bind municipalities, counties, school districts, or non-cabinet state entities. Recorded per the run parameter to note the agency regime; for municipalities the free-page item is silent. Source type: an Executive Order (not in the V2 source-type list; nearest is Official Guidance). Signing date is in the image signature block, not the PDF text layer. Opened via the Kansas Government Information Online Library (KGI, Kansas State Library) copy of the filed order.

LA.legal_concept: Commissioner of administration adopts uniform copy-fee schedule for executive-branch state agencies
LA.atomic_rule: The commissioner of administration, with the governor's approval, shall by rule adopt a uniform fee schedule for copies of public records of executive-branch state agencies, and such copies shall be furnished at the scheduled fees except where a fee is otherwise fixed by law.
LA.trigger: Request for copies of an executive-branch state agency's public records
LA.source_language: the commissioner of administration, with the approval of the governor, shall, by rule or regulation, adopt a uniform fee schedule for copies of public records of executive branch state agencies furnished to persons so requesting by custodians thereof, as provided by R.S. 44:32.  Copies of the public record furnished to a person so requesting shall be provided at fees according to the schedule, except for copies of public records, the fees for the reproduction of which are otherwise fixed by law.
LA.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY (executive branch). Delegation followed: 44:32(C)(2)(a) -> 39:241 -> LAC 4:I.301. Not binding on municipalities, whose fees rest on 44:32(C)(1)(a) (LA-0021).

LA.legal_concept: Uniform fee schedule: minimum $0.25 per page (paper/microfiche up to 8.5x14; two-sided = two pages)
LA.atomic_rule: For state agencies, charges for the first copy of any public record shall be at a minimum $0.25 per page for microfiche reproductions or paper copies up to 8 1/2 by 14 inches; a two-sided copy counts as two pages.
LA.trigger: State-agency copy request, paper/microfiche up to 8.5x14
LA.source_language: B.1. Charges for the first copy of any public records shall be at a minimum $0.25 per page for microfiche reproductions or paper copies up to 8 1/2 by 14 inches. 2. A two-sided copy shall be considered two pages.
LA.source_authority: La. Admin. Code tit. 4, pt. I, §301(B)
LA.effective_status: Current (Promulgated LR 8:411, Aug. 1982; amended LR 12:229, Apr. 1986; DOA compilation)
LA.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY; 'at a minimum' makes this a floor (an agency exceeding it must justify under §301.E, LA-9002/LA-9005). Cities are not bound; historically the AG urged local bodies to adopt this schedule 'to ensure objective reasonableness' (AG Op. 96-270 — not opened; cited second-hand, manual verification). Index page: https://www.doa.la.gov/doa/osr/louisiana-administrative-code/

LA.legal_concept: Uniform fee schedule: oversized copies at actual cost
LA.atomic_rule: For state agencies, charges for copies on paper larger than 8 1/2 by 14 inches shall equal the actual cost to the agency of copying them.
LA.trigger: State-agency copy request, paper larger than 8.5x14
LA.source_language: C. Charges for copies of public records on paper larger than 8 1/2 by 14 inches shall be the same as the actual cost to the agency for copying same.
LA.source_authority: La. Admin. Code tit. 4, pt. I, §301(C)
LA.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY. Standard term: 'actual cost to the agency'.

LA.legal_concept: Uniform fee schedule: computer-stored records — printout schedule approved by DOA; estimate required for programming; actual cost incl. programming charged if it differs
LA.atomic_rule: For state agencies, preprinted computer reports are charged at the §301 page rate; each agency shall adopt a DOA-approved schedule for database printouts; where reproduction requires program modification or specialized programs the requester shall be given an estimate, told it is an estimate, and charged the actual cost of reproduction including programming costs if it differs.
LA.trigger: State-agency request for computer-stored records requiring program modification or specialized programs
LA.source_language: D. Charges for copies of public records on preprinted computer reports shall be the same rate specified in §301.A and B. Each agency shall develop a uniform fee schedule for providing printouts of public records stored in a computer data base utilizing routing utility programs. Such uniform fee schedule shall be first approved by the Division of Administration. An estimated cost shall be given for reproduction of public records stored in a computer which require program modification or specialized programs. The requesting party shall be advised of the estimate, and that it is an estimate, but the actual cost for reproduction, including programming costs, shall be charged if it differs from the estimate.
LA.source_authority: La. Admin. Code tit. 4, pt. I, §301(D)
LA.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY. Bundles an estimate notice (structural), a programming-cost charge (actual cost), and an overrun rule (actual charged if it differs from estimate — no percentage trigger). Kept in one row because the source states them as one conditional sequence.

LA.legal_concept: Uniform fee schedule: agency fees above the schedule need written justification approved by DOA
LA.atomic_rule: A state agency with an established copy fee exceeding the schedule must justify that fee in writing and have it approved by the Division of Administration.
LA.trigger: State agency charges more than LAC 4:I.301 rates
LA.source_language: E. Agencies which have an established fee for copying public records that is in excess of those set forth in the rule must justify that fee in writing and have the established fee approved by the Division of Administration.
LA.source_authority: La. Admin. Code tit. 4, pt. I, §301(E)
LA.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY. §301.G: schedule does not apply where a fee is otherwise fixed by law nor to agency-to-agency requests: 'G. This schedule does not apply to copies of public records, the fees for the reproduction of which are otherwise fixed by law, nor shall this schedule apply to requests for copies from one state agency to another.'

LA.legal_concept: Uniform fee schedule: free or reduced copies for indigent citizens or public-purpose users
LA.atomic_rule: State agencies shall furnish copies without charge or at a reduced charge to indigent citizens of Louisiana or to persons whose use of the copies will be limited to a public purpose (e.g., a hearing before a governmental regulatory commission).
LA.trigger: State-agency requester is indigent or will use copies only for a public purpose
LA.source_language: F. Copies of public records shall be furnished without charge, or at a reduced charge, to indigent citizens of this state or the persons whose use of such copies will be limited to a public purpose, including, but not limited to, use in a hearing before any governmental regulatory commission.
LA.source_authority: La. Admin. Code tit. 4, pt. I, §301(F)
LA.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY. Note the rule says 'shall be furnished' whereas 44:32(C)(2)(a) says 'may be furnished' — statute governs (discretionary); the rule's mandatory phrasing is noted as an inconsistency. Municipal waiver ground is indigency only (LA-0025).

LA.legal_concept: Reasonable compensation for custodian's representative during after-hours examination, funded in advance by the examiner
LA.atomic_rule: Examinations must occur during regular office or working hours unless the custodian authorizes otherwise, in which event the persons designated to represent the custodian during the examination are entitled to reasonable compensation paid by the public body out of funds provided in advance by the person examining after hours.
LA.trigger: Custodian authorizes examination outside regular office/working hours
LA.source_language: examinations of records under the authority of this Section must be conducted during regular office or working hours, unless the custodian shall authorize examination of records in other than regular office or working hours.  In this event the persons designated to represent the custodian during such examination shall be entitled to reasonable compensation to be paid to them by the public body having custody of such record, out of funds provided in advance by the person examining such record in other than regular office or working hours.
LA.effective_status: Current (last amended Acts 2024, No. 411; fee text of (C)(1)(a) as amended by Acts 2023, No. 247, eff. Aug. 1, 2023; no 2025 or 2026 amendment found)
LA.notes: AMENDS LA-0027: source opened verbatim (is_paraphrase now false) and the citation corrected from 44:32(B) to 44:32(A)(1) (subsection B is the segregation clause). 'Reasonable compensation' is a soft standard the public body sets; AG 17-0056 (LA-9009) limits it to time the employee is present during the examination. Applies to all public bodies.

LA.legal_concept: No fee for retrieval, review, segregation/redaction time or for copies made in the course of redaction, absent judicial authorization
LA.atomic_rule: A custodian may not charge a requester for pre-examination retrieval, review, and separation of records, nor for copies the custodian makes in the process of redacting nonpublic information, unless a court authorizes such a fee; the only authorized fees are reasonable copy fees.
LA.trigger: Custodian incurs staff time locating, reviewing, or redacting records
LA.source_language: You ask whether the official can be paid for the time spent retrieving the responsive documents, and more specifically, the time spent segregating public and non-public records. As outlined above, La. R.S. 44:32(B) states that if a record contains material which is not public, the non-public information may be segregated from the response; however, La. R.S. 44:32 does not specifically authorize a fee to be collected in this scenario. If such segregation takes an extraordinary amount of time to compile, then the elected official may wish to consult with the city attorney to determine whether it is appropriate for the city to seek a judicial determination requesting that a fee be charged to the requestor for the segregation. [quoted from a prior opinion] ... Thus, although the law allows a custodian to collect reasonable fees when a request seeks copies of public records, there is no specific authorization for a fee to be collected for segregating or redacting nonpublic information when a request seeks only to inspect public records. As such, we are of the opinion that the general rule of La. R.S. 44:32(C)(3) applies when a public records custodian makes copies of public records in the process of redacting nonpublic information when responding to a request to examine public records, and a custodian may not charge a fee to the requester for such copies unless the custodian receives judicial authorization for such a fee.
LA.source_authority: La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 17-0056 (Apr. 2, 2018), pp. 5-7, construing La. R.S. 44:32(B), (C)(1)-(3)
LA.effective_status: Current (opinion issued Apr. 2, 2018; clarified on other points by Op. 17-0056A, July 27, 2018)
LA.notes: Text extracted by OCR from the AG's scanned PDF; wording checked against the page image. Opinion addressed a parish sheriff (local body) — treated as applying to all custodians. The prior opinion it quotes is printed as 'La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 15-0173'; the opinion posted under that number on the AG portal is unrelated (vessel salvage), so the quoted opinion's number needs manual verification. Framed mainly around inspection requests; DOJ's 2023 guidance (LA-9012) states the rule generally: 'Can't charge for the time to process the request.'

LA.legal_concept: After-hours compensation limited to time the employee is present during the examination, not preparation
LA.atomic_rule: A custodian may require advance payment of an employee's compensation only for the time the employee is present during the requester's after-hours examination, not for pre-examination preparation, absent a judicial declaration allowing otherwise.
LA.trigger: After-hours examination authorized; custodian seeks compensation for preparation/overtime
LA.source_language: No provision of the Public Records Law directly authorizes such a charge to the requester. We must therefore return to La. R.S. 44:32(C)(3) and the default rule that a requester may not be charged a fee in connection with a request to examine public records, nor for a custodian's pre-examination retrieval, review, and separation of records. See La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 15-0173, supra. We are therefore of the opinion that a custodian may require a requester to provide advance payment of an employee's compensation only for the time the employee is present during the requester's examination, not for pre-examination preparation, absent a judicial declaration allowing otherwise.
LA.source_authority: La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 17-0056 (Apr. 2, 2018), p. 7
LA.notes: OCR-extracted verbatim. Same opinion reaffirms that after-hours inspection may be required only when the request 'disrupts normal office procedure to the point where the office ceases to operate' (citing Ops. 96-0079, 98-0366, 01-0244).

LA.legal_concept: 'Reasonable fee' for copies includes at minimum the actual cost of making the copies; excludes generation cost/value of the information
LA.atomic_rule: A reasonable copy fee under 44:32(C)(1)(a) is fact-specific, is not designed to recoup the cost of preparing the records, does not include the original cost of generating the information or its value, and includes at a minimum the actual costs for making the copies.
LA.trigger: Non-state-agency custodian sets or applies a copy fee (incl. electronic copy on disc)
LA.source_language: The Public Records Act allows a custodian to charge a "reasonable fee" for making copies of public records. What constitutes a reasonable fee is ultimately a fact-specific question. However, we do note that the Public Records Act is not designed to recoup costs incurred by a public entity in preparing the records requested. Similar to the scenario you have presented, though, when considering what constituted a reasonable fee for providing access to an electronic copy of the assessment rolls, the First Circuit Court of Appeals stated: "This fee does not include the original cost of generation of the information or the actual value of the information. It does include, at a minimum, the actual costs for making the copies."
LA.source_authority: La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 15-0056 (Oct. 8, 2015), p. 4 (quoting Granger v. Litchfield, 94-0114 (La. App. 1 Cir. 11/10/94), 645 So.2d 1262)
LA.notes: Text-layer PDF, opened. Opinion addressed a parish assessor (local body); footnote 7 confirms 44:32(C)(1)(a) governs non-state agencies. Gives the reasonableness standard content without a number.

LA.legal_concept: No per-page fee when a requester copies records with a personal hand-held scanner during inspection
LA.atomic_rule: A person who inspects public records and copies them with a personal hand-held scanner is not obligated to pay a per-page fee.
LA.trigger: Requester makes own copies with own equipment during inspection
LA.source_language: a person who makes a valid public records request to inspect documents and at the time of inspection uses a personal hand-held scanner to copy said public records is not obligated to pay a fee for each page copied.
LA.notes: OCR-extracted verbatim; scanned PDF. Relies on Title Research Corp. v. Rausch, 450 So.2d 933 (La. 1984); Thornton v. DPS, 536 So.2d 595 (La. App. 1 Cir. 1988); Alliance for Affordable Energy v. Frick, 695 So.2d 1126 (La. App. 4 Cir. 1997); First Commerce Title v. Martin, 887 So.2d 716 (La. App. 2 Cir. 2004). Footnote 2: the only fees chargeable to a person merely inspecting are after-hours supervision (44:32(A)) and a court-set fee for pre-disclosure review (44:32(C)(3)).

LA.legal_concept: DOJ guidance: no charge for time to process a request; charge only for copying and electronic transmission; posted schedule required
LA.atomic_rule: Per Louisiana DOJ guidance, a custodian cannot charge for the time to process a request, to examine/review records, or for a requester's own scanner; a custodian can charge for copying (state agencies per the Administrative Code, non-state agencies a reasonable fee) and for transmission of electronic copies, and must post a fee schedule.
LA.source_language: Fees (44:32) • Providing public records is a duty and service you offer • Can't charge for the time to process the request • Can't charge people to examine or review records • Can't charge someone for bringing their own scanner • CAN charge for copying • State agencies (Administrative Code) • Non-state agencies (reasonable) • CAN charge for the transmission of electronic copies of public records (non-state agencies) • **Need fee schedule posted (Acts 2023, No. 247) • Timing of payment
LA.source_authority: Louisiana Department of Justice, 'Public Records Law' (Alicia Edmond Wheeler, Asst. Attorney General), 2023 CLE outline, slide 'Fees (44:32)', p. 21
LA.notes: Official guidance, not law — ranks below statute and formal AG opinions; included because it states the labor rule generally (not limited to inspection requests). Slide bullets reproduced verbatim; separator '•' added between bullets.

LA.legal_concept: Reasonable copy fee may include transmission of electronic copies
LA.atomic_rule: The custodian's reasonable copy fee may include the transmission of electronic copies of public records.
LA.trigger: Requester asks for electronic copies / electronic delivery
LA.source_language: The custodian may establish and collect reasonable fees for making copies of public records, which may include the transmission of electronic copies of public records.
LA.source_authority: La. R.S. 44:32(C)(1)(a) (as amended by Acts 2023, No. 247 (SB 213), eff. Aug. 1, 2023)
LA.notes: Split from LA-0021 so electronic-copy/transmission charges join the fee.electronic_media_charge / delivery concepts. Act 247 résumé digest: 'Existing law allows a custodian ... to establish and collect reasonable fees for making copies of public records, including the transmission of electronic copies ... New law ... further requires a custodian of public records that are not public records of a state agency who elects to establish and collect fees under existing law to set and publicly post a reasonable fee schedule.' Non-state-agency custodians (municipalities).

MA.legal_concept: Per-page cap extended to any size susceptible to ordinary production
MA.atomic_rule: The charge for black-and-white paper copies or printouts of records of ANY SIZE susceptible to ordinary means of production shall not exceed $0.05 per page, single- or double-sided.
MA.trigger: RAO provides B&W paper copies/printouts of records reproducible by ordinary means, regardless of page size.
MA.source_language: the charge for black and white paper copies or printouts of records of any size susceptible to ordinary means of production shall not exceed $0.05 per page, for both single and double-sided black and white copies or printouts.
MA.notes: Regulatory extension of the statutory § 10(d)(i) cap (MA-0030): adds 'of any size susceptible to ordinary means of production', so oversized-but-ordinary pages are inside the 5-cent cap; non-ordinary reproduction falls to MA-9002. Amends nothing; supplements MA-0030.

MA.legal_concept: Actual cost for copies not susceptible to ordinary reproduction
MA.atomic_rule: For copies of public records not susceptible to ordinary means of reproduction, the actual cost incurred in providing a copy may be assessed.
MA.trigger: Requested record cannot be reproduced by ordinary means (specialty/oversized/nonstandard media).
MA.source_language: for copies of public records not susceptible to ordinary means of reproduction, the actual cost incurred in providing a copy may be assessed.
MA.notes: Bound: actual cost incurred. Covers specialty reproduction (photographs, maps, A/V and other non-ordinary media). Sits under the overall actual-cost ceiling (MA-0029).

MA.legal_concept: No copying fee for electronic or facsimile copies
MA.atomic_rule: A records access officer shall not assess a copying fee for electronic copies or for copies of public records transmitted via facsimile.
MA.trigger: Records are provided as electronic copies or transmitted by facsimile.
MA.source_language: a records access officer shall not assess a copying fee for electronic copies or copies of public records transmitted via facsimile.
MA.notes: Prohibits the COPYING fee component for electronic/fax delivery; labor above the free-hour threshold and the actual cost of a physical storage device (MA-0031) remain chargeable. Material for the engine: electronic production zeroes the duplication line.

MA.atomic_rule: 'Employee time' means time required by employees or necessary vendors, including outside legal counsel, technology and payroll consultants or others as needed by the municipality.
MA.trigger: Labor fee is computed for a request (determines whose time counts toward the >2-hour trigger and the billable hours).
MA.source_language: As used in this section, ''employee time'' means time required by employees or necessary vendors, including outside legal counsel, technology and payroll consultants or others as needed by the municipality.
MA.notes: Definition the fee engine branches on: vendor time (e.g., IT extraction work) counts as employee time and is therefore subject to the same trigger, free hours, and rate ceiling — there is no separate uncapped vendor pass-through for labor.

MA.legal_concept: Small-municipality charging of the first two hours; census burden
MA.atomic_rule: A municipal RAO in a municipality with a population of 20,000 or fewer may assess a fee for the first two hours of time spent compiling, segregating, redacting and reproducing a requested record, provided population is determined by the decennial U.S. Census and the RAO bears the burden of providing population data in responses assessing such fees.
MA.trigger: Municipality of 20,000 or fewer population assesses labor fees for the first two hours.
MA.source_language: a municipal records access officer in a municipality with a population of 20,000 persons or fewer may assess a fee for the first two hours of time spent compiling, segregating, redacting and reproducing a requested record, provided: i. population data shall be determined by the decennial U.S. Census; and ii. it shall be the burden of the municipal records access officer to provide population data information in responses in which it seeks to assess such fees.
MA.notes: Complement of MA-0034's population gate: makes explicit that small municipalities may charge from hour zero, resolves the population source (decennial Census) and puts the evidentiary burden on the RAO. Supersedes nothing; refines the note on MA-0034 (which read small municipalities as 'not entitled to charge labor at all' — the regulation states the opposite: they may charge the first two hours).

MA.legal_concept: Conditions on denial for prior nonpayment
MA.atomic_rule: An RAO may deny access by written notice to a requester who failed to compensate the custodian for previously produced records only if a compliant fee estimate was prepared for the previous request and the requester agreed to pay it, and the written notice must detail the reasons for denial including an itemized list of outstanding balances.
MA.trigger: Requester with unpaid balances for previously produced records submits a new request.
MA.source_language: A records access officer may provide written notice denying access to public records to a requester who has failed to compensate the custodian for previously produced public records, provided: 1. a fee estimate for a previous request was prepared in compliance with 950 CMR 32.00 and the requester agreed to pay the previous fee; 2. the written notice details the reasons for denial, including an itemized list of any balances attributed to previously produced records.
MA.notes: Narrows MA-0041 (§ 10(d)(vi)): prior-debt denial requires (a) a 950-CMR-compliant estimate on the earlier request AND (b) the requester's agreement to pay it; itemized-balance notice duty mirrors § 10(d)(vii). Engine gate on the requestor ledger.

MA.legal_concept: Postage at actual cost, conditioned and lowest-cost
MA.atomic_rule: An RAO may assess the actual cost of postage to mail copies only if the requester specifically requests mailing or cannot receive copies in person, and must charge the lowest mailing cost available, at the requester's discretion.
MA.trigger: Copies are mailed at the requester's request or because the requester cannot receive them in person.
MA.source_language: a records access officer may assess the actual cost of postage to mail copies of public records, provided: 1. the requester specifically requests that records be mailed or is unable to receive copies in person; and 2. the records access officer shall charge the lowest cost available for such mailings, at the discretion of the requester.
MA.notes: Bound: actual postage cost, lowest available service. Two gate conditions before any postage line may appear on an invoice. No handling surcharge authorized.

MA.atomic_rule: A records access officer's failure to comply with the 950 CMR 32.06(4) petition provisions results in a waiver of the right to assess fees for the public records; petitions do not relieve the RAO of the 10-business-day initial-response duty.
MA.trigger: RAO files (or should have filed) a 32.06(4) petition for extension or fee-limit waiver and fails to comply with its provisions.
MA.clock_spec: terminal: fee-assessment right waived on 950 CMR 32.06(4) noncompliance
MA.source_language: petitions filed under 950 CMR 32.06(4) do not affect the requirement that a records access officer shall provide an initial response to a requester within ten business days following receipt of a request for public records, pursuant to 950 CMR 32.06(2)(a) or (b). Failure to comply with 950 CMR 32.06(4) will result in a waiver of the right to assess fees for public records.
MA.notes: Second, regulation-level forfeiture trigger alongside § 10(e) (MA-0040): procedural noncompliance with the petition rules costs the body its fee entitlement. Terminal effect on the fee right, like MA-0040.

MA.atomic_rule: A records access officer shall inform a requester of the availability of records online to avoid delays and fees associated with the provision of public records.
MA.source_language: A records access officer shall inform a requester of the availability of records online to avoid delays and fees associated with the provision of public records.
MA.notes: Mandatory fee-avoidance notice: a required communication step before charging for records that are posted online. Pairs with the itemized-estimate duty (MA-0039).

MI.legal_concept: Paper copies on other than 8-1/2x11 / 8-1/2x14 paper - actual incremental duplication cost
MI.atomic_rule: Paper copies on paper other than 8-1/2 x 11 or 8-1/2 x 14 inches are charged at the actual total incremental cost of necessary duplication or publication, not including labor, calculated and itemized as a total cost per sheet; the 10-cent cap applies only to the two named sizes.
MI.trigger: Paper copies provided on paper sizes other than 8-1/2 x 11 or 8-1/2 x 14 inches (oversized/nonstandard).
MI.source_language: For paper copies of public records provided to the requestor, the actual total incremental cost of necessary duplication or publication, not including labor. The cost of paper copies shall be calculated as a total cost per sheet of paper and shall be itemized and noted in a manner that expresses both the cost per sheet and the number of sheets provided. The fee must not exceed 10 cents per sheet of paper for copies of public records made on 8-1/2- by 11-inch paper or 8-1/2- by 14-inch paper.
MI.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
MI.notes: Fills the oversized/nonstandard gap: the per-sheet 10-cent ceiling (MI-0038) is textually limited to letter/legal sizes; all other paper sizes stay under the actual-total-incremental-cost clause with mandatory per-sheet itemization. Amends nothing; complements MI-0038.

MI.legal_concept: State minimum hourly wage rate (external figure for the 6x contracted-redaction-labor cap)
MI.atomic_rule: The state minimum hourly wage rate referenced by MCL 15.234(1)(b)'s contracted-redaction-labor cap (6x that rate) is $12.48 beginning February 21, 2025, $13.73 beginning January 1, 2026, and $15.00 beginning January 1, 2027, with treasurer-calculated CPI adjustments published each October beginning October 2027 - making the contracted-labor ceiling $82.38/hour during 2026.
MI.trigger: Public body charges contracted labor for separating/deleting exempt information under MCL 15.234(1)(b) (no capable employee, FOIA-coordinator determined, contractor named on itemization).
MI.source_language: (1) Subject to the exceptions specified in this act, the minimum hourly wage rate is: (a) Beginning February 21, 2025, $12.48. (b) Beginning January 1, 2026, $13.73. (c) Beginning January 1, 2027, $15.00.
MI.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws § 408.934(1) (Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act, 2018 PA 337)
MI.effective_status: Current (Am. 2025 PA 1, imd. eff. Feb. 21, 2025; original initiative revived per Mothering Justice v Attorney General, No. 165325 (Mich. July 31, 2024)); $13.73 step effective Jan 1, 2026; $15.00 step Jan 1, 2027; CPI-adjusted thereafter unless state unemployment >= 8.5%
MI.notes: Delegation instrument for MI-0036's 6x cap - a moving external figure. 6 x $13.73 = $82.38/hour through Dec 31, 2026; becomes 6 x $15.00 = $90.00/hour on Jan 1, 2027. Opened at legislature.mi.gov (MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026).

MN.legal_concept: Suspension of further response when available data/copies are not inspected or collected and paid for within five business days
MN.atomic_rule: If the responsible authority has notified the requester that responsive data or copies are available and the requester does not inspect the data or collect the copies within five business days of the notification, the authority may suspend any further response to the request until the requester inspects the data or collects and pays for the produced copies.
MN.trigger: Availability notification sent; requester fails to inspect or collect within 5 business days.
MN.clock_spec: pauses: any further response, 5 business-days from availability notification; resumes on inspection or collection-and-payment
MN.source_language: If a responsible authority has notified the requesting person that responsive data or copies are available for inspection or collection, and the requesting person does not inspect the data or collect the copies within five business days of the notification, the responsible authority may suspend any further response to the request until the requesting person inspects the data that has been made available, or collects and pays for the copies that have been produced.
MN.notes: NEW 2025 provision — the library's known recency gap. Permissive ('may suspend'); consequence is suspension, not withdrawal; cure restores processing. Also the statute's only payment gate: further response may be withheld until produced copies are paid for.

MN.legal_concept: Actual costs of making, certifying, and electronically transmitting copies (general copy path)
MN.atomic_rule: When copies or electronic transmittal are requested (outside the 100-or-fewer b/w letter/legal page band), the responsible authority may require payment of the actual costs of making, certifying, and electronically transmitting the copies.
MN.trigger: Request for copies or electronic transmittal not on the <=100-page b/w flat-rate band.
MN.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost (making + certifying + electronic transmission)
MN.source_language: If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time, and for making, certifying, and electronically transmitting the copies of the data or the data, but may not charge for separating public from not public data.
MN.notes: Complements MN-0008 (which carries the search/retrieval half of the same sentence) with the making/certifying/transmitting half. Displaced by the $0.25/page ceiling on the <=100-page b/w band (MN-0009). Refined by delegated rule Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4 (MN-9006).

MN.legal_concept: No charge for separating public from not public data (redaction/segregation)
MN.atomic_rule: The responsible authority may not charge for separating public from not public data.
MN.trigger: Responsive records require redaction/segregation of not-public data before release.
MN.source_language: ... but may not charge for separating public from not public data.
MN.notes: Makes review/redaction labor categorically non-chargeable statewide. Guidance layer concurs: Advisory Opinion 04-072 (employee time to separate public from not public data excluded; sorting/reviewing/verifying accuracy excluded if not necessary for copying).

MN.legal_concept: Additional reasonable fee for copies of commercial-value data developed with significant public expenditure
MN.atomic_rule: When a request involves receipt of copies of public data with commercial value that is a substantial/discrete portion or all of a formula, compilation, program, database, or system developed with significant public expenditure, the responsible authority may charge a reasonable fee in addition to copy costs; the fee must be clearly demonstrated to relate to actual development costs, and sufficient justifying documentation must be provided on request.
MN.trigger: Request for copies of commercial-value data (substantial/discrete portion of a publicly funded formula, compilation, program, database, or system).
MN.clock_spec: ceiling: demonstrable actual development costs of the information (added to copy costs)
MN.source_language: When a request under this subdivision involves any person's receipt of copies of public government data that has commercial value and is a substantial and discrete portion of or an entire formula, pattern, compilation, program, device, method, technique, process, database, or system developed with a significant expenditure of public funds by the government entity, the responsible authority may charge a reasonable fee for the information in addition to the costs of making and certifying the copies. Any fee charged must be clearly demonstrated by the government entity to relate to the actual development costs of the information. The responsible authority, upon the request of any person, shall provide sufficient documentation to explain and justify the fee being charged.
MN.notes: Data-based, not requester-purpose-based: keys on the DATA's commercial value, not the requester's commercial purpose. Secondary rule type: Requirement (documentation-on-request duty). Fee sits ON TOP of the copy charge.

MN.legal_concept: Electronic-form copy of computer-stored data at actual cost; no format conversion required
MN.atomic_rule: An entity maintaining public data in a computer storage medium shall provide an electronic-form copy if it can reasonably do so, is not required to provide the data in a different format or program than the one in which it maintains the data, and may require payment of the actual cost of providing the copy.
MN.trigger: Request for an electronic copy of public data held in a computer storage medium.
MN.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of providing the electronic copy
MN.source_language: The responsible authority of a government entity that maintains public government data in a computer storage medium shall provide to any person making a request under this section a copy of any public data contained in that medium, in electronic form, if the government entity can reasonably make the copy or have a copy made. This does not require a government entity to provide the data in an electronic format or program that is different from the format or program in which the data are maintained by the government entity. The entity may require the requesting person to pay the actual cost of providing the copy.
MN.notes: Anchors electronic-media and programming/extraction charging at actual cost; the no-conversion-required sentence bounds what programming labor can be demanded. Media cost (USB etc.) includable per DPO guidance (MN-9008).

MN.legal_concept: Reasonable-fee factors for copies of public data (delegated rule)
MN.atomic_rule: In setting a reasonable fee for copies of public data, the responsible authority shall be guided by: (A) cost of materials including paper; (B) cost of labor to prepare the copies; (C) any schedule of standard copying charges established by the agency in its normal course of operations; (D) special costs necessary to produce copies from machine-based record-keeping systems including computers and microfilm systems; and (E) mailing costs.
MN.trigger: Responsible authority determines a fee for providing copies of public data.
MN.clock_spec: soft-standard: 'reasonable fee' guided by five enumerated cost factors (no dollar figures)
MN.source_language: The responsible authority may charge a reasonable fee for providing copies of public data. In determining the amount of the reasonable fee, the responsible authority shall be guided by the following: A. the cost of materials, including paper, used to provide the copies; B. the cost of the labor required to prepare the copies; C. any schedule of standard copying charges as established by the agency in its normal course of operations; D. any special costs necessary to produce such copies from machine based record keeping systems, including but not limited to computers and microfilm systems; and E. mailing costs.
MN.source_authority: Minn. R. 1205.0300, subp. 4 (statutory authority Minn. Stat. § 13.07)
MN.notes: Delegated instrument opened per the step-2 mandate (§ 13.07 delegation to the commissioner of administration). Contains NO dollar figures — only the reasonable-fee factor framework. Predates and must be read with the § 13.03 subd. 3(c) 25-cent band and separation prohibition; the statute governs on conflict. Factor C expressly lets the entity use its own standard copying-charge schedule.

MN.legal_concept: Data subject: free viewing of private data; reasonable fee for copies (delegated rule)
MN.atomic_rule: The responsible authority shall not charge the data subject any fee where the data subject only desires to view private data, and may charge the data subject a reasonable fee for providing copies of private data.
MN.trigger: Data subject seeks to view, or requests copies of, private data about themselves.
MN.clock_spec: soft-standard: reasonable fee for copies only; viewing free
MN.source_language: The responsible authority shall not charge the data subject any fee in those instances where the data subject only desires to view private data. The responsible authority may charge the data subject a reasonable fee for providing copies of private data.
MN.source_authority: Minn. R. 1205.0400, subp. 5 (statutory authority Minn. Stat. § 13.07)
MN.notes: Second delegated instrument opened. Secondary rule type: Permission (copies fee). Data-subject regime — mirrors § 13.04 subd. 3 (MN-0010: actual costs of making and certifying; no search/retrieval charge to data subjects per DPO guidance). Fee-amount criteria cross-reference part 1205.0300 (MN-9006).

MN.legal_concept: Actual-cost components: lowest-paid-capable-employee rate; includable and excluded cost categories (Commissioner advisory-opinion guidance)
MN.atomic_rule: In calculating actual cost, employee time must be based on the wages/salary (may include benefits) of the lowest-paid entity employee who could complete the task; includable: media, mailing, copy-preparation time, outside reproduction costs, search/retrieval time (except for data-subject requesters); excluded: separation/redaction time, copier operating expenses, invoice preparation, off-site return, unnecessary sorting/review, sales tax, accounting functions, inspection-related costs.
MN.trigger: Entity calculates an actual-cost copy charge.
MN.clock_spec: soft-standard: actual cost, employee time at lowest-paid-capable-employee rate
MN.source_language: Note: Employee time must be calculated based on the wages/salary (may include benefits) of the lowest-paid entity employee who could complete the task (Advisory Opinion 04-056)
MN.source_authority: MN Dept. of Administration, Data Practices Office, 'Actual Cost' page (Advisory Opinions 04-056, 00-054, 95-044, 97-012, 04-072, 01-066, 04-040, 04-055, 94-059, 99-024, 04-003, 04-038)
MN.notes: GUIDANCE LAYER, not statute — Commissioner of Administration advisory opinions are persuasive interpretation of § 13.03 subd. 3(c). The atomic rule condenses the page's includable/excluded lists; the quoted clause is verbatim from the opened page. Underlying opinions not individually opened — cite the guidance page, flag opinion-level verification if litigated.

MN.legal_concept: 25-cent band glosses: 50 cents two-sided; flat rate with no add-on charges (guidance)
MN.atomic_rule: On the 100-or-fewer-page black-and-white letter/legal band, the maximum charge is 25 cents per page or 50 cents for a two-sided copy, as a flat rate to which no additional charges (such as mailing or paper) may be added.
MN.trigger: Request on the <=100-page b/w letter/legal paper-copy band.
MN.clock_spec: ceiling: $0.25/page single-sided, $0.50 two-sided, flat — no add-ons
MN.source_language: For 100 or fewer pages of black and white, letter or legal sized paper copies, the maximum charge allowed is 25 cents for each page copied, or 50 cents for a two-sided copy. This charge is a flat rate; government cannot add on any additional charges, such as cost of mailing or paper.
MN.source_authority: MN Dept. of Administration, Data Practices Office, 'Copy Costs' page
MN.notes: GUIDANCE LAYER: the 50-cent two-sided figure and the no-add-on 'flat rate' reading appear ONLY on this DPO page, not in § 13.03 subd. 3(c) itself. Statute governs on conflict; treat the glosses as the Commissioner's interpretation. Also states charging is permissive: 'The Data Practices Act allows, but does not require, government to charge for copies.'

MO.legal_concept: Oversized paper copies (larger than 9x14) priced by cost components
MO.atomic_rule: Fees for paper copies larger than nine by fourteen inches shall include only the cost of copies, staff time (not exceeding the average hourly rate of pay for staff required for making copies and programming), and the cost of the medium used for the duplication.
MO.trigger: Producing a paper copy larger than 9x14 inches
MO.source_language: Fees for providing access to public records maintained on computer facilities, recording tapes or disks, videotapes or films, pictures, maps, slides, graphics, illustrations or similar audio or visual items or devices, and for paper copies larger than nine by fourteen inches shall include only the cost of copies, staff time, which shall not exceed the average hourly rate of pay for staff of the public governmental body required for making copies and programming, if necessary, and the cost of the disk, tape, or other medium used for the duplication.
MO.notes: Extracted because MO-0023's row named only electronic/media records; the same clause expressly covers oversized paper copies, which the prior pass left silent. ceiling: enumerated actual-cost components only.

MO.legal_concept: Maps/blueprints/plats requiring special expertise — trained-personnel compensation
MO.atomic_rule: Fees for maps, blueprints, or plats that require special expertise to duplicate may include the actual rate of compensation for the trained personnel required to duplicate them.
MO.trigger: Duplicating maps, blueprints, or plats that require special expertise
MO.source_language: Fees for maps, blueprints, or plats that require special expertise to duplicate may include the actual rate of compensation for the trained personnel required to duplicate such maps, blueprints, or plats.
MO.notes: ceiling: actual rate of compensation of the trained personnel (an actual-cost bound, no dollar figure). Lifts the default staff-average-rate cap for this record class only.

MO.legal_concept: Programming beyond the customary and usual level — actual costs
MO.atomic_rule: If programming beyond the customary and usual level is required to comply with a request, the fees may include the actual costs of such programming.
MO.trigger: Request requires programming beyond the customary and usual level
MO.source_language: If programming is required beyond the customary and usual level to comply with a request for records or information, the fees for compliance may include the actual costs of such programming.
MO.notes: ceiling: actual programming costs; exceeds the ordinary staff-average-rate cap (MO-0023) only when the programming is beyond customary/usual. Secondary rule type: Calculation.

MO.atomic_rule: Based on the scope of the request, the public governmental body shall produce the copies using employees of the body that result in the lowest amount of charges for search, research, and duplication time.
MO.trigger: Assigning staff to fulfill a copy request
MO.source_language: Based on the scope of the request, the public governmental body shall produce the copies using employees of the body that result in the lowest amount of charges for search, research, and duplication time.
MO.notes: Amends MO-0021 (was is_paraphrase=true / 'Requires manual verification'): operative clause now confirmed verbatim from the opened current statute. It is a mandatory duty ('shall produce'), scoped by 'Based on the scope of the request'. Config home corrected to structural — it is a cost-minimization duty the engine applies, not a value the city fills in.

MO.legal_concept: Requester-initiated cost estimate before production (verbatim confirmation)
MO.atomic_rule: Prior to producing copies, the person requesting the records may request the public governmental body to provide an estimate of the cost.
MO.trigger: Requester asks for a cost estimate before copies are produced
MO.source_language: Prior to producing copies of the requested records, the person requesting the records may request the public governmental body to provide an estimate of the cost to the person requesting the records.
MO.notes: Amends MO-0022 (was is_paraphrase=true / 'Requires manual verification'): clause confirmed verbatim from the opened current statute. Estimate is requester-initiated; no threshold obliges the body to volunteer one.

MO.legal_concept: Public-interest fee waiver with commercial-interest limiter (full verbatim)
MO.atomic_rule: The body may furnish documents without charge or at a reduced charge when it determines the waiver or reduction is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the body's operations or activities and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.
MO.trigger: Body determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest and not primarily in the requester's commercial interest
MO.source_language: Documents may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge when the public governmental body determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the public governmental body and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester;
MO.notes: Amends MO-0024: its source_language omitted the conjunctive second ground 'and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester' — a waiver DISQUALIFIER the engine must test. Both grounds are conjunctive; do not fragment. Whether the commercial-interest clause predates the 2025 act was not determined from the prior-version text (flagged in gaps); the current operative text is verbatim.

MO.legal_concept: Mandatory withdrawal-warning notice in the request for payment
MO.atomic_rule: When requesting payment of fees, the public governmental body shall include notice to the requester that failure to remit payment within ninety days (one hundred fifty days if the requested fees exceed one thousand dollars) makes the request considered withdrawn.
MO.trigger: Body issues a request for payment of fees
MO.source_language: The public governmental body shall include notice to the requester that if the requester fails to remit payment of the fees within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, then the request for public records shall be considered withdrawn.
MO.notes: NEW 2025. Required notice content on every fee/payment request; the withdrawal clock (MO-0026) presumably depends on a compliant notice — statute does not state the consequence of an omitted notice (flagged in gaps).

MO.legal_concept: Clarification nonresponse — request deemed withdrawn (90/150 days)
MO.atomic_rule: If the body seeks clarification of a request and receives no response within ninety days (one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars) of sending the clarification request, the request is considered withdrawn.
MO.trigger: Body sends a clarification request; no response received within 90/150 days
MO.clock_spec: 90 calendar-days from sending the clarification request (150 calendar-days if requested fees > $1,000); expiry = request considered withdrawn
MO.source_language: If the public governmental body responds to a request for public records in order to seek a clarification of the request and no response to the request for clarification is received by the public governmental body within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, of sending the request for clarification, then such request for public records shall be considered withdrawn.
MO.notes: NEW 2025. Sits in the fee section and keys its 150-day variant to the requested FEES exceeding $1,000, but operates as a clarification-abandonment clock. Concept key proposed (clarification.nonresponse_abandonment) — not among the 23 supplied fee/payment concepts; map to the master dictionary's clarification family at reconcile.

MO.legal_concept: Mandatory withdrawal-warning notice in the clarification request
MO.atomic_rule: The body's request for clarification shall include notice that failure to respond within ninety days (one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars) makes the request considered withdrawn.
MO.trigger: Body issues a request for clarification
MO.source_language: The request for clarification by the public governmental body shall include notice to the requester that if the requester fails to respond within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, then the request shall be considered withdrawn.
MO.notes: NEW 2025. Companion notice duty to MO-9008.

MO.legal_concept: Six-month re-request fee carryover after withdrawal
MO.atomic_rule: If the same or a substantially similar request is made within six months after expiration of the 90/150-day period and no fee was remitted (or no clarification response received), the body may request payment of the original expired request's fees in addition to any allowable fees for the subsequent request.
MO.trigger: Same/substantially similar request within 6 months after a 90/150-day withdrawal for nonpayment or clarification nonresponse
MO.source_language: If the same or a substantially similar request for public records is made within six months after the expiration of the ninety-day period, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, and no fee was remitted for such request or no response was received to the request for clarification, then the public governmental body may request payment of the same fees made for the original request that has expired in addition to any allowable fees necessary to fulfill the subsequent request.
MO.notes: NEW 2025. Requestor-ledger structural rule: requires matching a new request against the requestor's withdrawn requests from the prior 6 months and carrying the expired fees forward. 'Same or a substantially similar' is a soft standard — do not automate the similarity judgment; human confirms the match.

MO.legal_concept: Lawsuit exception to the withdrawal regime
MO.atomic_rule: The subsec. 2(2) withdrawal provisions do not apply if a lawsuit has been filed against the public governmental body with regard to the records that are the subject of the request.
MO.trigger: A lawsuit is filed against the body regarding the requested records
MO.clock_spec: undefined-soft: withdrawal regime 'shall not apply' while a lawsuit regarding the records is filed — no day-count; disables the 90/150-day terminal clocks
MO.source_language: The provisions of this subdivision shall not apply if a lawsuit has been filed against the public governmental body with regard to the records that are the subject of the request under this subdivision.
MO.notes: NEW 2025. Disables the entire subdivision (withdrawal, notices, carryover) once litigation over the records is filed. Clock effect recorded as pauses in the sense of disabling the terminal clocks; statute does not say whether they resume post-suit (flagged in gaps).
