MO.legal_concept: Attorney review time not chargeable as research time
MO.atomic_rule: A public governmental body may not charge attorney review time (review of responsive documents for privileged information) as research time under § 610.026.1(1).
MO.trigger: Attorney reviews responsive documents in fulfilling a request
MO.source_language: (2021) Section does not authorize a public governmental body to charge attorney review time as research time required for fulfilling records requests. Gross v. Parson, 624 S.W.3d 877 (Mo.banc).
MO.notes: Source language is the revisor's official case annotation on the opened § 610.026 page, quoted verbatim (it is the annotation's text, not the opinion's own words); AG Sunshine book states the holding identically ('does not include time for attorney to review responsive documents for privileged information'). Narrow holding only — does not decide non-attorney redaction time.

NC.legal_concept: Statutory definition of 'actual cost' for copy fees
NC.atomic_rule: For copy fees, 'actual cost' is limited to direct, chargeable costs related to the reproduction of a public record as determined by generally accepted accounting principles, and excludes costs the public agency would have incurred if the reproduction request had not been made.
NC.trigger: Agency computes the fee for an uncertified copy
NC.related_rule_ids: ceiling: direct chargeable reproduction costs (GAAP); excludes costs incurred regardless of the request
NC.is_paraphrase: For purposes of this subsection, "actual cost" is limited to direct, chargeable costs related to the reproduction of a public record as determined by generally accepted accounting principles and does not include costs that would have been incurred by the public agency if a request to reproduce a public record had not been made.
NC.official_link: Current (ncleg.gov General Statutes current through S.L. 2026-30; § 132-6.2 last amended S.L. 2004-129 — no 2024, 2025 or 2026 amendment; no pending 2026 modification listed for §§ 132-6, 132-6.2, 132-1.4A(l), 132-10)
NC.amends: Definition the copy-rate, media, and labor items all hang on. Excludes ordinary staff time and fixed equipment costs (costs incurred anyway). Binds every public agency incl. municipalities. May duplicate pruned NC-0020 (referenced by NC-0019 but absent from the corpus).

NC.legal_concept: State policy: copies free or at minimal (actual) cost
NC.atomic_rule: It is State policy that the people may obtain copies of public records free or at 'minimal cost', defined as the actual cost of reproducing the record, unless otherwise specifically provided by law.
NC.related_rule_ids: ceiling: actual cost of reproducing the record
NC.is_paraphrase: Therefore, it is the policy of this State that the people may obtain copies of their public records and public information free or at minimal cost unless otherwise specifically provided by law. As used herein, "minimal cost" shall mean the actual cost of reproducing the public record or public information.
NC.official_link: Current (ncleg.gov current through S.L. 2026-30; § 132-1 last amended S.L. 2023-134 s. 27.7(f) and S.L. 2023-138 s. 5(b) — subsection (b) text unchanged since 1995)
NC.amends: 'Free' is expressly contemplated — supports discretionary no-charge decisions; no de-minimis threshold or waiver criteria attach.

NC.legal_concept: State CIO mediation of unfair/unreasonable copy fees
NC.atomic_rule: A requester charged a fee the requester believes to be unfair or unreasonable may ask the State Chief Information Officer or designee to mediate the dispute.
NC.trigger: Requester believes a charged fee is unfair or unreasonable
NC.is_paraphrase: If anyone requesting public information from any public agency is charged a fee that the requester believes to be unfair or unreasonable, the requester may ask the State Chief Information Officer or his designee to mediate the dispute.
NC.official_link: Current (ncleg.gov General Statutes current through S.L. 2026-30; § 132-6.2 last amended S.L. 2004-129 — no 2024, 2025 or 2026 amendment; no pending 2026 modification listed for §§ 132-6, 132-6.2, 132-1.4A(l), 132-10)
NC.amends: State-level fee-dispute path binding all public agencies incl. cities; mediation, not a binding order and not a fee-waiver appeal. Proposed concept key fee.dispute_mediation (no existing key fits). May duplicate pruned NC-0022.

NC.legal_concept: Copy fee for law-enforcement agency recordings (body-worn / dashboard camera)
NC.atomic_rule: A law enforcement agency may charge a fee to offset the cost incurred to make a copy of a recording for release, and the fee shall not exceed the actual cost of making the copy.
NC.trigger: Release of a copy of a law enforcement agency recording under § 132-1.4A
NC.related_rule_ids: ceiling: actual cost of making the copy
NC.is_paraphrase: ( l ) Fee for Copies. - A law enforcement agency may charge a fee to offset the cost incurred by it to make a copy of a recording for release. The fee shall not exceed the actual cost of making the copy.
NC.official_link: Current (ncleg.gov current through S.L. 2026-30; § 132-1.4A last amended S.L. 2025-70 s. 21; pending S.L. 2026-40 s. 4.53 (eff. 10/01/2026) amends subsection (b) only)
NC.amends: Binds municipal police departments as 'law enforcement agencies'. No per-minute rate, no free minutes. Recordings under § 132-1.4A are not public records; release generally requires a court order — the fee applies to copies made for release.

NC.legal_concept: GIS copies at reasonable cost; written no-resale/non-commercial-use condition
NC.atomic_rule: A county or city shall furnish copies of its GIS databases and data files at reasonable cost and, as a condition of furnishing an electronic copy, may require the recipient to agree in writing that the copy will not be resold or otherwise used for trade or commercial purposes (news-media publication, real-estate trade association / MLS publication or at-cost resale, and non-resale use by a licensed professional in practice are not commercial use).
NC.trigger: Request for copies of county/city GIS databases or data files
NC.is_paraphrase: Upon request, the county or city shall furnish copies, in documentary or electronic form, to anyone requesting them at reasonable cost. As a condition of furnishing an electronic copy, whether on magnetic tape, magnetic disk, compact disk, or photo-optical device, a county or city may require that the person obtaining the copy agree in writing that the copy will not be resold or otherwise used for trade or commercial purposes.
NC.official_link: Current (ncleg.gov current through S.L. 2026-30; § 132-10 last amended S.L. 1997-193)
NC.amends: The only commercial-purpose mechanism in N.C. public-records law and it is municipal/county-specific and record-specific (GIS). 'Reasonable cost' is a soft standard distinct from § 132-6.2(b) 'actual cost'. No surcharge; the condition is a written agreement, not a price.

NC.legal_concept: Copies furnished upon payment of lawful fees
NC.atomic_rule: The custodian shall, as promptly as possible, furnish copies of public records upon payment of any fees as may be prescribed by law.
NC.trigger: Copy request where a lawful fee applies
NC.is_paraphrase: Every custodian of public records shall permit any record in the custodian's custody to be inspected and examined at reasonable times and under reasonable supervision by any person, and shall, as promptly as possible, furnish copies thereof upon payment of any fees as may be prescribed by law.
NC.amends: Read as permitting the custodian to collect the copy fee before or at delivery ('upon payment'); no deposit, prepayment threshold, or nonpayment-withdrawal rule attaches. Inspection carries no fee condition.

NC.legal_concept: AG guidance: labor generally not chargeable; special service charge cannot recover redaction/review time
NC.atomic_rule: Under the actual-cost definition, fees may not under most circumstances include the labor costs of the employees who make the copies; a special service charge for extensive clerical or supervisory assistance must be reasonable and based on actual labor costs and cannot be charged to recover time spent examining or removing confidential information from records.
NC.trigger: Agency considers a labor component in a copy fee
NC.is_paraphrase: "Actual cost" is defined as "direct, chargeable costs related to the reproduction of a public record as determined by generally accepted accounting principles." The law does not give examples of actual costs but it does say that actual cost may not include costs the agency would have incurred if the copy request had not been made. This means that under most circumstances, fees may not include the labor costs of the agency employees who make the copies. However, if making the copies involves extensive clerical or supervisory assistance, the agency may charge a special service fee in addition to actual duplication costs. This service charge must be reasonable and based on actual labor costs but cannot be charged to recover fees for time spent examining or removing confidential information from records. Agencies also may charge to recover the costs of mailing copies. Complaints or disputes about all records copying fees may be directed to the State Chief Information Officer or their designee for mediation.
NC.source_type: N.C. Attorney General, North Carolina Open Government Guide (2019), 'Charging Fees', p. 20
NC.official_link: Current as posted (2019 edition, Attorney General Josh Stein / N.C. Press Association; guidance, not law; predates the Jan. 2025 change of Attorney General — no later edition located)
NC.amends: Guidance restating § 132-6.2(b) and § 132-6(c); adds the express statement that review/redaction time is never recoverable through the special service charge. Guide co-authored with the N.C. Press Association and published by NCDOJ.

NC.legal_concept: AG guidance: recovery of mailing costs
NC.atomic_rule: Agencies may charge to recover the costs of mailing copies.
NC.is_paraphrase: Agencies also may charge to recover the costs of mailing copies.
NC.source_type: N.C. Attorney General, North Carolina Open Government Guide (2019), 'Charging Fees', p. 20
NC.official_link: Current as posted (2019 edition, Attorney General Josh Stein / N.C. Press Association; guidance, not law; predates the Jan. 2025 change of Attorney General — no later edition located)
NC.amends: Guidance only — the statute's 'actual cost' is tied to 'reproduction'; postage recovery rests on the AG's reading. No handling fee addressed.

NC.legal_concept: Governor's Cabinet-agency guidance: 5 cents/page recommended; no fee for electronic production or inspection
NC.atomic_rule: For State Cabinet agencies, no fee may be charged for inspecting public records or for records produced electronically; a nominal copying fee may be charged for printed copies — five cents per page is recommended — but no fee may exceed the actual cost of making the copies.
NC.related_rule_ids: recommended: $0.05/page printed; ceiling: actual cost; electronic: no fee
NC.is_paraphrase: Assessing Cost. No fees may be charged for inspecting public records or records produced electronically. Agencies may charge a nominal copying fee for records produced in printed format. Five cents per page is recommended, but no fee charged should exceed the actual cost of making the copies.
NC.source_type: Office of Governor Roy Cooper, 'Guidance for Public Records and Meetings Access for North Carolina State Government Employees' (July 2018), p. 2
NC.official_link: Current as posted (July 2018, Office of Governor Roy Cooper; guidance for Cabinet agencies, not law; predates the Jan. 2025 change of Governor — no later edition located)
NC.amends: STATE-AGENCY ONLY (Cabinet-level employees and commissions) — does not bind municipalities; recorded for the agency-regime note. Text extracted by OCR from an image-only PDF page; wording matches the rendered page but verify against the PDF.

NC.legal_concept: AG best practice: written acknowledgment with timetable and cost information
NC.atomic_rule: As a best practice (advisory), the agency should notify the requester in writing that the request was received, give a reasonable timetable, and — if fees might be charged — include information about those costs.
NC.trigger: Request received for which fees might be charged
NC.is_paraphrase: As a best practice, notify the requesting party in writing that the request has been received and give a reasonable timetable for a response. If this is a request for which fees might be charged, include information about those costs, but check with your agency's public records staff to make sure it is charging that kind of fee.
NC.source_type: N.C. Attorney General, North Carolina Open Government Guide (2019), p. 10
NC.official_link: Current as posted (2019 edition, Attorney General Josh Stein / N.C. Press Association; guidance, not law; predates the Jan. 2025 change of Attorney General — no later edition located)
NC.amends: 'Should'-level guidance, not law; sets no threshold, window, or estimate format. Recorded so the estimate item's absence is documented against the guidance, not just the statute.

NC.legal_concept: No fee for inspection of public records
NC.atomic_rule: Government agencies may not charge fees for inspecting public records.
NC.trigger: Requester inspects rather than obtains copies
NC.is_paraphrase: May an agency charge fees for inspecting public records? Government agencies may not charge fees for inspecting public records.
NC.source_type: N.C. Attorney General, North Carolina Open Government Guide (2019), p. 20; cf. N.C. Gen. Stat. § 132-6(a) (fee condition attaches only to furnishing copies)
NC.official_link: Current as posted (2019 edition, Attorney General Josh Stein / N.C. Press Association; guidance, not law; predates the Jan. 2025 change of Attorney General — no later edition located)
NC.amends: Statute § 132-6(a) imposes the payment condition only on furnishing copies; the AG Guide states the no-inspection-fee rule expressly. Governor's 2018 Cabinet guidance says the same for state agencies (NC-9010).

NE.legal_concept: Attorney General enforcement safe harbor: photocopy charges up to 25 cents per page not questioned
NE.atomic_rule: Under the Attorney General's current enforcement policy, the AG's office will not question copying charges of up to 25 cents per page for copies of public records, in addition to the other allowable charges (labor/special service charge) permitted under 2024 LB 43.
NE.trigger: Custodian sets a per-page photocopy charge; AG review of fees under § 84-712.03(1)(b).
NE.source_language: Under the Attorney General's current enforcement policy, this office will not question copying charges of up to 25 cents per page for copies of public records in addition to the other allowable charges discussed in Op. Att'y Gen. No. 01029 and permitted under the provisions of 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43.
NE.source_authority: Nebraska Attorney General, 'Outline of Nebraska Public Records Statutes', Part B (Copies of Public Records), Rev. 7/2024 (citing Op. Att'y Gen. No. 01029)
NE.effective_status: Current — Attorney General 'Outline of Nebraska Public Records Statutes', marked Rev. 7/2024 (post-LB 43); official guidance / enforcement policy, not law.
NE.notes: Guidance, not law: an enforcement-policy safe harbor under the statutory 'actual added cost' ceiling, applicable to any custodian the AG reviews (state and local). It does not authorize a city to exceed actual added cost and does not bind courts. Op. Att'y Gen. No. 01029 (Aug. 2, 2001) itself could not be opened (AG online archive begins 2003) — manual verification of the opinion text.

NE.legal_concept: Photocopy actual-added-cost components (supplies, equipment, contractor time)
NE.atomic_rule: For photocopies, the actual added cost of making the copies available shall not exceed the reasonably calculated actual added cost of the photocopies, which may include a reasonably apportioned cost of supplies such as paper, toner, and equipment used in preparing the copies, plus any additional payment obligation of the custodian for contractor time necessarily incurred to comply with the request.
NE.source_language: For purposes of this subdivision, (i) for photocopies, the actual added cost of making the copies available shall not exceed the amount of the reasonably calculated actual added cost of the photocopies, which may include a reasonably apportioned cost of the supplies, such as paper, toner, and equipment, used in preparing the copies, as well as any additional payment obligation of the custodian for time of contractors necessarily incurred to comply with the request for copies,
NE.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
NE.notes: Component definition under the § 84-712(3)(b) ceiling (NE-0019). Employee labor is governed separately by (3)(c)–(d) (NE-0020, NE-9004, NE-9006).

NE.legal_concept: Actual-added-cost components for computer printouts and electronic data (run time, materials, analysis and programming, report production)
NE.atomic_rule: For printouts of computerized data on paper the actual added cost shall include the reasonably calculated actual added cost of computer run time and the cost of materials; for electronic data it shall include computer run time, any necessary analysis and programming by the public body or its contracted third-party IT services company, and the production of the report in the form furnished to the requester.
NE.trigger: Copies requested as printouts of computerized data or as electronic data.
NE.source_language: (ii) for printouts of computerized data on paper, the actual added cost of making the copies available shall include the reasonably calculated actual added cost of computer run time and the cost of materials for making the copy, and (iii) for electronic data, the actual added cost of making the copies available shall include the reasonably calculated actual added cost of the computer run time, any necessary analysis and programming by the public body, public entity, public official, or third-party information technology services company contracted to provide computer services to the public body, public entity, or public official, and the production of the report in the form furnished to the requester.
NE.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
NE.notes: Also the basis for electronic-media (disc/USB) and programming/data-extraction charges; no dollar figures. Interplay with the eight-hour resident labor exclusion (which lists searching, identifying, physically redacting, copying — not programming) is unstated: human legal review.

NE.legal_concept: Special service charge for labor beyond eight cumulative hours (residents)
NE.atomic_rule: For a resident's request, a special service charge reflecting the calculated labor cost may be included in the fee for time required in excess of eight cumulative hours of searching, identifying, physically redacting, or copying.
NE.trigger: Resident requester (incl. news media); labor exceeds eight cumulative hours on the request.
NE.source_language: A special service charge reflecting the calculated labor cost may be included in the fee for time required in excess of eight cumulative hours, since that large of a request may cause some delay or disruption of the other responsibilities of the custodian's office, except that the fee for records shall not include any charge for the services of an attorney or any other person to review the requested public records seeking a legal basis to withhold the public records from the public.
NE.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
NE.notes: Basis is the 'existing salary or pay obligation' / 'calculated labor cost' — no hourly rate, no overhead multiplier. The estimate must disclose 'any special service charge' (§ 84-712(4)). Reviewable by AG petition (NE-9010).

NE.legal_concept: No charge for attorney or other legal review seeking a basis to withhold (residents)
NE.atomic_rule: For a resident's request, the fee for records shall not include any charge for the services of an attorney or any other person to review the requested public records seeking a legal basis to withhold the public records from the public.
NE.source_language: A special service charge reflecting the calculated labor cost may be included in the fee for time required in excess of eight cumulative hours, since that large of a request may cause some delay or disruption of the other responsibilities of the custodian's office, except that the fee for records shall not include any charge for the services of an attorney or any other person to review the requested public records seeking a legal basis to withhold the public records from the public.
NE.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
NE.notes: Distinguish 'physically redacting' (chargeable labor within (3)(c)) from review 'seeking a legal basis to withhold' (never chargeable to residents). Nonresidents: proportional attorney-review charge permitted (NE-9006).

NE.legal_concept: Nonresident labor charge: proportional existing salary/pay from hour zero, including attorney review
NE.atomic_rule: For nonresidents of Nebraska, the actual added cost may include a charge for the proportion of the existing salary or pay obligation to the public officers or employees, including a proportional charge for the services of an attorney to review the requested public records, for the time spent searching, identifying, physically redacting, copying, or reviewing such records.
NE.trigger: Requester is not a resident (not domiciled in Nebraska and not news media).
NE.source_language: For nonresidents of Nebraska, the actual added cost used as the basis for the calculation of a fee for records may include a charge for the proportion of the existing salary or pay obligation to the public officers or employees, including a proportional charge for the services of an attorney to review the requested public records, for the time spent searching, identifying, physically redacting, copying, or reviewing such records.
NE.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
NE.notes: Second labor regime added by 2024 LB 43; no free hours and no legal-review exclusion for nonresidents. Residency is determined by domicile; news media are residents regardless of domicile (§ 84-712(5), NE-9012).

NE.legal_concept: No fee for copies of blank forms or fully redacted pages
NE.atomic_rule: No special service charge or fee shall be charged for copies of blank forms or pages that have all meaningful information redacted.
NE.trigger: Responsive pages are blank forms or have all meaningful information redacted.
NE.source_language: No special service charge or fee shall be charged for copies of blank forms or pages that have all meaningful information redacted.
NE.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
NE.notes: Categorical page-level no-charge rule (not a page-count allowance).

NE.legal_concept: Public-interest waiver: statutory definition of 'in the public interest'
NE.atomic_rule: Waiver or reduction of a fee is in the public interest if disclosure of the public record at issue is likely to contribute to the understanding of the operations or activities of government and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the person requesting the records.
NE.trigger: Custodian considers a discretionary waiver/reduction under § 84-712(3)(h).
NE.source_language: The custodian may waive or reduce any fee described in this section if the waiver or reduction of the fee would be in the public interest. Waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest if disclosure of the public record at issue is likely to contribute to the understanding of the operations or activities of government and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the person requesting such records.
NE.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
NE.notes: Amends NE-0022 (which quotes only the first sentence and cites § 84-712(1); the current location is § 84-712(3)(h) and the definition sentence was added by 2024 LB 43). Waiver remains discretionary ('may'); the two-part test is the standard, not a mandate.

NE.legal_concept: Certified copies on demand: $1.00 certificate fee; copy at cost (typewritten 30¢ per hundred words) where no other statute sets the fee
NE.atomic_rule: Every state, county or political subdivision officer having custody of a public record must give any person on demand a certified copy on payment of the legal fees; where fees are not otherwise expressly provided by statute, the fee is thirty cents per hundred words for a typewritten copy or the cost of the mechanically reproduced copy, plus one dollar for the officer's certificate.
NE.trigger: Request for a certified copy of a public record.
NE.source_language: Every state, county or political subdivision officer having the custody of a public record or writing is bound to give any person on demand a certified copy thereof on payment of the legal fees therefor. Where fees are not otherwise expressly provided by statute, the fee shall be thirty cents per hundred words if the copy is a typewritten copy, and the cost of the mechanically reproduced copy when the copy is made by photographic or offset process. In addition thereto a fee of one dollar shall be charged for the certificate of the officer.
NE.effective_status: Current — last amended Laws 1977, LB 126, § 1; no later amendment in the codified source line; cited by the AG Outline (Rev. 7/2024).
NE.notes: Default statutory certification fee; yields to any statute that 'expressly' provides a different fee (e.g., § 33-109 for county clerk/register of deeds). Certified copies for VA claimants are free (§ 84-712.02, NE-9014).

NE.legal_concept: Attorney General review of whether fees estimated or charged are actual added costs or special service charges
NE.atomic_rule: A person denied rights under §§ 84-712 to 84-712.03 may petition the Attorney General to review, among other things, whether the fees estimated or charged by the custodian are actual added costs or special service charges as provided under § 84-712; the Attorney General must make the determination within fifteen calendar days after submission of the petition and, if the public body is not in compliance, order it to comply.
NE.trigger: Requester disputes an estimate or charge (or a denial).
NE.clock_spec: 15 calendar-days from submission of the petition (AG determination)
NE.source_language: (b) Petition the Attorney General to review the matter to determine whether a record may be withheld from public inspection or whether the public body that is custodian of such record has otherwise failed to comply with such sections, including whether the fees estimated or charged by the custodian are actual added costs or special service charges as provided under section 84-712. This determination shall be made within fifteen calendar days after the submission of the petition.
NE.effective_status: Current — as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 10 (fee-review language added); no 2025–2026 amendment found.
NE.notes: Administrative (AG) review path for fee disputes; alternative is mandamus in district court (§ 84-712.03(1)(a)). Not a waiver-denial appeal as such. Concept key proposed (fee.dispute_review) — no existing key covers fee-specific administrative review.

NE.legal_concept: 'Resident' for the fee sections: domiciled in Nebraska; news media are residents regardless of domicile
NE.atomic_rule: For purposes of §§ 84-712 to 84-712.09, resident means a person domiciled in this state and includes news media without regard to domicile.
NE.trigger: Determining whether the resident (eight free hours; no legal-review charge) or nonresident (proportional salary from hour zero) labor regime applies.
NE.source_language: For purposes of sections 84-712 to 84-712.09, resident means a person domiciled in this state and includes news media without regard to domicile.
NE.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
NE.notes: Definition the fee engine branches on (added by 2024 LB 43). Eligibility to request is unaffected — any person may request (NE-0001/0002).

NE.legal_concept: State-agency portal fees approved by the State Records Board may be included in actual added cost
NE.atomic_rule: State agencies providing electronic access to public records through a portal established under § 84-1204 must obtain approval of their proposed reasonable fees under §§ 84-1205.02 and 84-1205.03, and the actual added cost of making copies available may include the approved portal fee.
NE.trigger: State agency provides records through the Nebraska.gov portal.
NE.source_language: State agencies which provide electronic access to public records through a portal established under section 84-1204 shall obtain approval of their proposed reasonable fees for such records pursuant to sections 84-1205.02 and 84-1205.03, if applicable, and the actual added cost of making the copies available may include the approved fee for the portal.
NE.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
NE.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY — does not bind municipalities; recorded so the agency regime is visible. The delegated instrument (State Records Board fee approvals under §§ 84-1205.02–.03) was not opened because it cannot apply to a city.

NE.legal_concept: Certified copies free of charge for claimants before the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
NE.atomic_rule: When a claimant before the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (or the claimant's agent or attorney) requests certified copies of any public record for presentation of the claim, the officer in charge shall furnish the certified copy free of charge.
NE.trigger: Certified-copy request by a VA claimant, agent, or attorney for a VA claim.
NE.source_language: When it is requested by any claimant before the United States Department of Veterans Affairs or his or her agent or attorney that certified copies of any public record be furnished for the proper and effective presentation of any such claim in such department, the officer in charge of such public records shall furnish or cause to be furnished to such claimant or his or her agent or attorney a certified copy thereof free of charge.
NE.effective_status: Current — last amended Laws 1991, LB 2, § 30; no later amendment.
NE.notes: Mandatory zero-fee category (contrast the discretionary public-interest waiver, NE-0022/NE-9008).

NJ.legal_concept: Flat statutory duplication rate — actual-cost override repealed
NJ.atomic_rule: As amended by P.L.2024, c.16, the public agency shall assess $0.05 per letter-size-or-smaller page and $0.07 per legal-size-or-larger page for duplication of printed matter, and may no longer charge a demonstrated higher actual cost of duplication (the former override sentence was deleted).
NJ.trigger_conditions: Request for paper copies of a government record embodied in printed matter; no other law or regulation prescribes a record-specific fee
NJ.source_language: Enacted text: Except as otherwise provided by law or regulation and except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection, the fee assessed for the duplication of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter shall be $0.05 per letter size page or smaller, and $0.07 per legal size page or larger. || Text deleted by P.L.2024, c.16 (bracketed in S2930 [2R]): [If a public agency can demonstrate that its actual costs for duplication of a government record exceed the foregoing rates, the public agency shall be permitted to charge the actual cost of duplicating the record. The actual cost of duplicating the record, upon which all copy fees are based, shall be the cost of materials and supplies used to make a copy of the record, but shall not include the cost of labor or other overhead expenses associated with making the copy except as provided for in subsection c. of this section.] || GRC Handbook 8th ed.: Custodians must charge a flat rate of $0.05 per letter size (8 ½” x 11”) page or smaller, and $0.07 per legal size (8 ½” x 14”) page or larger, if providing a requestor with paper copies. Note that P.L. 2024, c.16 removed consideration of calculating an “actual cost” exceeding the foregoing copying costs.
NJ.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(b)(1), as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2 (S2930 [2R] markup); GRC Custodian's Handbook, 8th ed. (Jan 2025) p.27
NJ.effective_status: Amended effective 2024-09-03 (P.L.2024, c.16 took effect 90 days after 2024-06-05 enactment); codified text checked 2026-08-18
NJ.notes: Amends NJ-M01 by recording that the rate is a mandatory flat rate with no actual-cost escape. Applies to all public agencies (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1 'public agency' includes political subdivisions). Municipal ordinances cannot alter it (NJ-9006).

NJ.legal_concept: Special service charge computation basis (GRC guidance)
NJ.atomic_rule: A special service charge under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(c) is computed at the hourly rate of the lowest-level employee capable of fulfilling the request, without fringe benefits, on a case-by-case basis, and may not be established in advance by ordinance.
NJ.trigger_conditions: Custodian assesses a special service charge for an extraordinary expenditure of time and effort
NJ.source_language: Actual direct cost means hourly rate of the lowest level employee capable of fulfilling the request (no fringe benefits). A special service charge is calculated on a case-by-case basis. No special service charges can be established in advance by ordinance. || Toolkit response template: [Identify lowest level employee capable of fulfilling the request, their direct hourly rate (minus fringe benefits), the number of hours anticipated to complete request and the total estimated special service charge]. Kindly respond in writing with your acceptance or rejection of this estimated charge. We will not begin to process this request until we receive your written acceptance.
NJ.source_authority: GRC Custodian's Handbook, 8th ed. (Jan 2025) p.27; GRC Custodian's Toolkit (2011) response template; GRC Special Service Charge 14-point analysis
NJ.effective_status: Current (GRC Custodian's Handbook, Eighth Edition, January 2025 — post-P.L.2024, c.16 guidance)
NJ.notes: Guidance construing the statutory 'actual direct cost'; consistent with Courier Post v. Lenape Reg'l H.S., 360 N.J. Super. 191 (Law Div. 2002) and Fisher v. Division of Law, 400 N.J. Super. 61 (App. Div. 2008) as cited by GRC. Handbook cautions its analysis 'may change given the new rebuttal standard' of P.L.2024, c.16.

NJ.atomic_rule: A requestor has 14 business days to retrieve the government records after the custodian gives notice that the request has been completed and the records are available.
NJ.trigger_conditions: Custodian notifies requestor that the request is completed and records are available
NJ.source_language: A requestor shall have 14 business days to retrieve the government records following notice from the custodian that the request has been completed and the records are available.
NJ.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2
NJ.effective_status: Current (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5 last amended P.L.2024, c.16, s.2, effective 2024-09-03; official codified text checked 2026-08-18 shows no later amendment)
NJ.notes: New in P.L.2024, c.16. Statute states no consequence beyond the window (closure implied); not expressly a nonpayment rule but the operative pickup/payment-on-delivery clock. Mapped to payment.nonpayment_consequence as the nearest canonical concept.

NJ.atomic_rule: Where the requestor agrees to pay an assessed special service charge, the custodian is not required to provide access until the requestor has remitted payment; if the requestor objects and refuses to pay, the custodian may deny the request; per the GRC form, an accepted special service charge may require a deposit or payment in full before reproduction and the balance is due upon delivery.
NJ.trigger_conditions: Fee/special service charge assessed and accepted (or refused) by requestor
NJ.source_language: GRC Handbook: If the requestor objects to the special service charge and refuses to pay it, the custodian may deny the request for access to the record. However, if the requestor is willing to pay for it, the custodian is not required to provide access until the requestor has remitted payment. || GRC form: The custodian may require a deposit against costs for reproducing documents whenever the custodian anticipates that the documents requested will cost in excess of $5 to reproduce. N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f). Where a special service charge is warranted under OPRA, that amount will be communicated to you as required under the statute. You have the opportunity to review and object to the charge prior to it being incurred. If, however, you approve of the fact and amount of the special service charge, you may be required to pay a deposit or pay in full prior to reproduction of the documents. You may be charged a prepayment or deposit when a request for copies exceeds $5.00. The custodian will contact you and advise you of any deposit requirements. You agree to pay the balance due upon delivery of the records.
NJ.source_authority: GRC Custodian's Handbook, 8th ed. (Jan 2025) p.24; GRC official OPRA request form (2024-9-3) pp.2,5; GRC FAQ citing Paff v. City of Plainfield, GRC Complaint No. 2006-54 (July 2006)
NJ.effective_status: Current (GRC Custodian's Handbook, Eighth Edition, January 2025 — post-P.L.2024, c.16 guidance)
NJ.notes: Guidance, not statutory text; statute (5(f)) only authorizes prepayment/deposit and requires the form to state whether it is required.

NJ.legal_concept: Actual cost of media = purchase price of the material, no labor (GRC guidance)
NJ.atomic_rule: The 'actual cost' chargeable for supplies used to provide electronic records (flash drives, CDs, DVDs, tapes) is the specific fee the agency paid to purchase the material; e-mail and fax delivery are free.
NJ.trigger_conditions: Records provided on a physical electronic medium
NJ.source_language: Records provided via e-mail and facsimile are free of charge. However, custodians may charge for the actual cost to provide access to electronic records on supplies such as flash drives, CDs, DVDs, videotapes, audiotapes, etc. The “actual cost” is the specific fee the agency paid to purchase the materials. For example, if the GRC purchased a package of 100 CD-ROMs for $100 and provided records to a requestor on 1 CD-ROM, the actual cost of said CD-ROM is $1.00 ($100 ÷ 100 = $1.00).
NJ.effective_status: Current (GRC Custodian's Handbook, Eighth Edition, January 2025 — post-P.L.2024, c.16 guidance)
NJ.notes: Also stated in OPRA Alert Vol.3 Iss.2 (Nov 2010) and GRC FAQ ('cannot include any labor fees').

NJ.legal_concept: Municipal ordinances cannot set OPRA copy fees or special service charges (GRC guidance)
NJ.atomic_rule: A municipal ordinance is not a 'law or regulation' that can prescribe a different OPRA copy fee, and no special service charges can be established in advance by ordinance; the statutory rate and case-by-case special service charge govern.
NJ.trigger_conditions: Municipality purports to set OPRA copy or special service fees by ordinance
NJ.source_language: GRC FAQ: Municipal ordinances do not qualify under OPRA as being another law or regulation. || GRC Handbook: No special service charges can be established in advance by ordinance.
NJ.source_authority: GRC custodian FAQ ('How much can I charge to provide records in response to an OPRA request?'); GRC Custodian's Handbook, 8th ed. (Jan 2025) p.27; OPRA Alert Vol.2 Iss.2 (Nov 2009)
NJ.effective_status: Requires manual verification (GRC custodian FAQ page is undated and partly pre-dates P.L.2024, c.16; the quoted statement is not contradicted by the 2024 amendments)
NJ.notes: Guidance consistent with 47:1A-5(b)(1) 'shall be' language after P.L.2024, c.16 deleted the actual-cost override. Consequence for configuration: NJ municipalities have no local discretion over the per-page rate; special service charges are computed per request.

NJ.legal_concept: Actual postage recoverable for mailed delivery (GRC guidance)
NJ.atomic_rule: A custodian must grant access by the delivery method the requestor requests (regular mail, e-mail, fax) and may charge the associated actual costs, i.e., actual postage.
NJ.trigger_conditions: Requestor asks for delivery by mail
NJ.source_language: A custodian must grant access to a government record by the method of delivery requested (regular mail, e-mail, or fax). Custodians may charge associated costs for same (i.e. actual postage costs). || GRC form: [Payment Information box, column text as printed] Fees: Letter size pages - $0.05 per page Legal size pages - $0.07 per page Other materials (CD, DVD, etc) – actual cost of material Delivery: Delivery / postage fees additional depending upon delivery type. Extras: Special service charge dependent upon request.
NJ.source_authority: GRC Custodian's Toolkit, First Edition (March 2011) p.8; GRC official OPRA request form (2024-9-3) p.1
NJ.effective_status: Requires manual verification (GRC Custodian's Toolkit, First Edition, March 2011 — pre-P.L.2024, c.16; postage statement not contradicted by later law)
NJ.notes: Statute is silent on postage. Record-specific: N.J.S.A. 39:4-131 permits an additional fee of up to $5 for accident reports requested other than in person (not a general OPRA rule).

NJ.legal_concept: Fee waiver is discretionary; no statutory exemption from fees (GRC guidance)
NJ.atomic_rule: No one is exempt from OPRA fees by statute (other than the statutory no-fee categories); providing records free of charge is at the custodian's discretion.
NJ.trigger_conditions: Requestor asks for fees to be waived
NJ.source_language: Nothing in OPRA exempts anyone from having to pay the requisite fees to obtain government records. If a custodian wants to provide records to any person free of charge, it is at the custodian's discretion.
NJ.source_authority: GRC custodian FAQ ('An employee/member of the agency submitted an OPRA request. Is he/she exempt from paying the OPRA fees?')
NJ.effective_status: Requires manual verification (GRC custodian FAQ page is undated and partly pre-dates P.L.2024, c.16; the quoted statement is not contradicted by the 2024 amendments)
NJ.notes: FAQ page is undated and partly pre-dates P.L.2024, c.16 (it still describes the deleted actual-cost override); this waiver statement is not affected by the 2024 amendments but flag for manual verification.

NV.legal_concept: Repeal of extraordinary-use personnel/technology fee (former NRS 239.055)
NV.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may no longer charge an additional fee for extraordinary use of its personnel or technological resources in providing a copy of a public record; NRS 239.055 is repealed.
NV.trigger: Any request for a copy requiring staff time or technology use
NV.source_language: Sec. 13. NRS 239.055 is hereby repealed. | Section 13 of this bill eliminates the authority of a governmental entity to charge an additional fee for providing a copy of a public record when extraordinary use of personnel or resources is required. (NRS 239.055)
NV.source_authority: S.B. 287, 80th Sess. (Nev. 2019), § 13 (repealing NRS 239.055); Legislative Counsel's Digest
NV.effective_status: Current (repeal effective 2019; NRS 239.055 absent from NRS ch. 239 rev. 4/15/2026)
NV.notes: Read with NRS 239.005(1) as amended by the same act (staff costs 'incurred regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy' are not actual cost). Together they make labor categorically non-chargeable for all governmental entities incl. cities. Pre-2019 authorities (AGO 2002-32, AGO 2009-06) on 'extraordinary staff time' are superseded. AB 51 (2025) sought to restore a 'reasonable fee for the use of its personnel or technological resources' and died in committee 2025-04-12.

NV.legal_concept: State-agency written estimate when estimated actual cost exceeds $25
NV.atomic_rule: If an agency of the Executive Department charges a fee, its records official shall provide the requester an estimate of the fee (including postage if mail delivery requested) when the estimated actual cost is more than $25.
NV.trigger: Estimated actual cost of copies > $25 and agency charges a fee
NV.source_language: If an agency of the Executive Department charges a fee for providing a copy of a public record: 1. A records official shall provide a person who requests a copy of a public record with an estimate of the fee for the copy, if the estimated actual cost is more than $25. The estimate of the fee must include, without limitation, the amount of postage that the agency will charge the person if the person requested to have the copy delivered by mail.
NV.notes: Binds only 'an agency of the Executive Department' (adopted under NRS 239.008(3), NRS 378.255). Not applicable to cities; agency figure recorded as guidance for the municipal item. NAC 239.863(1)(f)(2) repeats the $25 figure on the agency request form.

NV.legal_concept: State-agency deposit capped at estimated actual cost
NV.atomic_rule: A records official of an Executive Department agency may require the requester to pay a deposit of not more than the estimate of the actual cost of providing the copy.
NV.trigger: Agency charges a fee and has estimated the cost
NV.source_language: 2. A records official: (a) May require the person who requests a copy of a public record to pay a deposit of not more than the estimate of the actual cost of providing the copy;
NV.notes: Agencies only. No dollar threshold in the regulation; the manual (NV-9008) ties the deposit to estimates over $25. No municipal analogue in NRS 239.

NV.legal_concept: State-agency payment in full before copy released
NV.atomic_rule: A records official of an Executive Department agency shall require the requester to pay the fee for the copy, including postage if applicable, before the person receives the copy.
NV.trigger: Agency charges a fee for a copy
NV.source_language: (b) Shall require the person who requests a copy of a public record to pay the fee for providing the copy, including, without limitation, postage for mailing the copy, if applicable, before the person receives the copy.
NV.notes: Agencies only. For all bodies the only statutory gate is NRS 239.030 (certified copies on payment/tender, NV-0018).

NV.legal_concept: State-agency disposal of unclaimed copies after 30 days
NV.atomic_rule: If a requester does not claim a reproduced copy, or notify the agency when it will be claimed, within 30 days after reproduction, the records official may dispose of the copy.
NV.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from reproduction of the copy (disposal permitted after)
NV.source_language: If a person who requests to receive a copy of a public record does not claim the copy, the records official may dispose of the copy if the person does not: (a) Claim the copy from the agency; or (b) Notify the agency of when the person will claim the copy, within 30 days after the copy is reproduced.
NV.notes: Agencies only. Nearest analogue to a nonpayment/abandonment consequence; no municipal rule.

NV.legal_concept: Fee list maintained and posted at each office
NV.atomic_rule: A governmental entity shall prepare and maintain a list of the fees it charges at each office where it provides copies, and post a legible sign stating the fee or the location where the fee list may be obtained.
NV.source_language: A governmental entity shall prepare and maintain a list of the fees that it charges at each office in which the governmental entity provides copies of public records. A governmental entity shall post, in a conspicuous place at each office in which the governmental entity provides copies of public records, a legible sign or notice which states: (a) The fee that the governmental entity charges to provide a copy of a public record; or (b) The location at which a list of each fee that the governmental entity charges to provide a copy of a public record may be obtained.
NV.notes: The city's own fee list is the operative municipal fee instrument in Nevada; the state sets only the actual-cost ceiling. NRS 239.053(2) adds a posting duty for the transcript surcharge.

NV.atomic_rule: An Executive Branch agency may charge for photocopying/photographic reproduction, electronic media, postage/delivery, and overtime actually incurred to comply; it may not charge for review to determine responsiveness, search/retrieval (unless a statute allows), regular staff time, a requester's use of a personal device, or recouping development cost across multiple requesters.
NV.source_language: An agency can charge for: Costs for photocopying or photographic reproduction; Costs of electronic or other media, such as CDs, DVDs, flash (thumb) drives, audiotapes, microfilm, etc.; Postage, express mail, delivery services, etc.; Overtime, if it is actually incurred by the agency in order to comply with a request. Fees are not a revenue-generating operation of an agency. An agency may not charge a fee for: Review of a record to determine if the record is a responsive record. Searching for or retrieving documents, unless otherwise allowed by statute. Regular staff time for complying with a public records request. Requestor’s use of a personal device to copy or photograph public records. Recouping the original cost of developing or producing the records, in the case of multiple requesters asking for the same records.
NV.source_authority: Nevada State Library, Archives and Public Records, 'Nevada Public Records Act: A Manual for Executive Branch Agencies' (Bulletin No. 3 rev., Aug. 2020), pp. 18-19; adopted by reference NAC 239.869
NV.effective_status: Current (2020 edition; NAC 239.869 adopts the 2014 edition and approved subsequent editions)
NV.notes: Guidance for Executive Department agencies only, but it is the only official Nevada text spelling out what 'actual cost' excludes; overtime carve-out is guidance, not in statute. Also states an agency 'may not charge the requester for the redaction' before inspection (p. 16). Bullets rendered inline for JSON; verbatim otherwise.

NV.legal_concept: State-agency deposit when estimate exceeds $25; no duty to fulfill until deposit paid
NV.atomic_rule: If an agency's fee estimate exceeds $25 it may request a deposit, must give written notice of the estimated amount, and is not required to fulfill the request until the deposit (in the amount of the estimated fee) is made.
NV.source_language: If an estimate of the fee exceeds $25, the agency may request a deposit from the person requesting a copy of the record. The agency must provide the person with written notice of the estimated amount of the fee. In such instances, the agency is not required to fulfill the public records request until the person makes a deposit in an amount of the estimated fee.
NV.source_authority: Nevada State Library, Archives and Public Records, 'Nevada Public Records Act: A Manual for Executive Branch Agencies' (2020), p. 19 'Fee Deposit'
NV.notes: Executive Department agencies only. Manual's response checklist (p. 23) adds: 'If the agency requires prepayment: No further work on the request need be taken until the estimated fees (if applicable) have been deposited' and 'If the estimated fee exceeds $25: The requester must acknowledge and approve the fee in writing before the agency fulfills the request.' No municipal analogue.

NY.legal_concept: No fee for inspection, search, review, or certification (COOG regulation)
NY.atomic_rule: An agency (state or local, including cities) shall not charge a fee for inspection of records where no redaction is permitted; for search, administrative costs, or employee time to prepare photocopies; for review of content to determine disclosure; or for any certification under Part 1401.
NY.trigger: Any FOIL request involving inspection, search, review, photocopy preparation, or certification
NY.source_language: Except when a different fee is otherwise prescribed by statute: (a) An agency shall not charge a fee for the following: (1) inspection of records for which no redaction is permitted; (2) search for, administrative costs of, or employee time to prepare photocopies of records; (3) review of the content of requested records to determine the extent to which records must be disclosed or may be withheld; or (4) any certification required pursuant to this Part.
NY.notes: COOG general regulations promulgated under POL § 89(1)(b)(iii) implementing § 87(1); Part 1401 expressly covers 'RECORDS OF STATE AND LOCAL AGENCIES, INCLUDING COUNTIES, CITIES, TOWNS, VILLAGES, SCHOOL DISTRICTS AND FIRE DISTRICTS' — municipal authority, unlike agency-specific parts (e.g., 21 NYCRR 9760.8). Adds beyond statute: photocopy employee time never chargeable; review never chargeable; certification free.

NY.legal_concept: Photocopy fee ceilings in the COOG regulation; no mandate to raise fees
NY.atomic_rule: An agency may charge for photocopies up to 25 cents per page (<=9x14 inches) and up to actual reproduction cost for photocopies over 9x14 inches; the regulation does not mandate raising fees where the agency historically charged less.
NY.trigger: Paper photocopies provided in response to a FOIL request
NY.source_language: (b) An agency may charge a fee for photocopies of records, provided that: (1) the fee shall not exceed 25 cents per page for photocopies not exceeding 9 by 14 inches. This section shall not be construed to mandate the raising of fees when an agency in the past has charged less than 25 cents for such copies; (2) the fee for photocopies of records in excess of 9 x 14 inches shall not exceed the actual cost of reproduction; or (3) an agency has the authority to redact portions of a paper record and does so prior to disclosure of the record by making a photocopy from which the proper redactions are made.
NY.notes: Restates the § 87(1)(b)(iii)(1) ceiling (NY-0024) with local scope explicit, and adds the anti-minimum clause and oversized actual-cost ceiling. Instrument row for the § 87(1)(a)-(b) delegation to COOG general regulations.

NY.legal_concept: Advance payment of copying fee may be required
NY.atomic_rule: An agency may require that the fee for copying or reproducing a record be paid in advance of preparing the copy.
NY.trigger: A copying/reproduction fee applies to the request
NY.source_language: An agency may require that the fee for copying or reproducing a record be paid in advance of the preparation of such copy.
NY.notes: No dollar threshold and no percentage cap — full prepayment may be required at any amount, at agency discretion. Binds/authorizes state and local agencies alike (Part 1401 scope).

NY.atomic_rule: An agency may waive a fee in whole or in part when making copies of records available.
NY.trigger: Any fee otherwise chargeable for copies
NY.source_language: An agency may waive a fee in whole or in part when making copies of records available.
NY.notes: Bare permission — no grounds, no mandatory cases, no purpose statement, no written-denial or appeal mechanics specific to waiver anywhere in POL art. 6 or Part 1401. Waiver policy is left to the agency/city.

NY.atomic_rule: In determining actual reproduction cost, an agency may include the actual cost of the storage devices or media provided to the requester in complying with the request.
NY.trigger: A storage device or media (CD/DVD/USB etc.) is provided to the requester
NY.source_language: ii. the actual cost of the storage devices or media provided to the person making the request in complying with such request;
NY.notes: Gives § 87(1)(c)(ii) its own row (previously only referenced inside NY-0026's exception). Mirrored for local agencies at 21 NYCRR 1401.8(c)(ii). Actual cost of the device — no fixed media rates exist.

NY.legal_concept: Copy provided upon payment or offer to pay; free certification of correctness
NY.atomic_rule: Upon payment of, or offer to pay, the prescribed fee, the entity shall provide a copy of the record and shall certify to the correctness of the copy if so requested (or certify non-possession / not-found after diligent search).
NY.trigger: Requester pays or offers to pay the prescribed fee for a copy
NY.source_language: Upon payment of, or offer to pay, the fee prescribed therefor, the entity shall provide a copy of such record and certify to the correctness of such copy if so requested, or as the case may be, shall certify that it does not have possession of such record or that such record cannot be found after diligent search.
NY.notes: Statutory basis of the payment production gate: the copy-production duty attaches on payment OR offer to pay. Certification of correctness is a duty within the same clause and carries no fee (see 21 NYCRR 1401.8(a)(4), NY-9001).

NY.legal_concept: Mandatory electronic retrieval when less burdensome; fee limited to labor + media components
NY.atomic_rule: When an agency can retrieve or extract a record from a computer storage system with reasonable effort, or doing so takes less employee time than manual retrieval/redaction, it must do so electronically, and may then charge only the preparation-labor and storage-media components of actual cost.
NY.trigger: Requested record/data retrievable or extractable from a computer storage system
NY.source_language: When an agency has the ability to retrieve or extract a record or data maintained in a computer storage system with reasonable effort, or when doing so requires less employee time than engaging in manual retrieval or redactions from non-electronic records, the agency shall be required to retrieve or extract such record or data electronically. In such case, the agency may charge a fee in accordance with paragraph (c)(i) and (ii) above.
NY.source_authority: 21 NYCRR § 1401.8(d); see also N.Y. Pub. Off. Law § 89(3)(a)
NY.notes: Companion statutory clause (§ 89(3)(a)): programming necessary to retrieve and transfer a record 'shall not be deemed to be the preparation or creation of a new record'. Constrains labor.programming charges to the (c)(i)-(ii) components.

OH.legal_concept: 'At cost' means 'actual cost'; the office sets its copy fee by policy reflecting actual cost
OH.atomic_rule: The 'at cost' standard of R.C. 149.43(B) means 'actual cost'; a public office, in its sound discretion, may adopt a reasonable policy setting a fee for copies that reflects the actual costs involved in making a copy, unless the cost is otherwise set by statute.
OH.trigger: A public office charges for copies of public records.
OH.source_language: Although the court has not defined "at cost," it has been stated that a public office, in its sound discretion, may adopt a reasonable policy setting a fee for copies obtained from the public office, with the fee reflecting the actual costs involved in making a copy, unless the cost is otherwise set by statute. 1989 Ohio Atty.Gen.Ops. No. 89-073; cf. State ex rel. Nelson v. Fuerst (1993), 66 Ohio St.3d 47, 48, 607 N.E.2d 836, 838, where the court referred in dicta to "reasonable cost" in a public records case. Since the General Assembly could have, but failed to, specify "reasonable cost," we hold that R.C. 149.43(B) means "actual cost."
OH.source_authority: State ex rel. The Warren Newspapers, Inc. v. Hutson, 70 Ohio St.3d 619, 1994-Ohio-5, ¶ 25 (Ohio 1994)
OH.effective_status: Current (Supreme Court of Ohio, decided Oct. 26, 1994; still cited as controlling in the AG's 2026 Sunshine Laws Manual, ch. 2 § 12 n.174)
OH.notes: Municipal case (Warren police department). Confirms that the operative per-page value is set by the city's own policy under an actual-cost ceiling; Ohio has no statewide per-page rate. Cites 1989 OAG 89-073 (policy may set fee reflecting actual costs). Secondary type: Permission (city may adopt a fee policy).

OH.legal_concept: Employee labor / staff time not chargeable under 'at cost'
OH.atomic_rule: The cost chargeable for copies under R.C. 149.43(B) shall not include labor costs regarding employee time (search, review, or copying time); Ohio specifies no charge for search and/or review time.
OH.trigger: A public office computes the charge for copies of public records (any record type other than law-enforcement/prosecutor video records under R.C. 149.43(B)(1) para. 2).
OH.source_language: Ohio does not specify any charge for search and/or review time in R.C. 149.43. ... Since respondents are already compensated for performing their duties, and responding to public records requests is merely another duty, the cost set forth in R.C. 149.43(B) should not include labor costs regarding employee time. Respondents' policy to the contrary was inconsistent with that provision. Additionally, there is no evidence in the record that the charge of $5 per initial page of each separate file is tied to the actual copying costs.
OH.source_authority: State ex rel. The Warren Newspapers, Inc. v. Hutson, 70 Ohio St.3d 619, 1994-Ohio-5, ¶ 26 (Ohio 1994); syllabus: 'Copies of public records available at actual cost without charges for labor or employee time.'
OH.effective_status: Current (Supreme Court of Ohio 1994; restated in AG 2026 Sunshine Laws Manual ch. 2 § 12: 'Except in rare exceptions, the cost of employee time cannot be included in the cost of copies or of delivery.')
OH.notes: Ellipsis in source_language omits only the FOIA comparison and Florida quotation between the two operative sentences; the quoted sentences are verbatim. Statutory exception: video records of state/local law enforcement or prosecutors (OH-9011), where 'actual cost' expressly includes staff time and overhead, capped at $75/hour of video produced and $750 total (OH-0019). A reasonable private-contractor copying/extraction cost may be passed through (Gibbs v. Concord Twp. 2003-Ohio-1586; Gambill v. Opperman 2013-Ohio-761, per Manual n.177) — not opened this pass.

OH.legal_concept: Flat/minimum charge not tied to actual copying cost impermissible
OH.atomic_rule: A charge for copies that is not tied to the actual copying costs (e.g., a $5 charge for the initial page of each file) is inconsistent with the 'at cost' requirement.
OH.trigger: A public office's fee policy imposes a flat, minimum, or initial-page charge for copies.
OH.source_language: Additionally, there is no evidence in the record that the charge of $5 per initial page of each separate file is tied to the actual copying costs. See, e.g., State ex rel. Bonnell v. Cleveland (Aug. 26, 1993), Cuyahoga App. No. 64854, unreported, 1993 WL 335426 (court relied on stipulated evidence regarding actual per-page copying costs consisting of costs of toner, paper and copying time). Relator's third proposition is sustained.
OH.source_authority: State ex rel. The Warren Newspapers, Inc. v. Hutson, 70 Ohio St.3d 619, 1994-Ohio-5, ¶ 26 (Ohio 1994)
OH.effective_status: Current (Supreme Court of Ohio 1994; AG 2026 Manual n.174 summarizes: 'public office cannot charge $5 for initial page or for employee labor, but only for "actual cost" of final copies')
OH.notes: The court's finding was evidentiary (no evidence tying the $5 to cost) rather than a per-se rule; treat as: any minimum/flat charge must be supported by actual copying cost. Bonnell (cited) describes actual per-page cost components as toner, paper and copying time.

OH.legal_concept: Customized/compiled documents: no charge for employee labor or computer programming time
OH.atomic_rule: When a public office creates a customized document by coordinating and compiling information from its public records, the fee under R.C. 149.43(B) is limited to actual costs, exclusive of any charges for employee labor or computer programming time in preparation or production.
OH.trigger: A requester asks for a customized/compiled document (data extraction, custom report or map) generated from existing public records.
OH.source_language: For purposes of determining the fee that may be charged pursuant to R.C. 149.43(B) for a customized document created by coordinating and compiling information from public records, "at cost" means actual costs, exclusive of any charges for employee labor or computer programming time involved in either the preparation or actual production of the document.
OH.effective_status: Current (listed in the AG's 'Opinions Interpreting Ohio's Sunshine Laws' index; not overruled)
OH.notes: Opinion was addressed to a county prosecutor (county offices) but reasons from R.C. 149.43(B) and Hutson, which bind all public offices including municipalities; applicability to a city is by parity of reasoning (flag). Contrast R.C. 149.43(F) (Bureau of Motor Vehicles only): 'special extraction costs' incl. programming time plus 10% — state-agency-only, not a municipal rule.

OH.legal_concept: Postage / delivery / supplies chargeable at cost, in advance
OH.atomic_rule: A public office shall transmit copies by U.S. mail or any other means of delivery or transmission within a reasonable period, and may require the requester to pay in advance the cost of postage (mail) or the cost of delivery (other means) and the costs incurred for other supplies used in the mailing, delivery, or transmission.
OH.trigger: A requester asks that copies be transmitted by mail or another delivery/transmission method.
OH.source_language: Upon a request made in accordance with division (B) of this section and subject to division (B)(6) of this section, a public office or person responsible for public records shall transmit a copy of a public record to any person by United States mail or by any other means of delivery or transmission within a reasonable period of time after receiving the request for the copy. The public office or person responsible for the public record may require the person making the request to pay in advance the cost of postage if the copy is transmitted by United States mail or the cost of delivery if the copy is transmitted other than by United States mail, and to pay in advance the costs incurred for other supplies used in the mailing, delivery, or transmission.
OH.effective_status: Current (R.C. 149.43 as amended eff. Sept. 30, 2025, H.B. 96, 136th G.A.; a further amendment by H.B. 31, 136th G.A., eff. Sept. 7, 2026, is enacted-awaiting-effect and does not touch the fee/payment language)
OH.notes: AMENDS OH-0023 (whose source_language was a paraphrase, not the statute's text). Ceiling = actual cost of postage/delivery/supplies; no figure. Prepayment permitted (structural gate). AG Model Policy: no charge for e-mailed documents (OH-9016).

OH.legal_concept: Digital-delivery cap of ten records per month for offices with a free, fully searchable public website
OH.atomic_rule: A public office that provides some or all of its public records on a website that is fully accessible and searchable at all times (other than acts of God or maintenance) and charges no fee to search, access, download, or receive records there may limit to ten per month the number of records it will deliver in a digital format to a person, unless the records are not provided on the website and unless the person certifies in writing non-commercial use.
OH.trigger: Office has such a website AND a person's digital-delivery requests exceed ten in a month AND the records are on the website OR the person has not certified non-commercial use.
OH.source_language: A public office that chooses to provide some or all of its public records on a web site that is fully accessible to and searchable by members of the public at all times, other than during acts of God outside the public office's control or maintenance, and that charges no fee to search, access, download, or otherwise receive records provided on the web site, may limit to ten per month the number of records requested by a person that the office will deliver in a digital format, unless the requested records are not provided on the web site and unless the person certifies to the office in writing that the person does not intend to use or forward the requested records, or the information contained in them, for commercial purposes.
OH.effective_status: Current (R.C. 149.43 as amended eff. Sept. 30, 2025, H.B. 96, 136th G.A.; a further amendment by H.B. 31, 136th G.A., eff. Sept. 7, 2026, is enacted-awaiting-effect and does not touch the fee/payment language)
OH.notes: AMENDS/SUPERSEDES OH-0026: the 'ninety-five per cent' online-availability threshold in OH-0026 does NOT appear in the statute; the actual condition is a website 'fully accessible to and searchable by members of the public at all times' that 'charges no fee'. Both exceptions must be satisfied to lift the cap ('unless ... and unless').

OH.atomic_rule: For the (B)(7) delivery caps, 'commercial' is narrowly construed and does not include reporting or gathering news, reporting or gathering information to assist citizen oversight or understanding of government, or nonprofit educational research.
OH.trigger: Office applies the ten-per-month delivery cap and evaluates a requester's non-commercial-use certification.
OH.source_language: For purposes of division (B)(7) of this section, "commercial" shall be narrowly construed and does not include reporting or gathering news, reporting or gathering information to assist citizen oversight or understanding of the operation or activities of government, or nonprofit educational research.
OH.effective_status: Current (R.C. 149.43 as amended eff. Sept. 30, 2025, H.B. 96, 136th G.A.; a further amendment by H.B. 31, 136th G.A., eff. Sept. 7, 2026, is enacted-awaiting-effect and does not touch the fee/payment language)
OH.notes: Ohio has NO commercial-purpose fee surcharge for municipalities; commercial purpose matters only for the delivery caps (and for the BMV bulk-extraction schedule in (F), state-agency-only). Per AG Manual ch. 2 (citing 1990 OAG 90-050 and R.C. 149.43(B)(4)), intended commercial use is otherwise irrelevant.

OH.legal_concept: Law-enforcement/prosecutor video: prepayment of estimated actual cost may be required; production obligation begins on full payment
OH.atomic_rule: A state or local law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office may include in its public records policy a requirement that the requester pay the estimated actual cost before it begins preparing a video record; where it does, its obligation to produce the video or make it available for inspection begins once the estimated actual cost is paid in full.
OH.trigger: Request for a video record held by a state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office AND the office's policy requires prepayment.
OH.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'reasonable period of time' (copies) / 'promptly' (inspection) runs from full payment of the estimated actual cost
OH.source_language: A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office may include in its public records policy the requirement that a requester pay the estimated actual cost before beginning the process of preparing a video record for inspection or production. Where a state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office imposes such a requirement, its obligation to produce a video or make it available for inspection begins once the estimated actual cost is paid in full by the requester.
OH.effective_status: Current (video-record cost language added eff. April 9, 2025 by H.B. 315, 135th G.A.; carried unchanged in the Sept. 30, 2025 (H.B. 96) and Sept. 7, 2026 (H.B. 31) versions)
OH.notes: Municipal police departments are 'local law enforcement agenc[ies]'. The gate must be in the office's written public records policy. Charging for video is optional (AG Manual ch. 2 § 13). Clock: the production obligation is contingent on payment — before payment there is no running duty; the statute states no fixed day-count.

OH.legal_concept: Law-enforcement/prosecutor video: estimated actual cost within five business days
OH.atomic_rule: A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office shall provide the requester with the estimated actual cost of preparing a video record within five business days of receipt of the public records request.
OH.trigger: Receipt of a public records request for a video record by a state or local law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office.
OH.clock_spec: 5 business-days from receipt of the public records request (estimated actual cost to requester)
OH.source_language: A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office shall provide the requester with the estimated actual cost within five business days of receipt of the public records request.
OH.effective_status: Current (video-record cost language added eff. April 9, 2025 by H.B. 315, 135th G.A.; carried unchanged in the Sept. 30, 2025 (H.B. 96) and Sept. 7, 2026 (H.B. 31) versions)
OH.notes: Statute text is unconditional ('shall provide'); the AG Manual reads it as applying where prepayment is required ('If prepayment is required, the agency must provide a cost estimate within five business days'). Record-specific; no general estimate deadline exists for other records.

OH.legal_concept: Law-enforcement/prosecutor video: overrun collectible only with advance notice and capped at 20% of estimate
OH.atomic_rule: If the actual cost of a video record exceeds the estimated actual cost, the agency may charge the difference upon fulfilling the request only if the requester was notified in advance that the actual cost may be up to twenty per cent higher than the estimate, and shall not charge a difference exceeding twenty per cent of the estimated actual cost.
OH.trigger: Actual cost of preparing a video record exceeds the estimate given to the requester.
OH.source_language: If the actual cost exceeds the estimated actual cost, a state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office may charge a requester for the difference upon fulfilling a request for video records if the requester is notified in advance that the actual cost may be up to twenty per cent higher than the estimated actual cost. A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office shall not charge a requester a difference that exceeds twenty per cent of the estimated actual cost.
OH.effective_status: Current (video-record cost language added eff. April 9, 2025 by H.B. 315, 135th G.A.; carried unchanged in the Sept. 30, 2025 (H.B. 96) and Sept. 7, 2026 (H.B. 31) versions)
OH.notes: ceiling: 20% of the estimated actual cost (overrun); plus a required advance notice (secondary type: Requirement). Combined with the $750 total cap (OH-0019). No revised-estimate mechanism; no such rule for non-video records.

OH.legal_concept: Law-enforcement/prosecutor video: 'actual cost' includes staff time and overhead
OH.atomic_rule: For video records only, 'actual cost' means all costs incurred by the state or local law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office in reviewing, blurring or otherwise obscuring, redacting, uploading, or producing the video, including the storage medium, staff time, and any other relevant overhead necessary to comply with the request.
OH.trigger: Charge computed for preparing a video record for inspection or production by a state or local law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office.
OH.source_language: As used in this division, "actual cost," with respect to video records only, means all costs incurred by the state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office in reviewing, blurring or otherwise obscuring, redacting, uploading, or producing the video records, including but not limited to the storage medium on which the record is produced, staff time, and any other relevant overhead necessary to comply with the request.
OH.effective_status: Current (video-record cost language added eff. April 9, 2025 by H.B. 315, 135th G.A.; carried unchanged in the Sept. 30, 2025 (H.B. 96) and Sept. 7, 2026 (H.B. 31) versions)
OH.notes: The one statutory exception to Ohio's no-labor rule (OH-9002). Bounded by OH-0019 ($75 per hour of VIDEO PRODUCED — not per staff hour — and $750 total). AG Manual ch. 2 § 13: charges must reflect documentable actual costs; a flat uniform per-hour rate 'may fail to reflect the actual costs and could be challenged'.

OH.legal_concept: Law-enforcement/prosecutor video: no fee for victims (or their counsel/insurer) on affidavit
