OH.atomic_rule: A state or local law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office shall not charge a fee for preparing or copying a video record when the requester is a victim (Ohio Const. art. I § 10a, or a tort victim under R.C. 2307.011) who reasonably asserts the video relates to the act or omission that caused the harm, or the victim's legal counsel or insurer; the fee may only be waived upon receipt of an affidavit by the victim or counsel identifying that the video will be used to investigate harm or damages captured on it.
OH.trigger: Video-record request by a qualifying victim, victim's legal counsel (with retention agreement/letter of representation), or victim's insurer, accompanied by the required affidavit.
OH.source_language: A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office shall not charge a fee for preparing a video record for inspection, or producing a copy of a video record, when the requester of the video record is a victim, as defined in Ohio Constitution, Article I, Section 10a, or who is a victim who suffered loss and could seek remedy through a tort action as defined by section 2307.011 of the Revised Code, who reasonably asserts that the video recording relates to the act or omission that caused the victim's harm or loss, or who is the legal counsel or insurer of the victim. A fee under this section may only be waived upon the receipt of an affidavit by the victim or the victim's legal counsel identifying that the use of the video is to investigate harm or damages that may have been captured on the video.
OH.effective_status: Current (division (B)(11) added eff. Sept. 30, 2025, H.B. 96, 136th G.A.; carried unchanged in the Sept. 7, 2026 (H.B. 31) version)
OH.notes: Mandatory waiver (Prohibition on charging) gated on an affidavit — the only fee-waiver rule in Ohio's Public Records Act. 'Legal counsel of the victim' is defined in the same division (attorney producing a signed retention agreement or letter of representation). No general fee-waiver grounds exist for other records; discretionary waivers are a matter of local policy.

OH.legal_concept: No duty to furnish copies without payment
OH.atomic_rule: A public office has no obligation to provide free copies to a requester who cannot or will not pay the cost of copies.
OH.trigger: Requester declines or fails to pay the (advance) cost of copies.
OH.source_language: There is no obligation to provide free copies to someone who cannot or will not pay.
OH.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, 2026 Ohio Sunshine Laws: An Open Government Resource Manual, ch. 2, § 12 'Copies, and delivery or transmission, "at cost"' (pp. 21-22), citing State ex rel. Call v. Fragale, 2004-Ohio-6589, ¶ 6; State ex rel. Dehler v. Mohr, 2011-Ohio-959, ¶ 3
OH.effective_status: Current (2026 edition of the AG manual, opened; underlying decisions not opened this pass)
OH.notes: Guidance restating case law; the underlying opinions (Fragale; Dehler) were not opened — flag manual verification of the holdings. No statutory withdrawal period (N days) exists; the request simply is not fulfilled until payment.

OH.legal_concept: Notice of amount due must precede any denial for nonpayment
OH.atomic_rule: Before denying a request for failure to pay, the public office must first inform the requester of the amount due.
OH.trigger: Office intends to withhold copies because the requester has not paid.
OH.source_language: However, before denying a request for failure to pay, the public office must first inform the requester of the amount due.
OH.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, 2026 Ohio Sunshine Laws: An Open Government Resource Manual, ch. 2, § 12 'Copies, and delivery or transmission, "at cost"' (pp. 21-22), citing State ex rel. Ware v. City of Akron, 2021-Ohio-624, ¶ 13-15
OH.effective_status: Current (2026 edition of the AG manual, opened; Ware v. Akron not opened this pass)
OH.notes: A required cost notice with no dollar threshold — the notice is due whenever payment is a precondition. Ware v. Akron (municipal) per the manual: office complied when it identified the cost of copies and offered copies upon payment. Flag: verify holding text in the opinion.

OH.legal_concept: AG Model Public Records Policy: per-page and per-disc charges are fill-in values under 'actual cost, not labor'
OH.atomic_rule: The AG's model policy (which public offices may use under R.C. 149.43(E)(2)) provides that requesters may be charged only the actual cost of making copies, not labor, with the office's paper per-page charge and per-disc charge entered as its own values.
OH.trigger: A public office adopts its public records policy and sets its copy charges.
OH.source_language: Those seeking public records may be charged only the actual cost of making copies, not labor. The charge for paper copies is [X] cents per page. The charge for electronic files downloaded to a compact disc is [X] per disc.
OH.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, Model Public Records Request Policy (developed under R.C. 109.43(E)), 'Copying and Mailing Costs'
OH.effective_status: Current (undated model; posted on the AG site; opened 2026-08-19)
OH.notes: Confirms defers-to-city under an actual-cost ceiling: '[X] cents per page' and '[X] per disc' are placeholders the office fills in. Guidance, not law; the AG model is optional ('may obtain guidance from the model'). Model is undated — flag manual verification of currency.

OH.legal_concept: AG Model Policy: delivery at actual cost; no charge for e-mailed documents
OH.atomic_rule: Per the AG model policy, a requester who asks for delivery may be charged the actual cost of postage and mailing supplies or other actual costs of delivery, and there is no charge for e-mailed documents.
OH.trigger: Requester asks for delivery of copies (mail, other carrier, or e-mail).
OH.source_language: If a requester asks that documents be delivered to them, he or she may be charged the actual cost of the postage and mailing supplies, or other actual costs of delivery. There is no charge for e-mailed documents.
OH.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, Model Public Records Request Policy, 'Copying and Mailing Costs'
OH.notes: The 'no charge for e-mailed documents' line is guidance consistent with 'at cost' (no incremental cost); the statute (B)(7)(a) itself only authorizes actual delivery/supply costs.

OH.legal_concept: Motor-vehicle accident report copy: nonrefundable $4 fee (or county-approved amount); photos/electronic formats extra
OH.atomic_rule: The law enforcement agency that submitted an accident report shall furnish a copy of the report and associated documents to a person claiming an interest arising out of the accident (or the person's attorney) upon payment of a nonrefundable fee of four dollars, or the amount approved by the board of county commissioners under division (B); photographs or other electronic formats are charged in addition (above $4 only if county-approved).
OH.trigger: Request for a copy of a motor-vehicle accident report (submitted under R.C. 5502.11) by a person claiming an interest arising out of the accident or their attorney.
OH.source_language: The law enforcement agency that submitted a report shall furnish a copy of such report and associated documents to any person claiming an interest arising out of a motor vehicle accident, or to the person's attorney, upon the payment of a nonrefundable fee of four dollars or the amount approved by the board of county commissioners of the county in which the law enforcement agency is located as provided in division (B) of this section. The cost of photographs or any other electronic format shall be in addition to the nonrefundable four-dollar fee for the accident report, whether the report was submitted by the state highway patrol or another law enforcement agency. A law enforcement agency may charge a fee that is in excess of four dollars for photographs and other electronic formats if such a fee is approved by a board of county commissioners of the county in which the law enforcement agency is located as provided in division (B) of this section.
OH.effective_status: Current (eff. July 17, 2009, H.B. 1, 128th G.A.; no later amendment shown on codes.ohio.gov)
OH.notes: Binds every submitting 'law enforcement agency', including municipal police. Listed by the AG Manual as an exception to 'at cost' (Manual ch. 2 § 12; a specific fee statute controls over the general 'at cost' rule, R.C. 1.51). Scope limited to interested persons; whether a non-interested requester may obtain the report 'at cost' under 149.43 is not addressed — flag.

OH.legal_concept: Public records policy may not cap records per person or per period, nor impose a fixed response wait
OH.atomic_rule: Except as otherwise provided in R.C. 149.43 (e.g., the (B)(7) delivery caps), a public office's public records policy may not limit the number of public records it will make available to a single person, may not limit the number it will make available during a fixed period of time, and may not establish a fixed period of time before responding unless that period is less than eight hours.
OH.trigger: Public office adopts or applies its public records policy to a requester's volume or timing of requests.
OH.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the policy may not limit the number of public records that the public office will make available to a single person, may not limit the number of public records that it will make available during a fixed period of time, and may not establish a fixed period of time before it will respond to a request for inspection or copying of public records, unless that period is less than eight hours.
OH.effective_status: Current (R.C. 149.43 as amended eff. Sept. 30, 2025, H.B. 96, 136th G.A.; a further amendment by H.B. 31, 136th G.A., eff. Sept. 7, 2026, is enacted-awaiting-effect and does not touch the fee/payment language)
OH.notes: Relevant to 'repeat/aggregated requests': Ohio permits no per-requester aggregation cap or fee aggregation; the only volume rule is the ten-per-month DELIVERY cap for commercial-purpose requesters. Concept key proposed (no existing key fits).

OH.atomic_rule: Public offices generally may not charge requesters for inspecting public records (including inspection of records posted online).
OH.trigger: Requester chooses to inspect rather than obtain copies.
OH.source_language: Generally, public offices may not charge requesters for inspecting public records.
OH.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, 2026 Ohio Sunshine Laws Manual, ch. 2 § 11 'Inspection at no cost during regular business hours' (p. 21), citing R.C. 149.43(B)(1) and 2014 Ohio Atty.Gen.Ops. No. 009
OH.notes: The statute states 'at cost' only for copies; the manual (and 2014 OAG 009, county auditor website) states the corollary that inspection carries no charge. Guidance restating statute/opinion.

OK.legal_concept: Advance payment of estimated fees when estimated cost exceeds $75
OK.atomic_rule: A public body may require advance payment of the estimated fees when the estimated cost of responding to the request exceeds $75.00.
OK.trigger: Estimated cost of responding to the request exceeds Seventy-five Dollars ($75.00).
OK.source_language: A public body may require advance payment of the estimated fees authorized under this section when the estimated cost exceeds Seventy-five Dollars ($75.00) or if the requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests.
OK.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4), as amended by Laws 2025, SB 535, c. 404, § 2
OK.effective_status: Current — effective November 1, 2025 (Laws 2025 SB 535); carried unchanged by Laws 2026 SB 2184 c. 217 § 72 (emerg. eff. 5/6/2026)
OK.notes: New provision post-dating the prior OK discovery pass. One sentence carries two independent triggers; split per the grain rule — the prior-debt trigger is OK-9003. Verified verbatim in the OSCN 2026 codified print AND in enrolled SB 535 (oklegislature.gov ENR PDF, underlined new language). Binds all public bodies including municipalities (§ 24A.3(2) 'public body' includes city, town).

OK.legal_concept: Mandatory refund of advance payment exceeding actual response costs
OK.atomic_rule: Any portion of an advance payment that exceeds the costs of responding to the request must be returned to the requestor.
OK.trigger: An advance payment was collected and exceeds the actual costs of responding to the request.
OK.source_language: Any portion of an advance payment that exceeds the costs of responding to the request shall be returned to the requestor.
OK.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4), as amended by Laws 2025, SB 535, c. 404, § 2
OK.notes: Close-out reconciliation duty whenever an advance payment was taken under OK-9001/OK-9003. No deadline stated for the refund.

OK.legal_concept: Advance payment may be required of a requestor with outstanding fees from previous requests
OK.atomic_rule: A public body may require advance payment of the estimated fees for a request, regardless of amount, if the requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests.
OK.trigger: Requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests.
OK.source_language: A public body may require advance payment of the estimated fees authorized under this section when the estimated cost exceeds Seventy-five Dollars ($75.00) or if the requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests.
OK.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4), as amended by Laws 2025, SB 535, c. 404, § 2
OK.notes: Second trigger of the SB 535 advance-payment sentence, split from OK-9001 per the grain rule. Requires a per-requestor outstanding-fees ledger to execute (cross-request state — relevant to the repeat/aggregated item). Not amount-gated.

OR.legal_concept: Petition to Attorney General or district attorney on unreasonable denial of fee waiver or reduction
OR.atomic_rule: A requester who believes a fee waiver or fee reduction was unreasonably denied may petition the Attorney General or the district attorney in the same manner as a requester petitions when inspection of a public record is denied; the AG, DA and court have the same authority as in a denial-of-inspection petition.
OR.trigger: Requester believes there has been an unreasonable denial of a fee waiver or fee reduction under ORS 192.324(5)
OR.source_language: A requester who believes that there has been an unreasonable denial of a fee waiver or fee reduction may petition the Attorney General or the district attorney in the same manner as a requester who petitions when inspection of a public record is denied under ORS 192.311 to 192.478. The Attorney General, the district attorney and the court have the same authority in instances when a fee waiver or reduction is denied as when inspection of a public record is denied.
OR.notes: The waiver-denial appeal path missing from the existing corpus (OR-0023's notes referenced reviewability but no row carried it). AG petitions route to the AG for state agencies and to the DA for local bodies under the 192.411/192.415 pattern; either way the review right binds cities. A waiver denial also starts the 60-day payment clock (OR-0025).

OR.legal_concept: Ordered fee waiver or reduction as remedy for undue delay or failure to respond
OR.atomic_rule: If the AG, DA or a court grants a petition under ORS 192.407, the order MAY require a fee waiver or fee reduction where the public body responded to the request with undue delay or failed to respond in the time and manner prescribed in ORS 192.329; a reviewing body may also find an unreasonable waiver denial on other grounds.
OR.trigger: Petition under ORS 192.407 granted after public body's undue delay or failure to respond as prescribed by ORS 192.329
OR.source_language: If the Attorney General, the district attorney or a court grants a petition filed under this section, the order granting the petition: (a) May require disclosure of nonexempt material responsive to the request within seven days, or within any other period that the Attorney General, district attorney or court concludes is appropriate to comply with ORS 192.329; (b) May require the public body to pay a penalty of $200 to the requester if the Attorney General, district attorney or court determines that the public body responded to the request with undue delay or failed to respond to the request; and (c) May order a fee waiver or a fee reduction if a public body has responded to the request with undue delay or has failed to respond to the request in the time and manner prescribed in ORS 192.329. Nothing in this subsection prohibits a reviewing body from finding an unreasonable denial of a fee waiver or a fee reduction on other grounds.
OR.notes: Oregon's fee-forfeiture-on-late-response analogue: discretionary and remedial (requires a petition and an order), never self-executing. The $200 penalty in (3)(b) is a remedy amount (out of engine scope under the V1/V2 Remove list) — retained here only because it rides in the same operative sentence; the operative engine fact is the orderable waiver in (3)(c).

OR.legal_concept: Carve-out fee regimes for records filed with the Secretary of State or a county clerk
OR.atomic_rule: Notwithstanding the actual-cost fee rules of ORS 192.324(4)(a)-(c), fees for records filed with the Secretary of State under ORS ch. 79A or ORS 81.230–81.263 are those set by Secretary of State rule, and fees for copies of records filed with a county clerk are those established under ORS 205.320.
OR.trigger: Requested public records are those filed with the Secretary of State (ORS ch. 79A / 81.230–81.263) or with a county clerk
OR.source_language: Notwithstanding paragraphs (a) to (c) of this subsection, when the public records are those filed with: (A) The Secretary of State under ORS chapter 79A or ORS 81.230 to 81.263, the fees for furnishing copies, summaries or compilations of the public records are the fees established by the Secretary of State by rule under ORS chapter 79A or ORS 81.230 to 81.263. (B) A county clerk, the fees for copies of records are the fees established under ORS 205.320.
OR.notes: NOT municipal authority — neither branch applies to city-held records; recorded because it bounds the reach of OR-0020/OR-0022. Delegation (B) followed: ORS 205.320 (opened, 2025 c.31 §2 current) fixes county-clerk figures — copies 25 cents/page plus not more than $3.75 for locating a record; official certificate $3.75; recording $5/page. Delegation (A) (SoS UCC-type filings) deliberately not pursued: no municipal item depends on it.

OR.legal_concept: Public body must publish written request procedure including fee amounts and manner of calculation
OR.atomic_rule: A public body shall make available to the public a written public-records-request procedure that includes the name(s) and address(es) of the individual(s) to whom requests may be sent and the amounts of and manner of calculating the fees the body charges for responding to requests.
OR.trigger: None stated (standing duty of every public body)
OR.source_language: A public body shall make available to the public a written procedure for making public records requests that includes: (a) The name of one or more individuals within the public body to whom public records requests may be sent, with addresses; and (b) The amounts of and the manner of calculating fees that the public body charges for responding to requests for public records.
OR.notes: The statutory hook that makes every fee value in Oregon a CITY-published figure: the state supplies the standard and the $25/60-day machinery, the city must publish its own amounts and calculation method. Also the anchor for the 5-business-day acknowledgment duty (192.324(2) keys on the individual identified in this procedure). Platform surface: published fee-schedule page.

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — black-and-white copy ceiling, tiered at 1,000 copies
PA.atomic_rule: Under the OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule an agency may charge up to $0.25 per black-and-white copy for the first 1,000 copies and up to $0.20 per copy beyond 1,000; a 'copy' is one side of a sheet of 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 paper.
PA.trigger: Requester seeks black-and-white paper copies
PA.source_language: Black & White Copies (first 1,000) — Up to $0.25 per copy. Black & White Copies (beyond 1,000) — Up to $0.20 per copy. A "copy" is either a single-sided copy, or one side of a double-sided copy, on 8.5"x11" or 8.5"x14" paper.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Delegated instrument under § 1307(b)(1)(i). Amends PA-0040: PA-0040's source language was a paraphrase and its authority line said 'adopted Dec. 30, 2024' — the OOR web page says Dec. 30, 2024 while the PDF header says Dec. 30, 2022; flag for verification. 'Up to' = ceiling; the city sets its operative rate under it. Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii). § 1307(b)(3) allows local-agency fees to reflect regional price differences, but the OOR schedule publishes a single uniform ceiling.

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — color copy ceiling
PA.atomic_rule: An agency may charge up to $0.50 per color copy; a requester may ask for black-and-white copies even if the original is in color.
PA.trigger: Requester seeks color paper copies
PA.source_language: Color Copies — Up to $0.50 per copy. A "copy" is either a single-sided copy, or one side of a double-sided copy, on 8.5"x11" or 8.5"x14" paper. Note that a requester may ask for black and white copies even if the original is in color and color copies are available.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: No volume tier for color. Secondary concept fee.nonstandard_rate. Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — specialized documents at actual cost
PA.atomic_rule: For specialized documents, including non-standard sized documents and blueprints, an agency may charge up to actual cost.
PA.trigger: Requester seeks copies of non-standard sized documents, blueprints or similar specialized documents
PA.source_language: Specialized Documents — Up to actual cost. Including, but not necessarily limited to, non-standard sized documents and blueprints.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Actual-cost ceiling; no dollar figure. Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — no fee for records delivered by e-mail or other electronic method
PA.atomic_rule: No additional fee may be imposed for records delivered via e-mail or other electronic method; if redaction cannot be done securely by electronic means the agency may print, redact, scan and charge the B&W or color copy fee for those pages.
PA.trigger: Records delivered electronically
PA.source_language: Records Delivered via Email or Other Electronic Method — No additional fee may be imposed. If a requester asks to receive records which require redactions in electronic format and the agency is unable to securely redact the records by electronic means, an agency may print the records to provide for secure redaction, then scan them in for delivery by email. Accordingly, the agency may charge the fees noted above for either B&W or color copies, as appropriate.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Consistent with OOR Advisory Opinion of Mar. 26, 2009 (Charging for Electronically Transmitted Public Records): 'When a document already exists in electronic format and can be attached to an email, it is not permissible to charge for copies, because none were required to be made in order to fulfill the request.' Secondary concept fee.electronic_media_charge. Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — CD/DVD, flash drive and other media
PA.atomic_rule: An agency may charge up to actual cost for a CD or DVD, not to exceed $1.00 per disc; up to actual cost for a flash drive; and up to actual cost for other media.
PA.trigger: Records duplicated onto physical electronic media
PA.source_language: CD / DVD — Up to actual cost, not to exceed $1.00 per disc. Flash Drive — Up to actual cost. Other Media — Up to actual cost.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Dollar ceiling only for optical discs; flash drives and other media are actual-cost. Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — facsimile at actual cost
PA.atomic_rule: An agency may charge up to actual cost for transmitting records by facsimile; if it must print records to fax them it may charge the B&W copy fee.
PA.trigger: Records transmitted by facsimile
PA.source_language: Facsimile — Up to actual cost. If an agency must print records to send them by facsimile, the agency may charge the fees noted above for B&W copies.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — no fee for redaction
PA.atomic_rule: No additional fee may be imposed for redaction; if the agency cannot securely redact electronically it may copy or print the records to redact and charge the B&W or color copy fee for those copies.
PA.trigger: Records require redaction
PA.source_language: Redaction — No additional fee may be imposed. If a requester seeks records requiring redaction and the agency is unable to securely redact the records by electronic means, an agency may copy or print the records to provide for secure redaction. Accordingly, the agency may charge the fees noted above for either B&W or color copies, as appropriate.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Also: 'Inspection of Redacted Records ... An agency may not charge the requester for the redaction itself ... If, after inspecting the records, the requester chooses to obtain the copies, no additional fee may be charged.' Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — conversion of electronic record to paper
PA.atomic_rule: An agency may charge up to $0.25 per page to convert an electronically maintained record to paper, subject to the § 1307(d) lesser-of rule unless the requester specifically asks for the more expensive medium.
PA.trigger: Requester asks for a paper copy of a record maintained only electronically or in other non-paper media
PA.source_language: Conversion to Paper — Up to $0.25 per page. If a record is only maintained electronically or in other non-paper media, duplication fees shall be limited to the lesser of the fee for duplication on paper or the fee for duplication in the original media, unless the requester specifically requests for the record to be duplicated in the more expensive medium. See §1307(d).
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — no fee for requester photographing a record
PA.atomic_rule: No additional fee may be imposed when a requester photographs a record with the requester's own camera; if redaction copies must be made before access the copy fee applies to those copies.
PA.trigger: Requester photographs records during inspection
PA.source_language: Photographing a Record — No additional fee may be imposed. This assumes the requester is using his or her own camera, such as a cellphone camera, to photograph the records. See Muenz v. Township of Reserve, OOR Dkt. AP 2015-1021, 2015 PA O.O.R.D. LEXIS 1176. If redaction is required prior to the requester being granted access to photograph records and the agency is unable to securely redact the records by electronic means, an agency may copy or print the records to provide for secure redaction. Accordingly, the agency may charge the fees noted above for either B&W or color copies, as appropriate.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — postage at actual cost of USPS first-class
PA.atomic_rule: An agency may charge postage up to the actual cost of USPS first-class postage.
PA.trigger: Records mailed to requester
PA.source_language: Postage — Up to actual cost of USPS first-class postage.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Implements § 1307(a) (PA-0038) and narrows 'actual cost of mailing' to first-class postage. Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — certification of a record, OOR-recommended maximum $5 per record
PA.atomic_rule: The OOR schedule lists certification at up to $5.00 per record and states that the OOR recommends no more than $5 per record; certification fees do not include notarization fees.
PA.trigger: Requester asks for a certified copy
PA.source_language: Certification of a Record — Up to $5.00 per record. Under the RTKL, an agency may impose "reasonable fees for official certification of copies if the certification is at the behest of the requester and for the purpose of legally verifying the public record." The OOR recommends no more than $5 per record to certify a public record. Certification fees do not include notarization fees.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Certification fees are governed by § 1307(c) ('reasonable fees'), which does not delegate fee-setting to the OOR; the schedule's own footnote calls the $5 a recommendation. Treated as advisory guidance on the statutory soft standard, not a binding ceiling — manual verification. Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — no fee for search, retrieval, staff time or the response letter
PA.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for searching for or retrieving records; an agency may not charge staff time or salary for complying with a request; no fee may be charged for the agency's response letter.
PA.trigger: Any request
PA.source_language: Fee Limitations: Except as otherwise provided by statute, the RTKL states that no other fees may be imposed unless the agency necessarily incurs costs for complying with the request, and such fees must be reasonable. No fee may be imposed for an agency’s review of a record to determine whether the record is a public record subject to access under the RTKL. No fee may be charged for searching for or retrieval of documents. An agency may not charge staff time or salary for complying with a RTK request. No fee may be charged for an agency’s response letter.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Statute text (§ 1307(g)) bars only review fees expressly; the categorical bar on search/retrieval and staff time is the OOR's published construction of § 1307(g), applied by the OOR as the appeals body for Commonwealth and local agencies. Labor is therefore not chargeable at all for municipalities. Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: No other fees unless necessarily incurred, and reasonable
PA.atomic_rule: Except as otherwise provided by statute, no fees other than those in § 1307 may be imposed unless the agency necessarily incurs costs for complying with the request, and such fees must be reasonable.
PA.trigger: Agency contemplates a charge not listed in § 1307 / the OOR schedule
PA.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by statute, no other fees may be imposed unless the agency necessarily incurs costs for complying with the request, and such fees must be reasonable.
PA.source_authority: 65 P.S. § 67.1307(g) (first sentence)
PA.effective_status: Current (no amendment to § 1307 through Act 29 of 2023; none found for 2024–2026)
PA.notes: PA-0042 carries only the second sentence of § 1307(g); this row carries the first. No request-level dollar cap exists in the RTKL.

PA.legal_concept: All applicable fees must be paid to receive access
PA.atomic_rule: All applicable fees shall be paid in order for the requester to receive access to the requested record.
PA.trigger: Fees are due on a request
PA.source_language: All applicable fees shall be paid in order to receive access to the record requested.
PA.effective_status: Current
PA.notes: OOR schedule adds: 'Once the request is fulfilled and prepared for release, the OOR recommends that the agency obtain payment prior to releasing the records.' Prepayment of an estimate is separately permitted by § 1307(h) when expected fees exceed $100 (PA-0046).

PA.legal_concept: Refusal to pay applicable fees is a ground for a 30-day extension; deemed denial thereafter
PA.atomic_rule: If the requester refuses to pay applicable fees, the open-records officer may extend the response time by written notice within five business days; if the expected response date is more than 30 days after the five business days the request is deemed denied unless the requester agrees in writing to the extension.
PA.trigger: Requester refuses to pay applicable fees authorized by the act
PA.clock_spec: up to 30 calendar-days beyond the 5 business-day response period from receipt by the open-records officer; deemed denied the day after the noticed date if not answered
PA.source_language: (a) Determination.--Upon receipt of a written request for access, the open-records officer for an agency shall determine if one of the following applies: ... (6) the requester refuses to pay applicable fees authorized by this act; ... (b) Notice.-- (1) Upon a determination that one of the factors listed in subsection (a) applies, the open-records officer shall send written notice to the requester within five business days of receipt of the request for access under subsection (a). (2) The notice shall include a statement notifying the requester that the request for access is being reviewed, the reason for the review, a reasonable date that a response is expected to be provided and an estimate of applicable fees owed when the record becomes available. If the date that a response is expected to be provided is in excess of 30 days, following the five business days allowed for in section 901, the request for access shall be deemed denied unless the requester has agreed in writing to an extension to the date specified in the notice. (3) If the requester agrees to the extension, the request shall be deemed denied on the day following the date specified in the notice if the agency has not provided a response by that date.
PA.effective_status: Current
PA.notes: This is the RTKL's only clock effect tied to nonpayment: nonpayment does not toll the clock; it is an extension ground with a hard 30-day outer limit absent written agreement.

PA.legal_concept: Extension notice must include an estimate of applicable fees
PA.atomic_rule: Every § 902 extension notice must include an estimate of the applicable fees that will be owed when the record becomes available.
PA.trigger: Open-records officer sends a § 902 extension notice
PA.source_language: The notice shall include a statement notifying the requester that the request for access is being reviewed, the reason for the review, a reasonable date that a response is expected to be provided and an estimate of applicable fees owed when the record becomes available.
PA.effective_status: Current
PA.notes: No dollar or hour threshold triggers an estimate; the estimate is a required element of any extension notice. The $100 figure in § 1307(h) is a prepayment threshold, not an estimate-notice threshold.

PA.legal_concept: Unretrieved copies may be disposed of after 60 days; fees paid retained
PA.atomic_rule: If the agency's response states that copies are available for delivery at its office and the requester fails to retrieve them within 60 days of the response, the agency may dispose of the unretrieved copies and retain any fees paid to date.
PA.trigger: Response says copies available at agency office; requester does not retrieve within 60 days
PA.clock_spec: 60 days from the agency's response (statute says 'days'; not stated as business days)
PA.source_language: If an agency response to a requester states that copies of the requested records are available for delivery at the office of an agency and the requester fails to retrieve the records within 60 days of the agency's response, the agency may dispose of any copies which have not been retrieved and retain any fees paid to date.
PA.effective_status: Current
PA.notes: Trigger is failure to retrieve (which includes failure to pay, since § 901 conditions access on payment). Discretionary ('may dispose').

PA.legal_concept: Access may be withheld until fees owed from an earlier request are paid
PA.atomic_rule: An agency may process a new request but withhold access until all applicable fees, including fees owed for earlier requests (even where the earlier copies were never retrieved), are paid; it must still respond or issue an extension notice within five business days and should state the past-due fees as a reason in its response.
PA.trigger: Requester owes fees from a prior RTKL request
PA.source_language: In Department of Transportation v. Drack, 42 A.3d 355, 363 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2012), the Commonwealth Court held that, when a requester "owes money for an agency’s fulfillment of an earlier request ... Section 901 of the RTKL permits an agency to process the request but to withhold access to the request until all applicable fees, including fees for earlier requests, are paid" ... Based on the pertinent language in Drack in conjunction with Sections 901 and 905 of the RTKL, it can be discerned that agencies may deny access to records sought in RTKL requests based on a requester’s outstanding fees stemming from a prior RTKL request. This would apply even where the requester never retrieved the records, because the agency, in responding to the prior request, had been required to produce physical copies of the requested records. However, even if fees are owed in response to a prior RTKL request, agencies must still timely process future RTKL requests. ... Further, if an agency chooses to deny a request due to fees owed as a result of a prior request, the agency should raise all applicable reasons for denying access, including the fact that past due fees are owed, in its response.
PA.source_authority: OOR Advisory Opinion, Jan. 12, 2016 (Requiring Payment When A Requester Has Not Retrieved Records From A Prior Request), applying Dep't of Transp. v. Drack, 42 A.3d 355 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2012), 65 P.S. §§ 67.901, 67.905
PA.effective_status: Current (advisory; OOR states advisory opinions are not binding and may be superseded)
PA.notes: Scanned PDF read via OCR — quotation transcribed from the OCR text; verify against the PDF image. The same opinion notes (footnote 1) that fees set in an agency response may be appealed to the OOR within 15 business days under § 1101 (citing Prison Legal News v. OOR, 992 A.2d 942 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2010)).

PA.legal_concept: Complex data sets may be priced at market value, except for news media and nonprofit educational research
PA.atomic_rule: For complex and extensive data sets (e.g., GIS or integrated property assessment lists) copying fees may be based on the reasonable market value of the same or closely related data sets, but not for a request by a person employed by or connected with a news organization for publication/broadcast or by a nonprofit organization for educational research, whose fees remain subject to the ordinary duplication rules.
PA.trigger: Request for a complex and extensive data set
PA.source_language: (4) The following apply to complex and extensive data sets, including geographic information systems or integrated property assessment lists. (i) Fees for copying may be based on the reasonable market value of the same or closely related data sets. (ii) Subparagraph (i) shall not apply to: (A) a request by an individual employed by or connected with a newspaper or magazine of general circulation, weekly publication, press association or radio or television station, for the purpose of obtaining information for publication or broadcast; or (B) a request by a nonprofit organization for the conduct of educational research. (iii) Information obtained under subparagraph (ii) shall be subject to paragraphs (1), (2) and (3).
PA.effective_status: Current
PA.notes: The RTKL's only purpose-sensitive fee rule; there is no commercial-purpose surcharge, and § 703 / § 1308(2) bar requiring a statement of purpose. Secondary concept fee.commercial_charge (inverse: exemption for media/nonprofit-educational requesters). See also OOR § 1307(e) approvals list for county GIS/assessment data fees.

PA.legal_concept: All schedule fees may be waived at the agency's discretion
PA.atomic_rule: All fees established in the OOR schedule may be waived at the discretion of the agency.
PA.trigger: Agency elects to waive fees
PA.source_language: Fees May Be Waived: All fees established herein may be waived at the discretion of the agency.
PA.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
PA.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
PA.notes: Extends § 1307(f) (duplication-fee waiver, PA-0043) to every schedule fee. No mandatory waiver ground, no purpose statement (barred by § 703 / § 1308(2)). Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

PA.legal_concept: Enhanced electronic access user fees — permitted methods, must be reasonable, OOR-approved, no exclusion or profit
PA.atomic_rule: If an agency offers enhanced electronic access beyond the inspection/duplication access the act requires, it may set user fees for that access (flat rate, subscription, per-transaction, cumulative-time or other reasonable method), but the fees must be reasonable, must be approved by the Office of Open Records, and may not be set with the intent or effect of excluding persons from access or creating profit for the agency.
PA.trigger: Agency offers optional enhanced electronic access
PA.source_language: The user fees for enhanced electronic access may be a flat rate, a subscription fee for a period of time, a per-transaction fee, a fee based on the cumulative time of system access or any other reasonable method and any combination thereof. The user fees for enhanced electronic access must be reasonable, must be approved by the Office of Open Records and may not be established with the intent or effect of excluding persons from access to records or duplicates thereof or of creating profit for the agency.
PA.source_authority: 65 P.S. § 67.1307(e) (second and third sentences)
PA.effective_status: Current
PA.notes: Amends PA-0045, which quoted only the first sentence and omitted the OOR pre-approval requirement. OOR publishes an Enhanced Electronic Access Fee Application Form and a list of approvals (e.g., Berks County delinquent tax data, Oct. 9, 2025). Not a general programming/labor rate — approvals are agency-specific.

PA.legal_concept: Fees set in an agency response may be appealed to the OOR within 15 business days
PA.atomic_rule: A requester may appeal the fees set forth in an agency's response to the Office of Open Records within 15 business days under § 1101.
PA.trigger: Agency response imposes fees the requester disputes
PA.clock_spec: 15 business-days from the agency response (§ 1101 appeal window)
PA.source_language: The OOR notes that the Requester in this scenario could appeal the fees set forth in the agency’s response within 15 business days pursuant to 65 P.S. § 67.1101. See Prison Legal News v. Office of Open Records, 992 A.2d 942 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2010); State Employees’ Ret. Sys. v. Office of Open Records, 10 A.3d 358 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2010).
PA.source_authority: OOR Advisory Opinion, Jan. 12, 2016, n.1 (citing 65 P.S. § 67.1101 and Prison Legal News v. OOR, 992 A.2d 942 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2010))
PA.effective_status: Current (advisory)
PA.notes: OCR-transcribed from a scanned PDF; verify against the image. Proposed concept key appeal.administrative.fee_dispute (no fee/payment key fits a fee-appeal path).

PA.legal_concept: OOR Advisory Opinion — no per-page charge for e-mailing a record that already exists electronically
PA.atomic_rule: When a document already exists in electronic format and can be attached to an e-mail, an agency may not charge for copies; a copy charge is permissible only where the agency had to duplicate the original on a traditional copier (e.g., copying a bound volume in order to scan it), because fees are based on actual out-of-pocket expenses for paper, toner, etc.
PA.trigger: Requester asks for records by e-mail attachment
PA.source_language: When a document already exists in electronic format and can be attached to an email, it is not permissible to charge for copies, because none were required to be made in order to fulfill the request. However, in the example you provided — a request for a collective bargaining agreement - it would be appropriate to charge for copies if a bound volume is copied and then a PDF or other attachment is made from scanning those copies. In that instance, the agency has incurred the expense of copying the bound volume in order to make a document capable of being scanned, attached to an email and transmitted electronically. It is only permissible to charge for copies if it is required to duplicate the original using a traditional copier as fees are based upon actual out-of-pocket expenses for paper, toner, etc.
PA.source_authority: OOR Advisory Opinion, Mar. 26, 2009 (Charging for Electronically Transmitted Public Records)
PA.effective_status: Current (advisory; the OOR schedule now states the rule directly)
PA.notes: Scanned PDF read via OCR — verify against the image. Superseded in practice by the schedule line 'Records Delivered via Email or Other Electronic Method — No additional fee may be imposed' (PA-9004); retained because it states the actual-out-of-pocket rationale.

PA.legal_concept: Duplication fees for Commonwealth and local agencies are established by the Office of Open Records; reasonable, based on prevailing local rates; may reflect regional differences
PA.atomic_rule: Fees for duplication (photocopying, printing from electronic media or microfilm, copying onto electronic media, facsimile/electronic transmission and other duplication) by Commonwealth and local agencies are established by the Office of Open Records, must be reasonable and based on prevailing fees for comparable duplication services provided by local business entities, and for local agencies may reflect regional price differences.
PA.trigger: Requester seeks duplication of records
PA.source_language: (1) Fees for duplication by photocopying, printing from electronic media or microfilm, copying onto electronic media, transmission by facsimile or other electronic means and other means of duplication shall be established: (i) by the Office of Open Records, for Commonwealth agencies and local agencies; (ii) by each judicial agency; and (iii) by each legislative agency. (2) The fees must be reasonable and based on prevailing fees for comparable duplication services provided by local business entities. (3) Fees for local agencies may reflect regional price differences.
PA.effective_status: Current (no amendment to § 1307 through Act 29 of 2023; none found for 2024–2026)
PA.notes: Amends PA-0039 (which was a paraphrase flagged for manual verification) with the verbatim delegation clause. Delegation followed to the OOR schedule (PA-9001 et seq.). Municipalities cannot exceed the OOR schedule ceilings; the schedule itself does not publish regional variants.

SC.legal_concept: Public-interest fee waiver/reduction is discretionary; clause reaches local governmental bodies (AG reading)
SC.atomic_rule: A finding that disclosure is in the public interest, supporting a fee waiver or reduction under § 30-4-30(B), is discretionary on the part of the agency; a requestor might not be granted a waiver or reduction, and the AG reads the undefined term 'agency' as likely applying to local governmental bodies as well as state bodies.
SC.trigger: Requester seeks waiver or reduction of fees on public-interest grounds
SC.source_language: However, finding that a disclosure is in the public interest is discretionary on the part of the agency and the requestor might not be granted a waiver or reduction from the fee schedule. [footnote 1:] Because the term "agency" is not modified in S.C. Code Ann. § 30-4-30(B), a court may well hold it applies to state bodies as well as local governmental bodies, including school districts.
SC.source_authority: Op. S.C. Att'y Gen. to Rep. Forrest & Councilman Hudson (June 28, 2019), construing S.C. Code Ann. § 30-4-30(B)
SC.notes: Advisory only; SC AG opinions are not binding. Adds the applies_to judgment (local bodies covered) and the discretionary character; the operative statutory clause is SC-0015. Also confirms the General Assembly-member exception is not extended to other legislative bodies.

SC.legal_concept: Fees for a record the public body elects to create are governed by § 30-4-30(B)
SC.atomic_rule: A public body is not required to create a record that does not exist by extracting information from other documents, but may create such a document for a requestor if it chooses; the fees it may charge for doing so are governed by § 30-4-30(B).
SC.trigger: Requester asks for a compilation/extraction/transcript that does not exist and the body elects to create it
SC.source_language: The public body is not required to create a record where the record does not otherwise exist by extracting information from other documents which are in the possession of the public body. On the other hand, the public body may create such a document for a requestor if it chooses; the fees which may be charged by the public body for doing so would be governed by §30-4-30(b).
SC.source_authority: Op. S.C. Att'y Gen. (June 28, 2019), quoting Op. S.C. Att'y Gen., 1996 WL 190741 (Mar. 5, 1996)
SC.effective_status: Current (advisory; 1996 opinion restated 2019 under the post-2017 statute)
SC.notes: Advisory. Ties programming/data-extraction and transcript work to the § 30-4-30(B) fee clauses without naming which clause (staff-time conversion vs. search/retrieval salary cap vs. copy ceiling) — flagged for manual verification on labor.programming.rate and dup.specialty.rate.

TN.legal_concept: Prior-debt bar: no further requests need be honored until unpaid copies are paid
TN.atomic_rule: If a requestor fails to pay for copies after they were produced, the governmental entity is not required to comply with any further public records request from that person until the copies are paid for, provided an estimate was given under (a)(7)(B)(ii) before production and the person agreed to pay it.
TN.trigger: Copies produced; requestor was given an estimate, agreed to pay it, and then failed to pay.
TN.source_language: (b) If a person makes a request for copies of a public record and, after copies have been produced, the person fails to pay to the governmental entity the cost for producing such copies, the governmental entity is not required to comply with any public records request from the person until the person pays for such copies; provided, that the person was provided with an estimated cost for producing the copies in accordance with subdivision (a)(7)(B)(ii) prior to producing the copies and the person agreed to pay the estimated cost for such copies.
TN.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
TN.notes: No statutory withdrawal window (no 'withdrawn after N days'); the consequence is a bar on FUTURE requests until the debt is paid. Conditioned on a prior estimate the requestor agreed to. OORC FAQ (official) restates the same clause. Statute text taken verbatim from FindLaw's reproduction of Tenn. Code Ann. (current through Jan. 2, 2024); the official Lexis-hosted TCA could not be opened by the research tooling. Currency cross-checked against OORC Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 Legislative Updates (no amendment to the fee/estimate/payment provisions of § 10-7-503 in the 2024 or 2025 sessions) and the OORC FAQ (official) which quotes the same clauses. Confirm against the official TCA before library entry.

TN.legal_concept: Model-policy blank: no duplication cost below a dollar/page floor set by the entity
TN.atomic_rule: The OORC Model Public Records Policy leaves to the governmental entity an optional provision that no duplication costs will be charged for requests below a dollar amount or page count the entity fills in.
TN.trigger: Entity adopts the optional de-minimis/free-page clause in its policy.
TN.source_language: E. [No duplication costs will be charged for requests for less than [$][# of pages.]
TN.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.E
TN.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017, amended Aug. 16, 2017 (version posted on OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19).
TN.notes: Bracketed template text: the state supplies no number; the entity supplies both whether and the figure. Same blank serves a free-page allowance (# of pages) and a de-minimis dollar floor ($). Applies to every entity using the model (county/municipal policies required by § 10-7-503(g)(1)).

TN.legal_concept: Model-policy blank: advance payment required when estimated costs exceed an entity-set dollar amount
TN.atomic_rule: The OORC Model Public Records Policy provides that payment in advance will be required when costs are estimated to exceed a dollar amount the governmental entity fills in.
TN.trigger: Estimated charges exceed the entity's adopted prepayment threshold.
TN.source_language: G. Payment in advance will be required [when costs are estimated to exceed $______].
TN.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.G
TN.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017, amended Aug. 16, 2017 (version posted on OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19).
TN.notes: State sets no threshold; Schedule § I.E and Model Policy § VI.B independently permit prepayment of the (itemized) estimate before production regardless of amount. Entity chooses whether to use a threshold and its value.

TN.legal_concept: Model-policy waiver clause: waiver below an entity-set amount, approval above it, aggregated fees non-waivable option
TN.atomic_rule: The OORC Model Public Records Policy offers a waiver clause under which fees not exceeding an entity-set dollar amount may be waived, waiver requests above a second amount go to a designated official who decides whether waiver is in the entity's best interest and for the public good, and (optionally) fees on aggregated requests will not be waived.
TN.trigger: Requestor seeks waiver / entity applies its waiver clause.
TN.source_language: C. When fees for copies and labor do not exceed $_____, the fees may be waived. [Requests for waivers for fees above $_____ must be presented to _______________, who is authorized to determine if such waiver is in the best interest of [Name of Governmental Entity] and for the public good.][Fees associated with aggregated records requests will not be waived].
TN.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.C
TN.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017, amended Aug. 16, 2017 (version posted on OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19).
TN.notes: Discretionary; grounds ('best interest ... and for the public good') are the model's, not statutory; no purpose statement, written-denial or appeal requirement exists in state law for waiver decisions. OORC Best Practices § III.C lists advisory waiver factors (number of copies, dollar amount, record type, accessibility, public-interest dissemination).

TN.legal_concept: Delivery: presumption of in-person pickup; USPS First-Class Mail obligatory once actual delivery cost paid; other means discretionary at cost
TN.atomic_rule: Copies are presumed to be picked up in person; if the requestor chooses not to and has paid (or the policy waives) the actual cost of delivery plus other permitted charges, the custodian must deliver by USPS First-Class Mail; delivery by other means (including electronic) and its costs are within the custodian's discretion.
TN.trigger: Requestor elects not to retrieve copies in person.
TN.source_language: C. It is presumed copies of requested records will be provided in person to a requestor when the requestor returns to the records custodian's office to retrieve the records. D. If a requestor chooses not to personally retrieve records and the actual cost of delivering the copies, in addition to any other permitted charges, have been paid by the requestor or otherwise waived pursuant to the public records policy, then a records custodian is obligated to deliver the copies via USPS First-Class Mail. It is within the discretion of a records custodian to agree to deliver copies of records through other means, including electronically, and to assess the costs related to such delivery.
TN.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § III.C–D
TN.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017 (submitted to ACOG Nov. 8, 2016). Verified still posted as the operative schedule on the OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19; no revision published despite § 8-4-604(a)(1)(B) 'revised at least annually'.
TN.notes: Actual cost of delivery (postage) — no fixed handling fee. OORC FAQ (official): a requestor cannot be required to retrieve in person; 'the governmental entity is required to mail the records after receiving payment for the cost of delivering the public records.' § 8-4-604(a)(1)(A)(i) directs the schedule to consider 'the costs of mailing the documents if the requestor is not returning to retrieve the requested documents.'

TN.legal_concept: Electronic records: per-page charge only when new paper copies had to be produced (e.g., printed to redact)
TN.atomic_rule: When providing electronic records, a records custodian may charge per-page costs only when paper copies that did not already exist had to be produced in responding to the request, such as when a record must be printed to be redacted.
TN.source_language: When providing electronic records, a records custodian may charge per-page costs only when paper copies that did not already exist are required to be produced in responding to the request, such as when a record must be printed to be redacted.
TN.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § III.B (second sentence)
TN.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017 (submitted to ACOG Nov. 8, 2016). Verified still posted as the operative schedule on the OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19; no revision published despite § 8-4-604(a)(1)(B) 'revised at least annually'.
TN.notes: OORC FAQ (official) restates: for copies of electronic records an entity 'may only assess a per-page charge for paper copies that must be produced ... labor charges ... and its out-of-pocket costs for flash drives or other storage devices'; no charge may be assessed for inspecting electronic records.

TN.legal_concept: No charge to view/inspect a public record unless otherwise required by law
TN.atomic_rule: A governmental entity shall not assess a charge to view a public record unless otherwise required by law; therefore copy and labor charges attach only to requests for copies.
TN.trigger: Request to inspect/view (as opposed to copy).
TN.source_language: (7)(A)(i) A governmental entity shall not require a written request or assess a charge to view a public record unless otherwise required by law.
TN.source_authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(i); OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.A ('Records custodians may not charge for inspection of public records except as provided by law.')
TN.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
TN.notes: Bounds WHEN labor is chargeable: only in producing copies (Schedule § IV.B 'labor' = time to produce requested records). OORC FAQ: if a copy request is converted to inspection-only, no inspection-related costs may be charged; a staff member sitting with an inspecting requestor may not be charged for. Statute text taken verbatim from FindLaw's reproduction of Tenn. Code Ann. (current through Jan. 2, 2024); the official Lexis-hosted TCA could not be opened by the research tooling. Currency cross-checked against OORC Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 Legislative Updates (no amendment to the fee/estimate/payment provisions of § 10-7-503 in the 2024 or 2025 sessions) and the OORC FAQ (official) which quotes the same clauses. Confirm against the official TCA before library entry.

TN.legal_concept: OORC schedule is a guideline a custodian 'may use'; OORC policies are not UAPA rules
TN.atomic_rule: The Office of Open Records Counsel shall establish a schedule of reasonable charges that a records custodian may use as a guideline to charge a citizen requesting copies; the schedule shall be revised at least annually; the OORC policies and guidelines are not rules under the Uniform Administrative Procedures Act.
TN.source_language: (a) The office of open records counsel shall establish: (1)(A) A schedule of reasonable charges that a records custodian may use as a guideline to charge a citizen requesting copies of public records pursuant to title 10, chapter 7, part 5. ... (B) The schedule established pursuant to subdivision (a)(1)(A) shall be revised at least annually; (2) A separate policy related to reasonable charges that a records custodian may charge for frequent and multiple requests for public records; (3) A safe harbor policy for a records custodian who adheres to the policies and guidelines established by the office of open records counsel; ... (c) The policies and guidelines shall not be deemed to be rules under the Uniform Administrative Procedures Act, compiled in title 4, chapter 5.
TN.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
TN.notes: This is the delegation the fee figures flow through: § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)(i) → § 8-4-604 → OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges. Because the schedule is a 'guideline' with a documented-actual-cost escape (Schedule § II.C), its per-page figures are safe-harbor ceilings rather than hard statutory caps. Statute text taken verbatim from FindLaw's reproduction of Tenn. Code Ann. (current through Jan. 2, 2024); the official Lexis-hosted TCA could not be opened by the research tooling. Currency cross-checked against OORC Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 Legislative Updates (no amendment to the fee/estimate/payment provisions of § 10-7-503 in the 2024 or 2025 sessions) and the OORC FAQ (official) which quotes the same clauses. Confirm against the official TCA before library entry.

TN.legal_concept: Safe harbor: fees per adopted policy consistent with the OORC Schedule are presumed reasonable
TN.atomic_rule: Labor fees and copy charges are presumed reasonable if set forth in the entity's public records policy and developed in accordance with the OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges; aggregation charges likewise if developed under the Frequent and Multiple Requests policy.
TN.trigger: Entity charges fees under an adopted policy consistent with OORC guidelines.
TN.source_language: Any labor fees and charges related to copying or duplicating public records are presumed reasonable if the fees and charges are set forth in the governmental entity's public records policy and such fees and charges were developed in accordance with the provisions of the Schedule of Reasonable Charges. The aggregation of frequent and multiple requests for copies of public records and any fees and charges resulting from aggregation are presumed to be reasonable if the fees and charges are set forth in the governmental entity's public records policy and such fees and charges were developed in accordance with the provisions of the Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests Policy.
TN.source_authority: OORC Safe Harbor Policy (Tenn. Code Ann. § 8-4-604(a)(3))
TN.notes: Explains why the schedule's 'up to' figures operate as ceilings for practical purposes: exceeding them forfeits the presumption unless actual cost is documented (Schedule § II.C).

TN.legal_concept: Commercial-value GIS/geographic data: additional development-cost recovery fee capped at 10% (10–20% with approvals); not chargeable to individuals for themselves; news media at reproduction cost
TN.atomic_rule: For a copy request for a public record that has commercial value and requires reproduction of a publicly funded computer-generated map or similar geographic data, a state agency or political subdivision may impose reasonable additional fees tied to actual development costs, limited to 10% of total development costs (10–20% only with governing-body and ISC approval); such fees may not be assessed against individuals requesting for themselves or when the record lacks commercial value; news media may be charged cost of reproduction only.
TN.trigger: Copy request for commercial-value GIS/geographic data developed with public funds.
TN.source_language: (c)(1) If a request is made for a copy of a public record that has commercial value, and such request requires the reproduction of all or a portion of a computer generated map or other similar geographic data that was developed with public funds, a state department or agency or a political subdivision of the state having primary responsibility for the data or system may establish and impose reasonable fees for the reproduction of such record, in addition to any fees or charges that may lawfully be imposed pursuant to this section. The additional fees authorized by this subsection (c) may not be assessed against individuals who request copies of records for themselves or when the record requested does not have commercial value. State departments and agencies and political subdivisions of the state may charge a reasonable fee (cost of reproduction only) for information requested by the news media for news gathering purposes (broadcast or publication). ... (3) The development cost recovery set forth above shall be limited to not more than ten percent (10%) of the total development costs unless additional development cost recovery between ten percent (10%) and twenty percent (20%) is approved by the following procedures: ... For political subdivisions of the state, approval for additional development cost recovery as contained in a proposed business plan must be obtained from the governing legislative body. If the governing legislative body approves additional development cost recovery, such recovery shall be submitted to the ISC for approval. ... (4) As used in this subsection (c), "record that has commercial value" means a record requested for any purpose other than: (A) A non-business use by an individual; and (B) A news gathering use by the news media.
TN.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
TN.notes: AMENDS TN-0049 (which flagged § 10-7-506(c) as unopened): the enumerated fee is confined to commercial-value GIS/geographic-data reproductions; there is no general commercial-purpose surcharge and standard copy/labor charges do not vary by purpose (Schedule § I.F). Recovery of maintenance costs is not subject to the 10%/20% limits. Statute text taken verbatim from FindLaw's reproduction of Tenn. Code Ann. (current through Jan. 2, 2024); the official Lexis-hosted TCA could not be opened by the research tooling. Currency cross-checked against OORC Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 Legislative Updates (no amendment to the fee/estimate/payment provisions of § 10-7-503 in the 2024 or 2025 sessions) and the OORC FAQ (official) which quotes the same clauses. Confirm against the official TCA before library entry.

TN.legal_concept: Municipal policy must state fees for copies and billing/payment procedures
TN.atomic_rule: Every county and municipal governmental entity must have a written public records policy adopted by its governing authority that includes a statement of any fees charged for copies and the procedures for billing and payment, and must not impose requirements more burdensome than state law.
TN.source_language: (g)(1) No later than July 1, 2018, every county and municipal governmental entity subject to this section shall establish a written public records policy properly adopted by the appropriate governing authority. The public records policy shall not impose requirements on those requesting records that are more burdensome than state law and shall include: ... (C) A statement of any fees charged for copies of public records and the procedures for billing and payment; ...
TN.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
TN.notes: The statutory hook for every 'defers_to_city' resolution in this pass: fee amounts, waiver, prepayment thresholds, payment forms and aggregation are set in the locally adopted policy (Schedule § I.B: 'Charges for copies of public records must be pursuant to a public records policy properly adopted by the governing authority'). State agencies instead promulgate UAPA rules under (g)(2) — a separate regime. Statute text taken verbatim from FindLaw's reproduction of Tenn. Code Ann. (current through Jan. 2, 2024); the official Lexis-hosted TCA could not be opened by the research tooling. Currency cross-checked against OORC Fall 2024 and Fall 2025 Legislative Updates (no amendment to the fee/estimate/payment provisions of § 10-7-503 in the 2024 or 2025 sessions) and the OORC FAQ (official) which quotes the same clauses. Confirm against the official TCA before library entry.

TN.legal_concept: No charge may be collected until an estimate of reasonable charges has been provided
TN.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may not charge for the costs of providing copies until an estimate of reasonable charges has been provided to the requestor.
TN.trigger: Copies produced/charges assessed without a prior estimate.
TN.source_language: A governmental entity may not charge for the costs associated with providing copies of public records until an estimate of reasonable charges is provided to the requestor.
TN.source_authority: OORC Tennessee Public Records Act FAQs, 'What if a governmental entity does not provide an estimate of costs?' (applying Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)(ii))
TN.effective_status: Current (OORC FAQ page, no revision date shown; opened 2026-08-19)
TN.notes: Guidance interpretation of the statutory estimate duty; combined with § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(vii)(b) (bar applies only where the requestor 'agreed to pay the estimated cost'), an overrun beyond the agreed estimate is not covered by the nonpayment bar. No explicit revised-estimate rule exists.

TN.legal_concept: Notice of aggregation and right to appeal to OORC when threshold met
TN.atomic_rule: When the aggregation threshold is met, a custodian choosing to aggregate must inform the requestor(s) of the determination and of their right to appeal the decision to the OORC; disputes regarding aggregation are brought to the OORC.
TN.trigger: Aggregation threshold reached and custodian elects to aggregate.
TN.source_language: B. When the aggregation threshold is met, a records custodian choosing to aggregate requests must inform the requestor(s) of the determination to aggregate and of the right of the requestor(s) to appeal the records custodian's decision to aggregate to the OORC. ... D. Disputes regarding aggregation shall be brought to the OORC.
TN.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § II.B, II.D
TN.notes: Required notice + administrative appeal path (OORC) attached to the aggregation decision.

TN.legal_concept: Routinely released, readily accessible records exempt from aggregation
TN.atomic_rule: Requests for current records that are routinely released and readily accessible, such as agendas or meeting minutes, are exempt from the aggregation policy.
TN.trigger: Request is for routinely released, readily accessible current records.
TN.source_language: C. Requests for current records that are routinely released and readily accessible, such as agendas or meeting minutes, are exempt from this policy.
TN.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § II.C
TN.notes: Model Policy § VI.I.2.c has the entity list its excluded routine records.

TN.legal_concept: Policy must specify the level (entity / agency / department / office) at which requests are aggregated
TN.atomic_rule: A governmental entity's public records policy shall specify the level at which records requests will be aggregated — for the entire entity or by agency, department, office, or otherwise.
TN.source_language: E. A governmental entity's public record policy shall specify the level at which records requests will be aggregated, whether for the entire governmental entity or by agency, department, office, or otherwise.
TN.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.E
TN.notes: Aggregation is optional (policy purpose: 'It is within the discretion of each governmental entity to charge for frequent and multiple record requests').

TN.legal_concept: Best practice: full or partial prepayment of estimated charges when duplication costs are significant; segment payment with segmented production; prepay vendor cost
