WA.atomic_rule: An agency may add a customized service charge, up to the actual cost of the services, only when the request requires IT expertise for data compilations or customized electronic access not used for other agency purposes, and only after notice to the requestor with an explanation, a description of the expertise, a reasonable cost estimate, and an opportunity to amend the request.
WA.trigger: Request requires information technology expertise to prepare data compilations or provide customized electronic access services not used by the agency for other agency purposes.
WA.source_language: (3)(a)(i) In addition to the charge imposed for providing copies of public records and for the use by any person of agency equipment copying costs, an agency may include a customized service charge. A customized service charge may only be imposed if the agency estimates that the request would require the use of information technology expertise to prepare data compilations, or provide customized electronic access services when such compilations and customized access services are not used by the agency for other agency purposes. (ii) The customized service charge may reimburse the agency up to the actual cost of providing the services in this subsection. (b) An agency may not assess a customized service charge unless the agency has notified the requestor of the customized service charge to be applied to the request, including an explanation of why the customized service charge applies, a description of the specific expertise, and a reasonable estimate cost of the charge. The notice also must provide the requestor the opportunity to amend his or her request in order to avoid or reduce the cost of a customized service charge.
WA.notes: Amends WA-0029, which carried only a paraphrase flagged 'Requires manual verification' — verbatim text now confirmed from the owner-supplied official 42.56.120 page (fetched 2026-08-20). The deposit base includes this charge (120(4)).

WA.legal_concept: Installment charging; unclaimed installment ends duty
WA.atomic_rule: An agency providing a request on a partial or installment basis may charge for each part as it is provided; if an installment is not claimed or reviewed, the agency is not obligated to fulfill the balance of the request.
WA.trigger: Request produced on a partial or installment basis; an installment goes unclaimed or unreviewed.
WA.clock_spec: terminal: duty to fulfill the balance ends when an installment is not claimed or reviewed (no statutory day count)
WA.source_language: If an agency makes a request available on a partial or installment basis, the agency may charge for each part of the request as it is provided. If an installment of a records request is not claimed or reviewed, the agency is not obligated to fulfill the balance of the request.
WA.notes: Amends WA-0032 (was a paraphrase flagged 'Requires manual verification'); verbatim confirmed from the owner-supplied official text. No grace-period day count — that is a local-policy choice.

WA.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver per agency rules
WA.atomic_rule: An agency may waive any charge assessed for a request, pursuant to the agency's own rules and regulations.
WA.trigger: Agency elects to waive a charge under its adopted rules.
WA.source_language: An agency may waive any charge assessed for a request pursuant to agency rules and regulations.
WA.notes: Express delegation of waiver grounds to agency (city) rules — fully discretionary; no statutory grounds, purpose test, written-denial duty, or waiver appeal.

WA.legal_concept: Alternative fee arrangement for voluminous or frequent requests
WA.atomic_rule: An agency may enter into a contract, memorandum of understanding, or other agreement with a requestor providing an alternative fee arrangement to the statutory charges, including in response to a voluminous or frequently occurring request.
WA.trigger: Requestor and agency agree to alternative fee terms; or the request is voluminous or frequently occurring.
WA.source_language: An agency may enter into any contract, memorandum of understanding, or other agreement with a requestor that provides an alternative fee arrangement to the charges authorized in this section, or in response to a voluminous or frequently occurring request.
WA.notes: WA's only repeat/aggregated-requestor fee mechanism — negotiated, not formulaic. Mapped to fee.aggregation as the closest canonical concept (it is the frequent-requestor fee treatment).

WA.legal_concept: No fee for inspection or locating records
WA.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for the inspection of public records or for locating public documents and making them available for copying, except for body-worn-camera redaction costs (RCW 42.56.240(14)) and the customized service charge (RCW 42.56.120(3)).
WA.trigger: Requestor inspects records, or agency locates records and makes them available for copying.
WA.source_language: No fee shall be charged for the inspection of public records or locating public documents and making them available for copying, except as provided in RCW 42.56.240(14) and subsection (3) of this section.
WA.notes: Fixed at zero: search/retrieval and inspection labor categorically non-chargeable. This is the rule that makes labor.search.rate not_applicable in WA.

WA.legal_concept: Summary of charges on request before copying
WA.atomic_rule: If a requestor asks, the agency shall provide a summary of the applicable charges before any copies are made, and the requestor may revise the request to reduce the number of copies and the charges.
WA.trigger: Requestor asks for a summary of applicable charges.
WA.source_language: A requestor may ask an agency to provide, and if requested an agency shall provide, a summary of the applicable charges before any copies are made and the requestor may revise the request to reduce the number of copies to be made and reduce the applicable charges.
WA.notes: On-request duty with no dollar threshold — WA's version of the cost-notice gate. Restated in AG model rule WAC 44-14-07001(5) (advisory guidance).

WA.atomic_rule: A law enforcement or corrections agency may require a requester not exempt under RCW 42.56.240(14)(e) to pay the reasonable costs of redacting or obscuring portions of a body-worn-camera recording before disclosure, only to the extent required by applicable exemptions, using the least costly commercially available redaction method to the extent possible and reasonable.
WA.trigger: Request for body worn camera recordings from a law enforcement or corrections agency by a requester not listed in RCW 42.56.240(14)(e).
WA.source_language: A law enforcement or corrections agency responding to a request to disclose body worn camera recordings may require any requester not listed in (e) of this subsection to pay the reasonable costs of redacting, altering, distorting, pixelating, suppressing, or otherwise obscuring any portion of the body worn camera recording prior to disclosure only to the extent necessary to comply with the exemptions in this chapter or any applicable law.
WA.notes: The exception RCW 42.56.120(1) points to. Applies to law-enforcement/corrections agencies only (municipal police included). Exempt requesters per (14)(e): persons directly involved in the incident, their attorneys, and certain others. (14)(f)(iii): redaction time does not count against any local time/cost allocation for records responses. Section amended through 2026 c 174; text extracted from the official RCW page via retrieval tool (two consistent fetches) — flag for verify-pass confirmation against certified text.

WA.legal_concept: Cost statement adopted only after notice and public hearing
WA.atomic_rule: An agency's statement of actual copying costs (and the factors and manner used to determine them) may be adopted only after providing notice and a public hearing.
WA.trigger: Agency adopts or amends its statement of actual costs for copies.
WA.source_language: Each agency may establish, maintain, and make available for public inspection and copying a statement of the actual costs that it charges for providing photocopies or electronically produced copies, of public records and a statement of the factors and manner used to determine the actual costs. Any statement of costs may be adopted by an agency only after providing notice and public hearing.
WA.notes: Adoption-procedure gate on the city's own fee schedule; WA-0027 quoted only the first sentence — the notice-and-hearing sentence is the operative addition here. Verbatim from the certified 7/15/2026 PDF.

WA.legal_concept: Copy-and-send staff time includable in actual costs
WA.atomic_rule: Staff time to copy and send the requested public records may be included in an agency's actual copying costs; staff salaries, benefits, and general overhead otherwise may not be included unless directly related to the actual cost of copying.
WA.trigger: Agency calculates its actual costs for providing copies.
WA.source_language: In determining the actual costs for providing copies of public records, an agency may not include staff salaries, benefits, or other general administrative or overhead charges, unless those costs are directly related to the actual cost of copying the public records. Staff time to copy and send the requested public records may be included in an agency's costs.
WA.notes: The only generally chargeable labor in WA: copy-and-send time, folded into the published actual-cost calculation (no standalone hourly rate). Verbatim from the certified 7/15/2026 PDF; the final sentence was absent from WA-0028.

WA.legal_concept: Actual cost of media, container, and postage
WA.atomic_rule: Under the default schedule, an agency may charge the actual cost of any digital storage media or device it provides, the actual cost of any container or envelope used to mail the copies, and the actual postage or delivery charge.
WA.trigger: Copies are provided on agency-supplied media or mailed to the requestor.
WA.source_language: The actual cost of any digital storage media or device provided by the agency, the actual cost of any container or envelope used to mail the copies to the requestor, and the actual postage or delivery charge.
WA.notes: Basis is 'actual cost' passed through (no numeric ceiling). Charges under 120(2)(b) may be combined when more than one type applies (120(2)(c)). Covers both the media item (CD/DVD/USB) and mail delivery.

WI.legal_concept: Law enforcement audio/video redaction fee (verbatim, certified text)
WI.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of redacting recorded audio/video content; staff rate = pay rate of the authority's lowest paid employee capable of performing the task
WI.atomic_rule: A law enforcement agency may impose a fee for the actual, necessary and direct cost of redacting recorded audio or video content to the extent redaction is legally required; the fee is barred where an individual requester certifies non-financial-gain use AND has made no more than 10 A/V requests to that authority that calendar year, where the requester is directly involved in the event (or their attorney/representative/parent/guardian), or where the event is an officer-involved shooting; the staff-time rate must be based on the lowest-paid capable employee; and no fee may be imposed unless a written estimate was provided before fulfilling the request.
WI.trigger: A law enforcement agency redacts recorded audio or video content to respond to a request
WI.source_language: 2. Subject to subds. 3. to 7., an authority that is a law enforcement agency may impose a fee upon a requester for the actual, necessary, and direct cost of redacting, whether by pixelization or other means, recorded audio or video content to the extent redaction is necessary to comply with applicable constitutional, statutory, or common law. 3. An authority may not impose the fee under subd. 2. with respect to a request for records containing audio or video content for which all of the following apply: a. If the requester is an individual, the requester provides written certification to the authority that the requester will not use the audio or video content for financial gain, not including an award of damages in a civil action. Any individual providing a false certification under this subd. 3. a. shall be subject to a forfeiture of $10,000 for each violation. b. During the calendar year in which the authority receives the request, the same requester has not made more than 10 requests to the authority for records containing audio or video content, including the current request but excluding any request subject to subd. 4. or 5. 4. An authority may not impose the fee under subd. 2. with respect to a request for records containing audio or video content if the requester is an individual directly involved in the event to which the requested records relate, that individual’s attorney or other authorized representative, or that individual’s parent or guardian if the individual is under the age of 18. 5. An authority may not impose the fee under subd. 2. with respect to a request for records containing audio or video content if the event to which the requested records relate is a shooting involving an officer of a law enforcement agency. 6. In calculating the fee imposed under subd. 2., the rate for an actual, necessary, and direct charge for staff time spent redacting shall be based on the pay rate of the authority’s lowest paid employee capable of performing the task. 7. An authority may not impose the fee under subd. 2. with respect to a request for records containing audio or video content unless prior to fulfilling the request the authority provides to the requester in writing an estimate of the amount of the fee to be charged.
WI.effective_status: Current (certified 2023-24 Wisconsin Statutes through 2025 Wis. Act 247, published 2026-08-05)
WI.notes: AMENDS WI-0041, which was is_paraphrase=true and flagged for manual verification of exact text and effective status: the certified statutes (published 2026-08-05, through 2025 Act 247) resolve both. Text is codified and current; § 19.35 history line ends at 2023 a. 253. Narrow exception to WI-0033's general no-redaction-fee rule. 'Law enforcement agency' per § 19.36(8)(a)2. ((3)(h)1.), which includes municipal police.

WI.legal_concept: Computer-run cost chargeable as copying fee, not location fee
WI.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction (computer-run cost treated as copying)
WI.atomic_rule: The cost of a computer run may be imposed on a requester as a copying fee, but not as a location fee.
WI.trigger: Responding to a request requires a computer run
WI.source_language: Copying fees, but not location fees, may be imposed on a requester for the cost of a computer run. 72 Atty. Gen. 68.
WI.effective_status: Current (annotation carried in certified 2023-24 statutes published 2026-08-05)
WI.notes: Verbatim from the official annotation to § 19.35 in the certified statutes; the opinion body itself was not separately opened. Consequence: the $50 location-fee threshold of § 19.35(3)(c) does not gate computer-run charges, but the § 19.35(3)(a) actual-cost ceiling does. See also § 19.35(1)(L) (no duty to create new records) bounding when such work is owed.

WI.atomic_rule: A custodian may not require a requester to pay the cost of a certification the requester did not ask for; and unless a copy fee is established by law, the custodian may not charge more than the actual and direct cost of reproduction.
WI.trigger: Custodian certifies a copy the requester did not request certified
WI.source_language: A custodian may not require a requester to pay the cost of an unrequested certification. Unless the fee for copies of records is established by law, a custodian may not charge more than the actual and direct cost of reproduction. 72 Atty. Gen. 36.
WI.effective_status: Current (annotation carried in certified 2023-24 statutes published 2026-08-05)
WI.notes: Verbatim from the official annotation to § 19.35 in the certified statutes; opinion body not separately opened. The records law sets no certification rate; record-specific statutes may (via the § 19.35(3)(a) 'otherwise established by law' clause).

WI.legal_concept: No indigency fee exemption as of right
WI.atomic_rule: The public records law confers no exemption as of right on indigent requesters from payment of fees under § 19.35(3); any fee relief for indigents is only through the discretionary public-interest waiver.
WI.source_language: The public records law confers no exemption as of right on indigents from payment of fees under sub. (3). George v. Record Custodian, 169 Wis. 2d 573, 485 N.W.2d 460 (Ct. App. 1992).
WI.source_authority: George v. Record Custodian, 169 Wis. 2d 573, 485 N.W.2d 460 (Ct. App. 1992)
WI.effective_status: Current (annotation carried in certified 2023-24 statutes published 2026-08-05)
WI.notes: Verbatim from the official annotation to § 19.35 in the certified statutes. Secondary rule type: Discretion (relief remains available under § 19.35(3)(e) at the authority's option). Previously carried only as a note on WI-0039; promoted to a row because it is operative for the waiver item (no mandatory indigency ground).
